children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>
<s>Gautama Gṛhyasūtra</s>.
Together with <s>Maskarī's</s> commentary.
Having bowed with devotion to the primordial god (<s>Ādi-deva</s>), <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
under the pretext of [commenting on] <s>Gautama</s>'s [work], this compendium of all <s>smṛti</s> (law codes)

children.text: kriyate 'dya mayā bhāṣyaṃ sūnunā vāmanasya tu //
children.translated_text: is now composed by me, the son of <s>Vāmana</s>, as a commentary.

children.text: ko vābhisambandhaḥ ? ayamucyate-santi caturdaśa vidyāsthānāni, tadyathā-
children.translated_text: What is the connection (<s>abhisambandha</s>)? This is stated: there are fourteen branches of knowledge (<s>vidyāsthānas</s>), namely—
The [six] auxiliary sciences (<s>Aṅgas</s>), the four <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>, the extensive <s>Nyāya</s>,
<s>Purāṇa</s>, and <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> — these indeed are the fourteen sciences.
Thus.

children.text:
teṣāṃ madhye parigaṇitamidaṃ dharmaśāstramārabhyata ityabhisambandhaḥ /
athavā-puruṣasya sukhaduḥkhopabhogārthaiḥ śarīrendriyaviṣayaiḥ saṃyogaviyogarūpo janmajarāmaraṇaprabandhaḥ saṃsāraḥ /
sa ca dharmādharmanimitto nānyanimittaḥ /
tayośca dharmādharmayoriṣṭāniṣṭopabhogahetutvādupādānaparivarjanārhai tau bhavataḥ /
tadubhayamaparijñāne na sambhavatīti dharmādharmasvarūpāvabodhanārthaṃ gautamena śāstraṃ praṇītamiti /
prayojanamapi cāsyaitadeva, dharmādharmopādānaparivarjanayoḥ puruṣārthatvāditi /
abhidheyamaṣṭakādīni, yathā śrautānyagniṣṭomādīnyavaśyakartavyāni tathāṣṭakādīnmapīti /
tatra sarvakāryāṇāṃ kāraṇataḥ pravṛttidarśanātpūrvaṃ kāraṇaviśeṣapratipādanārthamāha-
children.translated_text: Among these, what is being commenced is this <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>, which is enumerated [among them] — this is the connection. Alternatively: the cycle of birth, old age, and death (<s>saṃsāra</s>), consisting in conjunction and disjunction with the body, senses, and objects that serve the purpose of experiencing pleasure and pain for a person — that is caused by <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), and by no other cause. And since those two — <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — are the causes of experiencing what is desired and undesired, they deserve to be cultivated and avoided [respectively]. Since that distinction between the two is impossible without proper knowledge, this <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) was composed by <s>Gautama</s> for the purpose of understanding the true nature of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. And the purpose of this [work] is exactly that — since the cultivation and avoidance of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> [respectively] is the aim of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). The subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>) is the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> rites and the like — just as the <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) rites such as the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> must necessarily be performed, so too must the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> rites and the like. Therein, since the operation of all effects is observed to proceed from causes, he states [the following] first, for the purpose of establishing the specific cause:
The <s>Veda</s> is the root of <s>dharma</s>. // <s>Gaut</s>. 1.1 //

children.text: nanu vidhipratiṣedharūpatvācchāstrasya 'upanayanaṃ brāhmaṇasyāṣṭame'; ityādyeva vaktavyam, na tvanuvādarūpatvādvedo dharmamūlamityādi, niṣprayojanatvādanuvādasyeti /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Since the <s>śāstra</s> has the nature of injunctions and prohibitions, one should state directly things like 'The <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [should be performed] in the eighth [year]' and so forth. But [a statement like] 'The <s>Veda</s> is the root of <s>dharma</s>' — having the nature of a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) — should not [be stated], since a restatement has no purpose.

children.text: na cānena vedasya prāmāṇyaṃ pratipādyate, tasya svata eva siddheḥ anyathā yena prāmāṇyaṃ pratipādyate tasyāpyanyena prāmāṇyaṃ tasyāpyanyenetyanavasthā syāditi //
children.translated_text: Nor does this [sūtra] establish the authoritativeness (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) of the <s>Veda</s>, since that is established by itself. Otherwise, that by which its authoritativeness is established — its authoritativeness too would need to be established by another, and that by yet another — [leading to] an infinite regress.

children.text:
ucyate-vedasya dharmamūlatvānuvādaḥ taddvāreṇa smṛtiśīlayorapi dharmamūlatvapratipādanārthaḥ /
kathamiti
children.translated_text: It is replied: The restatement that the <s>Veda</s> is the root of <s>dharma</s> is for the purpose of establishing, through that [statement], that <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) and <s>śīla</s> (conduct) are also roots of <s>dharma</s>. If asked 'how?'—

children.text: ceducyate-vedavacanāduccaritāttatpadārthavidāṃ viśiṣṭer'the yā pratipattirniḥsaṃdigdhā jāyate na ca kālāntare deśāntare puruṣāntare 'vasthāntare vā viparyeti sā dharmamūlamiti /
yacca niḥsaṃdigdhamaviparītaṃ ca jñānamutpadyate tasya prāmāṇyamadhyavasituṃ śakyate /
children.translated_text: And that knowledge which arises as free from doubt and non-erroneous — its authoritativeness can be ascertained.

children.text: na ca vedajanitapratyayasya kāraṇadoṣakṛtaṃ mithyātvaṃ, karturanabhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: Nor is the cognition generated by the <s>Veda</s> rendered false by a defect in its cause, since no author is admitted [for the <s>Veda</s>].

children.text: kartṛgato hi doṣaḥ śabdajanitasya pratyayasya mithyātvamāpādayati /
children.translated_text: For it is a defect in the author that renders the cognition generated by words false.
Thus, the restatement is for the purpose of [establishing] what follows.

it is stated: That understanding which arises from Vedic statement, which is free from doubt regarding the specific meaning for those who know the meaning of its words, and which does not become falsified in another time, place, person, or circumstance — that is the root of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text:
idānīṃ sūtraṃ vibrīyate-tatra vedo mantrabrāhmaṇākhyo grantharāśiḥ /
vida jñāne, jñāyate 'nena dharmādisvarūpamiti vedaḥ /
yadyapi smṛtyāderetattulyatvam /
tathāpi parivrājakādivadrūḍhatvādadoṣaḥ /
tathā ca smṛtyantaraṃ-
children.translated_text: Now the <s>sūtra</s> is explained: Here, the <s>Veda</s> is the body of texts known as <s>Mantra</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. [The word <s>Veda</s> is derived from] the root 'vid' meaning 'to know' — that by which the true nature of <s>dharma</s> and the like is known is the <s>Veda</s>. Although this [defining characteristic] applies equally to <s>smṛti</s> and the like, there is no fault since [the word <s>Veda</s>] is conventionally fixed [to denote only revealed scripture] — like [the word] <s>parivrājaka</s> (wandering ascetic) [which conventionally denotes a specific class]. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> states—

children.text: śrutiśtu vedo vijñeyo dharmaśāstraṃ tu vai smṛtiḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>Śruti</s> (revelation) is to be understood as the <s>Veda</s>; <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> (law-text) is indeed <s>smṛti</s> (tradition).'
Thus.

children.text:
sa ca ṛgvedādibhedena bhidyate /
jātyapekṣayaikavacanam /
dharmaḥ karma ācāra ityarthaḥ, apūrvākhyo vā /
mūlaṃ kāraṇaṃ jñāpakaṃ, pramāṇamityarthaḥ /
tatra vidhipratiṣedhātmako hi vedo dharmādyavabodhakatvaṃ pratipadyate, na tu mantrārthavādarūpa iti ceducyate- arthavādāderapi vidhyekavākyatvenopakārakatvāt pāraṃparyeṇa dharmamūlatvamaviruddham /
arthavādastāvat stutinindādvāreṇa vidhipratiṣedharūpatvaṃ pratipadyate, mantrastvanuṣṭānakāle vihitārthasmārakatvāt /
tataḥ sarvaprakāra eva vedo
children.translated_text: And that [<s>Veda</s>] is divided according to the distinction of <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the others. The singular number is due to [its being treated as one] generic class (<s>jāti</s>). <s>Dharma</s> means action, conduct — this is the meaning; or it is that which is called <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen transcendent result). <s>Mūla</s> (root) means cause, indicator — that is, 'means of valid knowledge' (<s>pramāṇa</s>) is the meaning. If it be objected that, since the <s>Veda</s> has the form of injunctions and prohibitions, it attains the capacity to make known <s>dharma</s> and the like [only] in its injunctive and prohibitive portions, but not in its <s>mantra</s> and <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) portions — it is replied: Since the <s>arthavāda</s> and the like also serve as auxiliaries by forming a single sentence with the injunction, their being a root of <s>dharma</s> indirectly is not contradictory. The <s>arthavāda</s> at least attains the form of injunction and prohibition through the medium of praise and blame. And the <s>mantra</s>, because it reminds one at the time of performance of the meaning that has been enjoined. Therefore, the <s>Veda</s> in every aspect is

children.text:
dharmamūlamiti /
kecinmantrārthavādamūlameva pratijānate yatā 'dhanvanniva prapā asi'; ityatra prapā kartavyetyādi /
anye tvāhuḥ-adhyayanamātrādeva dharmasiddhiḥ, yathā'ha-
children.translated_text: the root of <s>dharma</s>. Some maintain that <s>mantra</s> and <s>arthavāda</s> alone are the root — as in [the passage] 'Like a watering-place in a desert,' where [the injunction] 'A watering-place should be made' [is derived] and so forth. Others say: <s>Dharma</s> is accomplished by mere recitation (<s>adhyayana</s>) alone, as it is said—

children.text: ā haiva sa nakhāgrebhyaḥ paramaṃ tapyate tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: From the very tips of his nails, he performs the supreme austerity (<s>tapas</s>),
the twice-born one who, even wearing a garland, daily recites his own <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic study) according to his ability.
Thus.

children.text:
ataḥ pāṭha eva dharmamūlamiti /
tadayuktaṃ, karmaphalaśruteḥ ānarthakyaprasaṅgāt, mīmāṃsakairadhyayanaphalasya nistatvācca /
athavā vedavācyā kriyā vedaśabdenocyate, sa dharmasya mūlamiti /
śyenādiṣu na bhavatīti cet, ucyate-tatrāpi vairivadhāt prāṇadhanaputradārādirakṣaṇadvāreṇa dharmo 'styeveti /
tataścāvagamyate-yadidaṃ putrapaśugrāmādi dṛṣṭaṃ, yacca
children.translated_text: Therefore, mere recitation is the root of <s>dharma</s>. That is not correct, because it would lead to the purposelessness of scriptural statements about the fruits of rituals, and because the fruit of recitation has been determined by the <s>Mīmāṃsakas</s>. Alternatively: the ritual action expressed by the <s>Veda</s> is denoted by the word '<s>Veda</s>' — that is the root of <s>dharma</s>. [Objection:] In [rites like] the <s>Śyena</s> (hawk-sacrifice, aimed at killing an enemy) and the like, this does not hold. [Reply:] It is said — even there, <s>dharma</s> exists through the protection of one's life, wealth, sons, wife, and the like by [the destruction of] an enemy. And from this it is understood: whatever is seen — sons, cattle, village, and the like — and whatever is
unseen such as [good] creation (<s>sarga</s>) and the like — all of that has <s>dharma</s> as its cause.

children.text: dharmaḥ pañcaprakāraḥ-varṇadharma āśramadharmo guṇadharmo varṇāśramadharmo nimittadharma iti /
varṇadharmo 'dhyayanādiḥ, āśramadharmaḥ samidādhānādiḥ guṇadharmo 'bhiṣekādiguṇayuktasya rakṣaṇādiḥ, varṇāśramadharmo brāhmaṇasya pālāśo daṇḍa ityādiḥ, nimittadharmaḥ prāyaścittādiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Varṇa-dharma</s> is Vedic study (<s>adhyayana</s>) and the like. <s>Āśrama-dharma</s> is offering fuel-sticks (<s>samidādhāna</s>) and the like. <s>Guṇa-dharma</s> is the protection and the like incumbent upon one endowed with [special] qualities such as royal consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>). <s>Varṇāśrama-dharma</s> is [the rule that] 'a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s staff should be of <s>palāśa</s> [wood]' and the like. <s>Nimitta-dharma</s> is expiations (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) and the like.
<s>Mūla</s> (root) means cause.
And thus it is said: 'From the <s>Veda</s>, <s>dharma</s> has shone forth.'

children.text: sūtrārambhaprayojanaṃ ca-yathaiva vedo dharmamūlaṃ tathā smṛtiśīle apīti //
children.translated_text: And the purpose of commencing this <s>sūtra</s> [work] is: just as the <s>Veda</s> is the root of <s>dharma</s>, so too are <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) and <s>śīla</s> (conduct).

<s>Dharma</s> is of five kinds: <s>varṇa-dharma</s> (duty of one's social class), <s>āśrama-dharma</s> (duty of one's life-stage), <s>guṇa-dharma</s> (duty arising from [special] qualities), <s>varṇāśrama-dharma</s> (combined class-and-stage duty), and <s>nimitta-dharma</s> (duty arising from a specific occasion).

children.text: na kevalaṃ veda eva dharmamūlaṃ, kiṃ tarhi-
children.translated_text: Not only is the <s>Veda</s> alone the root of <s>dharma</s>, but also—
The <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) and <s>śīla</s> (conduct) of those who know it [the <s>Veda</s>] [are also roots of <s>dharma</s>]. // <s>Gaut</s>. 1.2 //

children.text:
vedavidāṃ ca ye smṛtiśīle te api dharmamūle bhavataḥ te api vedāvirodhinī, tadvidāmityārambhāt /
mūlaśabdaśceha dvābhyāmabhisambadhyamāno dvicanānto draṣṭavyaḥ /
tacchabdena ṣaḍaṅgo vedo lakṣyate /
smṛtirupanibanandhanaṃ manu-yama-vasiṣṭha-bhṛgvaṅgiro-bṛhaspatyuśano-bhāradvāja-gautapāpastamba-saṃvarta-vyāsa-śatātapa-
children.translated_text: The <s>smṛti</s> and <s>śīla</s> of those who know the <s>Veda</s> — these too are roots of <s>dharma</s>. They too are not contradictory to the <s>Veda</s>, [as indicated] by the commencement with 'of those who know it' (<s>tadvidām</s>). The word <s>mūla</s> (root) here, being connected with two [nouns], should be understood as taking a dual ending. By the word 'tat' (that), the <s>Veda</s> with its six auxiliary sciences (<s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>) is indicated. <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition) is the textual composition (<s>upanibandhana</s>) made by <s>Manu</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Uśanas</s>, <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Āpastamba</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Śātātapa</s>,

children.text:
śaṅkha-likhita-hārīta-bodhāyana-yājñavalkya-pracetādibhiḥ kṛtam /
śīlamanupanibaddhaḥ samācāraḥ kautukamaṅgalādiḥ bahutvātpratideśaṃ bhidyamānatvāccānupanibaddhaḥ /
cakāro 'nuktasamuccayārthaḥ /
yathā'ha manu--
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Likhita</s>, <s>Hārīta</s>, <s>Bodhāyana</s>, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, <s>Pracetas</s>, and others. <s>Śīla</s> (conduct) is the customary practice (<s>samācāra</s>) that is not textually codified — festive rites (<s>kautuka</s>), auspicious ceremonies (<s>maṅgala</s>), and the like — which, because of being numerous and varying from region to region, is not codified. The particle 'ca' (and) is for the purpose of including what is not [otherwise] mentioned. As <s>Manu</s> says—
The entire <s>Veda</s> is the root of <s>dharma</s>, as well as the <s>smṛti</s> and <s>śīla</s> of those who know it,
and the conduct of the virtuous, and self-satisfaction (<s>ātmatuṣṭi</s>) as well.
Thus.
Walking around [the fire] three times clockwise at the time of the <s>Sandhyā</s> (twilight) observance and the like — this is the practice of the learned (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>).

The conviction that arises in those who know the <s>Veda</s> and are devoted to all [prescribed] observances, due to their being free from [selfish] desire — that is self-satisfaction (<s>ātmatuṣṭi</s>).
He will state [later]: 'Whatever the self-controlled elders [approve]' and so forth.
Some explain: The non-codification of these — festive rites, auspicious ceremonies, and the like — is like the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> rites: there is no sin from non-performance.

children.text: ācārātmatuṣṭī api śīla evāntarbhūte iti na pṛthagupanyaste /
children.translated_text: Conduct (<s>ācāra</s>) and self-satisfaction (<s>ātmatuṣṭi</s>) are also included within <s>śīla</s> (conduct) itself, so they are not mentioned separately.
The particle 'ca' (and) is also only for the purpose of aggregating what has been mentioned.

children.text: idānīṃ pūrvapakṣīkaroti vedavidāṃ śīlaṃ dharmamūlaṃ na bhavati yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Now he presents the prima facie view (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>): The <s>śīla</s> of those who know the <s>Veda</s> cannot be a root of <s>dharma</s>, because—
Transgression of <s>dharma</s> is observed [even among them]. // <s>Gaut</s>. 1.3 //
The remainder is: [therefore their conduct] does not attain the status of being a root of <s>dharma</s>.

For example, <s>Prajāpati</s> desired his own daughter; as [was the case with] <s>Indra</s>'s going to <s>Ahalyā</s>; as [was the case with] <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, and others who did not reside in [any proper] <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life).
Furthermore—
And violent acts (<s>sāhasa</s>) by great persons [are also observed]. // <s>Gaut</s>. 1.4 //

children.text:
atrāpi dharmamūlatvaṃ na prāpnotīti śeṣaḥ caśabdopādānāt /
sahaḥśabdena balamucyate /
yathā ca nāradaḥ-"saho balamihocyate"iti /
tena śāstraṃ lokasaṃvyavahāraṃ cānavekṣya yat kriyate tat sāhasam /

children.translated_text: 'Of great persons' means of those who are renowned in the world.
For example, <s>Rāma</s>'s killing of women such as <s>Tāṭakā</s>.
<s>Jāmadagnya</s>'s (i.e., <s>Paraśurāma</s>'s) cutting off his mother's head; <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s entering the water [to drown himself]; and so forth.
Therefore, it is inappropriate for <s>śīla</s> (conduct) to be a root of <s>dharma</s>.

Here too, the remainder is: [their conduct] does not attain the status of being a root of <s>dharma</s> — because of the inclusion of the particle 'ca' (and). By the word 'sahas,' force (<s>bala</s>) is meant. As <s>Nārada</s> [says]: 'Sahas means force here.' By that, whatever is done disregarding the <s>śāstra</s> (scripture) and worldly convention — that is <s>sāhasa</s> (violent act).

children.text: kathaṃ punardharmavyatikramasāhasayoḥ bhedaḥ-viṣayābhilāṣeṇa yadayuktamācaryate, sa dharmavyatikramaḥ, krodhādyabhibhavena yat kriyate tat sāhasam //
children.translated_text: But how is the distinction between 'transgression of <s>dharma</s>' (<s>dharmavyatikrama</s>) and 'violent act' (<s>sāhasa</s>)? What is improperly done out of desire for sense objects — that is transgression of <s>dharma</s>. What is done under the overwhelming influence of anger and the like — that is a violent act.
To this he replies—
But not where a [worldly] purpose is apparent — because of the weakness of the inferior. // <s>Gaut</s>. 1.5 //

children.text:
tuśabda- pakṣanivṛttyarthaḥ /
dṛṣṭārtho dṛṣṭaprayojanaḥ tasmin dṛṣṭaprayojane śīlaṃ dharmamūlaṃ na bhavati /
tathā ca
children.translated_text: The particle 'tu' is for the purpose of negating the [prima facie] position. 'Where a purpose is apparent' (<s>dṛṣṭārtha</s>) means where a visible purpose is perceived; in that case — where a visible purpose is perceived — <s>śīla</s> (conduct) is not a root of <s>dharma</s>. And thus

children.text:
vasiṣṭhaḥ-"agṛhyamāṇakāraṇo dharmaḥ"iti /
naitādvivacanaṃ, dṛṣṭārthe dharmavyatikramasāhase iti /
tasmin gṛhyamāṇe"īdudet"ityādinā pragṛhyasaṃjñāyāṃ satyāṃ"dṛṣṭārthe avaradaurbalyāt"iti pāṭhaḥ prāpnoti /
avaradaurbalyāt na varaḥ avaro nikṛṣṭaḥ dveṣādyabhibhūtaḥ aparamārthajñāna ityarthaḥ tasya daurbalyāt dharmādharmaparijñānāśakterityarthaḥ /
etaccānena jñāpitaṃ bhavati- mahatāmapi tadvidāṃ kadā cidabhibhavo 'stīti, śarīravata- priyāpriyayoravaśyaṃbhāvitvāt /
children.translated_text: And this is indicated by him: even among the great ones who know it, there is sometimes an overpowering [by passion] — since for one who has a body, both the pleasant and unpleasant inevitably [occur].

children.text: tasmādyāvadeteṣāṃ rāgādidoṣeṇābhibhavaḥ, tāvatteṣāṃ ācāro 'pi na grāhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, to the extent that these are overpowered by the defect of passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the like, to that extent their conduct too should not be followed.
And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> [says]: 'A learned person (<s>śiṣṭa</s>), however, [is authoritative only when he is] free from selfish desire.'

children.text: athavā-avaraśabdenedānīṃtanāḥ kaliyugapuruṣā ucyante, teṣāṃ daurbalyāt asārmathyāt //
children.translated_text: Alternatively: by the word 'avara' (inferior), people of the present <s>Kali Yuga</s> are meant; [the conduct of those who knew the <s>Veda</s> is not to be a root of <s>dharma</s>] because of their weakness, i.e., incapacity.

<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> [says]: '<s>Dharma</s> is [only] that whose cause is not apprehended [i.e., whose reward is invisible].' This [sūtra] is not a <s>dvivacana</s> (dual statement) meaning 'transgression of <s>dharma</s> and violent acts are [excluded only] where a worldly purpose is apparent.' When that [dṛṣṭārtha] is apprehended, since the <s>pragṛhya</s> designation applies with [particles] 'ī', 'dū', and 'e' [as per <s>Pāṇini</s>], the reading 'where a purpose is apparent, because of the weakness of the inferior' is obtained. 'Because of the weakness of the inferior' — 'avara' means inferior, one who is degraded, one overpowered by hatred and the like, one who does not know the ultimate truth — this is the meaning. 'Because of his weakness' means because of [his] incapacity to discern <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: evaṃ smṛtipramāṇamuktvā adhunā ekārthopanipatitānāṃ vākyānāṃ parasparavirodhe sati kiṃ kravyamityāta āha-
children.translated_text: Having thus stated the authority of <s>smṛti</s>, now, [the question arises:] when statements that bear upon a single topic are mutually contradictory, what is to be done? To this he says—
When there is a conflict between [authorities of] equal force, there is an option (<s>vikalpa</s>). // <s>Gaut</s>. 1.6 //

children.text:
tulyapramāṇaprāpitaḥ padārthastulyabalaḥ /
tayoḥ parasparavirodhe sati vikalpo veditavyaḥ, ayaṃ vāyaṃ veti /
nobhayaparityāgaḥ, ubhayoḥ pramāṇaprāpitatvāt /
nānyataraparigrahaḥ, ekasmin gṛhyamāṇe dvitīyasyānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ syāditi /
kimudāharaṇaṃ-śrutau tāvat udite hotavyaṃ, anudite hotavyamityevamādi /
smṛtāvapi,"nityamabhojyaṃ keśakīṭāvapannam"iti gautamaḥ /
children.translated_text: A matter established by equal means of valid knowledge is 'of equal force' (<s>tulyabala</s>). When there is mutual conflict between two such [authorities], an option is to be understood — [one may follow] either this or that. There should not be the abandonment of both, since both are established by valid means of knowledge. Nor should one alone be accepted, since if one were [exclusively] accepted, the purposelessness of the second would follow. What is the example? In <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture): 'One should offer when [the sun] has risen'; 'One should offer when [the sun] has not risen' — and so forth. In <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) as well: <s>Gautama</s> [says] 'What has fallen on hair or insects is permanently unfit to eat.'
What has been eaten by birds, smelled by cows, shaken, or sneezed upon,
or contaminated by hair or insects — is purified by sprinkling earth [on it].
Thus [says] <s>Manu</s>.

children.text:
nanu-cātra sārmathyādeva vikalpaprasiddheḥ anarthakamidaṃ sūtraṃ samuccayastāvadatra na saṃbhatīti /
na hyanudite hutvā punarudite hotuṃ śakyate, guṇabhūtakālavaśena pradhānasya homasyāvṛtteranyāyyatvāt /
pradhānavaśavartino hi guṇāḥ, na guṇavaśavarti pradhānamiti /

children.translated_text: Nor can the [offering that is] not repeated be applied to both times.

children.text: evaṃ smṛtāvapi śuddhiparityāgayonairva samuccayaḥ sambhavatīti, parasparavirodhāditi /
children.translated_text: Likewise in <s>smṛti</s>, there is no possibility of cumulation of purification and rejection — because of mutual contradiction.
And it has been said that abandonment of both is not appropriate.
Therefore, the option alone results here, so this [sūtra] has no purpose.

[Objection:] But here, since the option is already well-established by the force of the [situation] itself, this <s>sūtra</s> is purposeless — for a cumulative application (<s>samuccaya</s>) is not possible here. For one cannot, having offered when [the sun] has not risen, offer again when it has risen — since the repetition of the principal [act], the offering, at the behest of a subordinate [factor], time, is unreasonable. For subordinate [factors] are governed by the principal, not the principal by subordinate [factors].

children.text:
evaṃ tarhi nyāyaprāptānuvādo 'yaṃ viśeṣārthaḥ /
ko viśeṣaḥ ? tulyabalayoreva virodhe vikalpaḥ, atulyabalayostu bādha eveti /
tena śrutismṛtyorvirodhe smṛtireva bādhyate /

children.translated_text: For in <s>śruti</s>, the word [of the <s>Veda</s>] is directly perceived (<s>pratyakṣa</s>); in <s>smṛti</s>, it is inferential (<s>ānumānika</s>).
And inference is not authoritative when it contradicts direct perception.

children.text: evaṃ smṛtyācāravirodhe ca mātuladuhitṛpariṇayanādyācāro bādhyata iti, tatra hyācārāt smṛtyanumānamiti /
children.translated_text: Similarly, when <s>smṛti</s> and [customary] conduct conflict, the conduct — such as marrying one's maternal uncle's daughter — is superseded, for in that case the <s>smṛti</s> is inferred from the conduct.

children.text: virodhe vikalpavacanāt, avirodhe tu tulyapramāṇaśiṣṭānāṃ samuccayaḥ yathā ācamanādīnāṃ śrauteṣu karmasviti //
children.translated_text: Because of the statement of option in [cases of] conflict; but in the absence of conflict, there is cumulation for those [authorities] that are of equal validity and are accepted by the learned — as [is the case with] the <s>ācamana</s> (sipping water for purification) and the like in <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) rites.

[Reply:] In that case, this is a restatement of what is already established by reason, and it serves a special purpose. What is the special purpose? The option applies [only] when the conflicting [authorities are] of equal force; but when they are of unequal force, there is outright supersession (<s>bādha</s>). Therefore, when there is a conflict between <s>śruti</s> (revelation) and <s>smṛti</s> (tradition), the <s>smṛti</s> alone is superseded.

children.text:
nanu ca yadi vedaliṅgaprabhavatvābhyupagama eva smṛteḥ śrutyā sahātulyabalatvamupapādyate, tadā hi mantrārthavādavākyeṣvanyapareṣvapi yāni smārtadharmamabalabhūtāni liṅgāni"kumārā viśikhā iva"ityevamādīni teṣāṃ pratyakṣavedavākyavirodhe sati virodhivākyānumānavirodhāt durbalatvaṃ prasajyate /
yadā tūtsannaśākhāpūrvikā smṛtirabhyupagame-yathā'hāpastambaḥ-"brāhmaṇoktā vidhayasteṣāmutsannāḥ pāṭhāḥ prayogādanumīyante"iti tadobhayośca vaidikatvāt tulyabalataiva prasajyate /
na hyanumitasya vedavākyasya pratyakṣasya ca balābalaviśeṣo 'sti pratyakṣānumānaparicchinnāgnivaditi /
syādetat yatra smṛtivacane vedavirodho 'sti tannaiva vedavākyānumāpakaṃ bhavati, kiṃ tarhi bhrāntyādiprabhavamevaitaditi /
tacca na yuktaṃ, dharmaśāstrapraṇeturanāptatvābhyupagame aviśvāsaprasaṅgāt /
yadāpi vedavadavicchinnapāraṃparyeṇāgatā smṛtirabhyupagamyate tadāpi tulyabalatvamupapadyata iti tatrāpi tannaivopapadyate /
yastāvanmātuladuhitṛpariṇayanādikaḥ samācāra upanyastaḥ sa kāmādyabhibhave sati duṣṭācāratvācchiṣṭācāra eva nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: Now, the custom that has been presented, such as marrying one's maternal uncle's daughter, when desire and the like prevail, being improper conduct, cannot be considered the conduct of the learned (<s>śiṣṭācāra</s>).

children.text: yastvavigānenoktalakṣaṇaiḥ śiṣṭairācaryate tasya vedamūlatvāviśeṣāt smṛtyā saha tulyabalatvameva prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: But that which is practiced by the learned who possess the stated characteristics, without dispute—since there is no difference in its having the <s>Veda</s> as its root, it has equal authority with <s>smṛti</s>.
But for restrictions and their establishment, a different purpose has been taught.

children.text: na ca samācārasya smṛtivākyāntaritarūpsaya vedavākyānumānasaṃnikarṣakṛtaṃ balābalatvaṃ sidhyati //
children.translated_text: And the relative strength or weakness of custom, whose form is mediated by <s>smṛti</s> statements, produced by the inferential connection with Vedic statements, cannot be established.

[Objection:] If it is maintained that the <s>smṛti</s>'s unequal force relative to <s>śruti</s> is established precisely because it is acknowledged to originate from Vedic indicators (<s>liṅga</s>), then indeed — regarding those indicators supporting <s>smārtadharma</s> (traditional law), which are weak [indicators found] in <s>mantra</s>, <s>arthavāda</s>, and other such Vedic passages — like 'boys like crests' and the like — when they conflict with directly perceived Vedic statements, weakness [of the <s>smṛti</s>] would follow, due to the conflict of an inference from a conflicting passage. But when <s>smṛti</s> is accepted as having originated from a lost Vedic branch (<s>utsanna-śākhā</s>) — as <s>Āpastamba</s> says: 'The injunctions stated by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — their [original Vedic] texts are lost; [the rules] are inferred from practice' — then, since both are Vedic in character, [the conclusion of] equal force alone follows. For there is no difference of strength between an inferred Vedic statement and a directly perceived one — just as fire ascertained by perception and by inference [is equally fire]. [Counter-objection:] It might be said: where a <s>smṛti</s> statement conflicts with the <s>Veda</s>, that [<s>smṛti</s> statement] simply is not inferential of a Vedic passage; rather, it is produced merely by error and the like. But that is not correct, because if the non-trustworthiness of the author of the <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> were accepted, distrust [of the entire text] would follow. And even when <s>smṛti</s> is accepted as having come down through an unbroken lineage like the <s>Veda</s> [itself], equal force is established — so in that case too, this [simple supersession] is not established.

children.text:
atrocyate-atulyabalatvaṃ tāvat vedādīnāṃ sūtrārambhasārmathyādevāvagamyate /
yadi hi tulyabalānyetāni syuḥ tadā virodhe vikalpaḥ sārmathyādeva siddhaḥ, kimanena sūtreṇeti tulyabalagrahaṇaṃ cānarthakaṃ syāditi /
asminapi vedādyurbalataratvaṃ smṛterupapadyate /
tatra liṅgaprabhavatvamupapadyate ityuktam /
tenāyameva
children.translated_text: To this we reply: the unequal authority of the <s>Veda</s> and the rest is understood from the very capacity of the commencement of the <s>sūtra</s>. For if these were of equal authority, then in case of conflict, the option would be established by capacity alone—what need then for this <s>sūtra</s>? Thus the thesis of equal authority—
—is reasonable as a position regarding the matter.

children.text: svatantrapakṣo 'bhihitaḥ, sa pakṣaḥ"tadvidāṃ ca smṛtiśīle"ityetasmin sati durupapāda eveti /
children.translated_text: The independent thesis has been stated; that thesis, given '<s>tadvidāṃ ca smṛtiśīle</s>' (and the conduct of those who know it), would be very difficult to sustain.
Therefore, it is established that <s>smṛtis</s> have their origin in Vedic indicators.

children.text: nanu caivamapi nopapadyate, kvacit smṛtyā śruterbādhadarśanāt yathā sāmānyena pravṛtto vaidikakarmādhikāraḥ smṛtyā upanītādipuruṣaviśeṣa evādhikriyate /
children.translated_text: But even so, it is not tenable, since sometimes <s>smṛti</s> is seen to override <s>śruti</s>. For example, the general Vedic entitlement to ritual actions is restricted by <s>smṛti</s> to specific persons such as the initiated (<s>upanīta</s>) and others.

children.text: tathā saṃskāraikadeśenāpyātmaguṇayoge sati viśiṣṭaphalābhidhānāt, tathā gāmālabheteti śruticodito 'pi govadhaḥ smārtapratiṣedhabalīyastvānna kriyate, tathāgnihotrādikaṃ coditajīvanopādhikaṃ karma dravyasādhyamapi na smārtacauryādipratiṣaddhenāpi dravyamārjayitvā tatkriyate /
children.translated_text: Likewise, because even through a partial <s>saṃskāra</s> (ritual consecration), when a personal qualification is present, a distinguished result is declared; likewise, even the killing of a cow, enjoined by the <s>śruti</s> '<s>gām ālabheta</s>' (one should slaughter a cow), is not performed because of the stronger force of the <s>smārta</s> (smṛti-based) prohibition; likewise, the <s>Agnihotra</s> and other rituals, even when enjoined—
Therefore, the statement that <s>smṛti</s> is overridden by <s>śruti</s> is incorrectly made.

children.text:
ucyate-virodhe sata pramāṇānāṃ balābalacintā yujyate /
yatra tu virodhābhāvaḥ tatra durbalopi naiva bādhyata iti /
yastāvadupanītasya karmādhikāraḥ saḥ śrutyā naiva virudhyate, upanayanasya vedagrahaṇārthatvāt, tasya ca karmārthatvāt, na cāpūrvasaṃyogamantareṇa pradhānasiddhiḥ /
yaccoktaṃ govardhestu śruticoditopi na kriyata iti, tadapi na kevalaṃ smṛtyā, kintu mantravarṇācca 'mā gāḥ pramāpayāśvān pramāpaya'; ityādi /
ataḥ smṛtyā śrutirnaiva bādhyate /
kecidutsannaśākhāpūrvikāṃ smṛtimāhuḥ /
tadayuktam /
tatra vicāryate-kiṃ smaraṇātpūrvameva naṣṭāḥ śākhāḥ utottarakālamiti /
children.translated_text: Here it is examined: were the [Vedic] branches lost before the remembering, or afterward?

children.text: yāde pūrvaṃ tatra smaraṇaṃ nopapadyate, vinaṣṭatvāt, pūrvavijñānasadṛśatvāt smṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: If before, then remembering is not possible, since they were destroyed—because <s>smṛti</s> (memory) requires similarity with a prior cognition.

children.text: yadyuttarakālaṃ, tadotsannaśākhāpūrvakatvaṃ vaktuṃ na yujyate, tadānīmupalabhyamānatvāt /
children.translated_text: If afterward, then it is not proper to say that they were preceded by lost branches, since they were being perceived at that time.

children.text: āpastamboktasyāpyayamabhiprāyaḥ-utsannāḥ kvacitkvaciddeśe na sarvatreti 'teṣāmutsannāḥ pāṭhāḥ prayogādanumīyante'; ityatrāpi vyākhyā kartavyā //
children.translated_text: The intention of <s>Āpastamba</s>'s statement is also this: 'lost' means in certain regions, not everywhere. Thus in '<s>teṣām utsannāḥ pāṭhāḥ prayogād anumīyante</s>' (their lost recensions are inferred from practice), this interpretation should also be applied.

We reply: when there is a conflict, consideration of the relative strength of the <s>pramāṇas</s> (authorities) is appropriate. But where there is no conflict, even the weaker [authority] is not overridden. Now, the entitlement of the initiated person to ritual action is not in conflict with <s>śruti</s>—

children.text:
evamiyaṃ dharmapramāṇaparibhāṣoktā /
idānīṃ smṛtyā yatpramīyate tadabhidhānārthamāha-
children.translated_text:
Thus the definition of the <s>pramāṇas</s> (authorities) of <s>dharma</s> has been stated.
Now, to state what is ascertained by <s>smṛti</s>, [the author] says—
"The <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [is to be performed] in the eighth [year]."

children.text:
vedasya agnerācāryasya yamaniyamānāṃ vā samīpe nayanamupanayanam /
tadaṣṭame varṣe, varṣagaṇanāsārmathyāt /
nityo 'yamupanayanakālaḥ, kāmyāpatkalpayorūrdhvamabhidhānāt /
kṣatriyavaiśyayorūrdhvamabhidhānāt śūdrasyaikajātitvādarthasiddhasyāpi brāhmaṇagrahaṇasya jātinimittatvaprasiddhyarthamārambhaḥ /
na ca dvijatvavat brāhmaṇatvaṃ kriyata iti /
children.translated_text: And <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-hood is not created [by the ceremony] in the same way as twice-born status.

children.text: evaṃ ca surāpasya brāhmaṇasya 'surāpasya brāhmaṇasyoṣṇāmāsiṃceyuḥ'; ityevamādayo brāhmaṇoddeśena vidhīyamānā anupanītasyāpi bhavanti /
children.translated_text: Thus, for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has drunk liquor, the injunctions directed at the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, such as '<s>surāpasya brāhmaṇasyoṣṇām āsiñceyuḥ</s>' (they should pour hot [liquor] on a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who drinks liquor), apply even to one who has not been initiated.

children.text: yadvā-brāhmaṇagrahaṇena vinā trayāṇāmapyetannityaṃ syāt, kāmyaṃ tu brāhmaṇasya navame pañcame vā syāt, itarayostvekādaśadvādaśayoḥ syātāṃ, kāmyānantaramabhidhānāt /
children.translated_text: Alternatively: without the word '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>,' this would be obligatory for all three [castes]; but the optional [time] for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> would be in the ninth or fifth [year]; for the other two, in the eleventh and twelfth—since it is stated after the optional [time].

children.text: pūrvasaṃskārabhāve 'pi upanayanenādhikriyate, na tvanena vinoparitanairiti garbhādhānādimanuktvā upanayanasyaivehārambhaḥ //
children.translated_text: Even in the presence of prior <s>saṃskāras</s>, one is entitled [to study] by <s>upanayana</s>, but not without it to those that follow—therefore, without stating the <s>garbhādhāna</s> (conception rite) and the rest, only the <s>upanayana</s> is commenced here.

Leading near (<s>upanayana</s>) means leading to the proximity of the <s>Veda</s>, or of the fire, or of the teacher, or of the restraints and observances. That is in the eighth year, due to the capacity of counting by years. This is the obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) time for <s>upanayana</s>, since the optional (<s>kāmya</s>) and emergency (<s>āpatkalpā</s>) [times] are stated later. For the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s>—
"The optional [time] is in the ninth or fifth [year]."

children.text:
kāmāya hitaṃ kāmyaṃ tadupatpādanasamartham /
pañcame navama iti vācye kramabhedaḥ anayorantarā kṣatriyavaiśyayoḥ kāmyakālaparigrahārthaḥ /
tathā ca manuḥ-
children.translated_text:
What is conducive to one's desire is <s>kāmya</s> (optional)—that which is capable of producing it. Where one should say 'fifth, ninth,' the difference in order is for the purpose of including the optional times for the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s> between them.
Thus <s>Manu</s> [states]:
"For a king desiring strength, in the sixth; for a <s>Vaiśya</s> desiring wealth, in the eighth."
The irregular compound is for the purpose of indicating different types of optional [times].

children.text: tathācaca smṛtyantaraṃ-'navame tvāyuṣmākaṃ pañcame brahmavarcasakāmam'; iti /
children.translated_text: And likewise another <s>smṛti</s>: 'In the ninth for longevity, in the fifth for one desiring sacred luster.'
The word '<s>vā</s>' (or) indicates an option.
That should be understood as depending on desire.
"The counting of years begins from the embryo (<s>garbha</s>)."
The ten months coexisting with the embryo are called '<s>garbha</s>' (embryo).

children.text: tatprabhṛti varṣagaṇanā kartavyā, na tu janmata ārabhya /
children.translated_text: From that [point] the counting of years is to be made, not from birth onward.
And therefore, in statements like '<s>upanayana</s> of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,' one should construe 'in the eighth from the embryo,' and so forth.
"That [<s>upanayana</s>] is the second birth."
That <s>upanayana</s> is the second birth.
The meaning is: one consecrated by it becomes a <s>dvija</s> (twice-born).
In [rules like] 'study for the twice-born,' and so forth, the designation '<s>dvija</s>' is made for practical purposes.
The use of that [term] is for including both the obligatory and optional <s>upanayana</s>.
"He on account of whom that [second birth occurs] is the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher)."
The use of that [term] is for including both the obligatory and optional <s>upanayana</s>.
In [passages like] 'the <s>ācārya</s> is the foremost of <s>gurus</s>,' and so forth, the designation is made for practical purposes.
"And because of the recitation of the <s>Veda</s>."

children.text:
vedānuvacanaṃ samastavedānucanam /
adṛṣṭārthamekadeśādhyāpanena guruḥ /
tathā ca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: Recitation of the <s>Veda</s> means the recitation of the entire <s>Veda</s>. One who teaches even a part [of the <s>Veda</s>] for an unseen [spiritual] purpose is a <s>guru</s>. Thus <s>Manu</s> [says]:

children.text: alpaṃ vā bahu vā yasya śrutasyopakaroti yaḥ /
children.translated_text: "He who benefits [a student] even in a small or large part of what has been learned—"
"He too should be known here as a <s>guru</s>, through that benefit of learning."

children.text:
dṛṣṭārthaṃ cedupādhyāyaḥ /
tathāca vasiṣṭhaḥ-'yastvekadeśaṃ sa upādhyāyaḥ'; iti /
cakārāt aṅgavyākhyātāpi /
tathāca yāskaḥ-'ācārya ācārānācinoti, arthānācinoti, buddhiṃ vā'; iti /
keciccakāraṃ pūrvasūtreṇa samuccayārthaṃ vyācakṣate /
tenobhayakaraṇādevācāryaḥ /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text:
For a visible [practical] purpose, he is an <s>upādhyāya</s> (sub-teacher).
Thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> [says]: 'He who [teaches] a portion is the <s>upādhyāya</s>.' The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) [includes] the expounder of the auxiliary [sciences]. Thus <s>Yāska</s> [says]: 'The <s>ācārya</s> imparts conduct, imparts meaning, or imparts understanding.'
"But one who, having initiated a disciple, teaches him the <s>Veda</s>—"
"—together with the <s>kalpa</s> and the esoteric [teachings]—him they call the <s>ācārya</s>."
"[The obligatory time for <s>upanayana</s>] of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s> is in the eleventh and twelfth [years]."
This is the obligatory time, since the optional and emergency [times] are stated later.

children.text: yadā tu nityakāmyayoḥ kenaciddurbhikṣādinā nimittenātikramaḥ syāt tadānīmāpatkalpamāha-
children.translated_text: But when, due to some cause such as famine, the obligatory and optional [times] are exceeded, then [the author] states the emergency rule—
"Up to the sixteenth [year], the <s>Sāvitrī</s> has not lapsed for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>."

children.text: āṅtrābhividhyarthaḥ, sahaṣoḍasena varṣeṇeti, 'dvyadhikāyāḥ'; iti liṅgāt 'ṣoḍaśe sarvakāmam'; iti smṛtyantaradarśanācca /

children.translated_text: '<s>Apatitā</s>' means 'not lapsed.'
By the word '<s>Sāvitrī</s>' is meant its means, the <s>upanayana</s>—the meaning is that one is entitled to <s>upanayana</s>.
And thus, even when the father and others have not performed the initiation, one is entitled to <s>upanayana</s> through expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>).
Thus <s>Āpastamba</s> [says]: 'He whose father... grandfather... great-grandfather...' and so forth.

The word '<s>ā</s>' has the meaning of inclusion—together with the sixteenth year. This is indicated by the word '<s>dvyadhikā</s>' (two more) and by the statement in another <s>smṛti</s>: 'in the sixteenth for all purposes.'
"For the <s>Rājanya</s> (Kṣatriya), up to the twenty-second [year]."
Here too, '<s>ā</s>' continues [from the previous rule], together with the year.
The use of the word '<s>rājanya</s>' is for establishing his royalty—for only one who is initiated has the right to kingship.
"For the <s>Vaiśya</s>, two more [i.e., the twenty-fourth year]."

children.text: dvābhyāmadhikābhyāṃ sahitā yā dvāviṃśatiḥ sā dvyadhikāḥ, caturviṃśāterityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Twenty-two conjoined with two more—'<s>dvyadhikā</s>' means twenty-four; this is the meaning.
Where one should have said 'twenty-four,' the [indirect] expression is for the purpose of indicating that '<s>ā</s>' [in the earlier rule] has the meaning of inclusion.

The time for <s>upanayana</s> has been stated.
Now, with the desire to state its means, [the author] says—
"Girdles of <s>muñja</s> grass, bowstring, and thread [are worn] in order."

children.text:
muñjavikārā mauñjī /
mūrvā prasiddhā, tadvikārā maurvī /
jyācāsau maurvī ceti samānādhikaraṇasamāsaḥ /
tataśca dhanuṣo 'panīya grāhyā /
sūtraṃ śaṇasūtram /
ekaguṇā maurvī, itare trivṛtau /
yathā'ha manuḥ-
children.translated_text: Made from <s>muñja</s> grass is '<s>mauñjī</s>.' <s>Mūrvā</s> is well known; made from it is '<s>maurvī</s>.' '<s>Jyā</s>' (bowstring) and '<s>maurvī</s>' being in apposition—thus it is to be taken from a bow. <s>Sūtra</s> (thread) means hemp thread. The bowstring is single-stranded; the others are triple-stranded—

children.text: mauñjī trivṛt samā ślakṣṇā kāryā viprasya mekhalā /
children.translated_text: "The girdle of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be made of <s>muñja</s>, triple, even, and smooth;"

children.text: kṣatriyasya tu maurvī jyā vaiśyasya śaṇatāntavī //
children.translated_text: "For a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, a bowstring; for a <s>Vaiśya</s>, of hemp thread."

children.text:
jyāmaurvyordvitvavyāvṛttyarthaṃ kramagrahaṇam /
kecidabhāve vaikalpikārthamiti varṇayanti /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: The mention of 'in order' is to exclude the duality [of options] for bowstring and <s>mūrvā</s>. Some explain it as indicating an option in [their] absence. Thus <s>Manu</s> [says]:
"In the absence of <s>muñja</s>, [the girdle] should be made of <s>kuśa</s>, <s>aśmantaka</s>, or <s>balbaja</s> [grasses],"
"Triple, with one knot, or with three or five."
Since it is established by reasoning, the mention of 'in order' serves a different purpose.
"Skins of a black antelope, a <s>ruru</s> deer, and a goat [are worn]."
The word '<s>ajina</s>' (skin) is construed with each [separately].

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ kṛṣṇamṛgaḥ, ruruḥ pṛṣanmṛgaḥ, bastaḥ prasiddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>kṛṣṇa</s> is the black antelope; the <s>ruru</s> is the spotted deer; the goat (<s>basta</s>) is well known.
These are the upper garments in order [for <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and <s>Vaiśya</s>].
Thus another <s>smṛti</s> [says]: 'They should wear the skin alone as the upper garment.'
"The garments for all are: hemp, linen, bark-cloth, and <s>kutapa</s> (mountain-goat wool)."
<s>Cīra</s> (bark-cloth) is made from <s>darbha</s> grass and the like.
<s>Kutapa</s> is made from the hair of mountain goats.
These are the lower garments.

children.text: viṣamasaṅkhyatvādeva sarveṣāṃ siddheḥ smṛtyantare 'śāṇaṃ kṣaumaṃ vāso brāhmaṇasya'; iti tadāśritya yadyathāsaṅkhyaṃ tannivṛttyarthaṃ sarveṣāṃ grahaṇaṃ, adhikārārthaṃ vā //
children.translated_text: Since the odd number [of items] by itself establishes [applicability] to all, and since another <s>smṛti</s> says 'hemp and linen garments for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'—relying on that, the mention of 'for all' is to prevent the respective correlation, or for the purpose of [specifying] entitlement.
Made of hemp (<s>śaṇa</s>) is <s>śāṇa</s>. <s>Kṣumā</s> is flax; made from it is <s>kṣauma</s> (linen).
"And cotton, undyed."
'For all' continues from the previous [rule], as does 'garment.'
'Undyed' means without connection with dye.
The meaning is: naturally white only.
The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) is for indicating that the previous [garments] are also undyed.
"Some [allow] even saffron-dyed [garments]."
Some desire [garments] connected with dye as well.
The word '<s>api</s>' (even) has the sense of censure.
Therefore, it should be understood [as allowed only] in the absence of the former [garments].
Now, for the purpose of restriction regarding the saffron-dyed option, [the author] says—
"Of tree-[dye] for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>."
Made with the dye of the <s>vṛṣa</s> (a type of tree) is '<s>vārkṣa</s>' (arboreal)—that alone is the garment of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
"Madder-dyed and turmeric-dyed for the other two."
Dyed with <s>mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder) for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
Dyed with <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric) for the <s>Vaiśya</s>.
"The staffs of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> are of <s>bilva</s> and <s>palāśa</s>."
The staff of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is of <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) or <s>palāśa</s> (<s>Butea monosperma</s>).

children.text: yadyapi dvandvanirdeśaiḥ, tathāpi 'yajñiyo vā sarveṣām'; ityekavacananirdeśāt, 'pratigṛhyepsitaṃ daṇḍam'; iti smṛtyantaradarśanācca ekasyaiva dhāraṇaṃ yuktam //
children.translated_text: Although stated as a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound), since there is a singular statement 'of any sacrificial [tree] for all,' and since another <s>smṛti</s> says 'having received the desired staff,' it is proper for one alone to be carried.
"Of <s>aśvattha</s> and <s>pīlu</s> for the remaining [two castes]."

children.text: aśvatthaḥ prasiddhaḥ, pīluḥ kalkiḥ, śeṣe kṣatriyavaiśyaviṣaye /
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) is well known; <s>pīlu</s> is the <s>kalki</s> tree. 'The remaining' refers to the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s>.
Among them, the <s>aśvattha</s> is for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and the <s>pīlu</s> is for the <s>Vaiśya</s>.
"Or of any sacrificial [tree] for all."

children.text: yajñārhe vā syāt vibhītakabilvakayāvakādirvarjito vṛkṣaviśeṣa ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: It should be of a tree-species fit for sacrifice—meaning one excluding <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>bilva</s>ka, barley-trees, and the like.
The word '<s>vā</s>' (or) indicates an option in [their] absence; therefore, [only] in the absence of the former [specified woods].
Otherwise, the word '<s>vā</s>' would be purposeless.
The word 'for all' [is used] lest it apply only to the immediately preceding [two castes].
Now [the author] states the qualities of the staff—
"Undamaged, curved at the top like a sacrificial post, with bark."

children.text:
apīḍitā vallīveṣṭanakīṭāgnyādibhiranupahatā ityarthaḥ /
yūpavakrāḥ yūpavannatāgrā ityarthaḥ /
saśalkāḥ satvacaḥ /
asamāsāt sarva evaṃrūpāḥ, na tu yathāsaṅkhyam /
tathā cāha manuḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Undamaged' means unhurt by creeper-wrapping, insects, fire, and the like. 'Curved at the top like a sacrificial post' means with the top bent like a <s>yūpa</s> (sacrificial post). 'With bark' means with the bark [intact]. Since there is no compound, all [staffs] are of this form—not in respective correlation. Thus <s>Manu</s> says:
"They should all be straight, without blemish, pleasing to look at,"
"Not causing alarm to people, with bark, and undamaged by fire."
"[The staffs should be] of the measure [reaching to] the crown, the forehead, and the tip of the nose."

children.text:
pramāṇaśabdaḥ pratyekaṃ sambadhyate /
mūrdhapramāṇā brahmaṇasya, lalāṭapramāṇāḥ kṣatriyasya, nāsāgrapramāṇā
children.translated_text: The word 'measure' is construed with each separately. Of the measure reaching the crown for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; of the measure reaching the forehead for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>; of the measure reaching the tip of the nose—
—for the <s>Vaiśya</s>. Thus <s>Manu</s> [says]:
"The staff of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should be made reaching to the hair-line in measure;"
"That of a king should be level with the forehead; that of a <s>Vaiśya</s> should reach the tip of the nose."
Now [the author] states the appearance of the <s>brahmacārin</s> (student)—
"Shaven, matted-haired, or with a topknot-lock."

children.text:
muṇḍo muṇḍitaśiraskaḥ /
jaṭilaḥ sakeśaḥ /
śikhā eva jaṭā yasya sa śikhājaṭaḥ /
evaṃ muṇḍaśabdena samastamuṇḍanamucyate /
cakāro vār'thaḥ pratyekamabhisambadhyate-muṇḍo vā jaṭilo vā śikhājaṭo veti /
brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyābhiprāyaṃ bahuvacanam /
yathākramanivṛttyarthaṃ veti noktam /
tathā ca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: '<s>Muṇḍa</s>' means with a shaven head. '<s>Jaṭila</s>' means with [unshorn] hair. One whose topknot (<s>śikhā</s>) alone is matted is a '<s>śikhājaṭa</s>.' Thus by the word '<s>muṇḍa</s>' complete shaving is meant. The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) has the meaning of option, construed with each separately: either shaven, or matted-haired—

children.text: muṇḍo vā jaṭilo vā syādasya vā syācchikhājaṭaḥ //
children.translated_text: One may be shaven-headed, or wear matted locks, or have a topknot of matted hair.
Thus.
Now, since eligibility for Vedic study depends on purity, the purification of objects is stated first for the purpose of purity—
One who is holding an object and becomes <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> (ritually impure from food remnants) should set it down and perform <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping of water). // Gaut. 1.30 //

children.text:
brāhmaṇabhojanādau pravṛtto dravyahastaḥ pūrvamanucchiṣṭaḥ kenacitkāraṇenocchiṣṭasparśādaprayato bhavati, tadā taddravyaṃ bhūmau nidhāya sthāpayitvā'cāmet /
tathā ca vasiṣṭhaḥ-
children.translated_text:
One who is engaged in feeding <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the like, holding an object, previously not <s>ucchiṣṭa</s>, becomes impure due to some reason such as touching something <s>ucchiṣṭa</s>; then he should place that object on the ground, set it down, and perform <s>ācamana</s>.
And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> states—
If, while engaged in distributing food, one should touch something <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> (ritually impure),
One should place that object on the ground, perform <s>ācamana</s>, and then resume the distribution.
Thus.

children.text:
puruṣaśaucavivakṣāyāṃ dravyahastagrahaṇamanarthakam /
ato dravyasya nidhānamātrādeva śuddhiḥ, puruṣasyācamanāt /
yattu dravyasya smṛtyantare prokṣaṇamukta-'bhūmau nikṣipya prokṣaṇāddravyaṃ śuddhyati'; iti tadabhyavahāryapakvadravyaviṣayameva draṣṭavyam /
kathaṃ punastulyasaṃhite sūtre viśeṣo 'vagamyate-nidhāyācacamanaṃ na punaranidhāyeti /
ucyate-yadyanidhāyācamanamiṣṭaṃ syāttato 'dravyahasta ucchiṣṭa ācāmet'; ityetāvadeva vaktavyaṃ syāt, kiṃ nidhānena kriyata iti, tataḥ sūtrātirekānnidhānapakṣa evābhīṣṭa ityavagamyate /
yattu manunoktaṃ-
children.translated_text: When the intention is to discuss the purification of the person, the mention of 'holding an object' would be purposeless. Therefore, the purification of the object comes merely from setting it down, and the purification of the person comes from <s>ācamana</s>. As for the sprinkling mentioned in another <s>smṛti</s> for the object—'the object is purified by placing it on the ground and sprinkling'—that should be understood as applying only to cooked food items. But how can a distinction be understood in the <s>sūtra</s> where the wording is equally balanced—that one should perform <s>ācamana</s> after setting down, not without setting down? It is answered: if <s>ācamana</s> without setting down were intended, then the statement would simply be 'one who is holding an object and becomes <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> should perform <s>ācamana</s>'—what purpose would the setting down serve? Therefore, from the additional wording of the <s>sūtra</s>, it is understood that setting down is indeed the intended course. But what <s>Manu</s> has stated—
One who is holding an object and is touched by something <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> in any manner,
Even without setting down that object, attains purity by performing <s>ācamana</s>.
Thus.

children.text:
tadanabhyavahāryadravyaviṣayaṃ draṣṭavyam /
evaṃcābhyavahāryadravyasyāpakvasya kadalīphalādeḥ nidhānamātrādeva śuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: That should be understood as applying to non-edible objects. And thus, for edible objects that are uncooked, such as banana fruits, purification comes merely from setting them down.
For cooked items, purification comes from placing them on the ground and sprinkling.
For non-edible objects such as cloth, purification comes from performing <s>ācamana</s> without setting them down.
Now he states the purification of objects—
The purification of objects consists of wiping, heating, scraping, and washing
for those made of metal, clay, wood, and thread respectively. // Gaut. 1.31 //

children.text:
taijasādīnāṃ dravyāṇāṃ parimārjanādinā krameṇa śuddhiḥ /
dravyatve siddhe teṣāṃ dravyavacanaṃ svakāryaniṣpādanasārmathyārtham /
tataśca bhinnabhāṇḍādīnāṃ na śaucam /
tejasā hetubhūtena yāni kriyante tāni taijasāni sauvarṇādīni /
teṣāṃ taijasānāmucchiṣṭaliptānām /
kuta etat ? mūtrādyupahatānāṃ smṛtyantare śuddhyantaravidhānāt /
tathā cauśanasaṃ-'taijasānāṃ mūtrapurīṣaretaḥ kuṇapopahatānāṃ āvartanamullekhanaṃ bhasmanā triḥ saptakṛtvaḥ parimārjanam /
ataijasānāmevaṃbhūtānāmutsargaḥ'; iti /
tathā anyaśarīramaladūṣite kaṇvavacanamārabdham- 'śleṣmādyupahatānāmekaviṃśatiparimārjanacchuddhiḥ'; iti /
tathācāspṛśyochiṣṭānāmauśanasaṃ vacanaṃ saṃgatamārabdham- 'anulomaśūdraśvakākopahatānāmullekhanaṃ pratilomeṣu spṛśyopahatānomakaviṃśatiparimarjanamaspṛśyopahatānāmāvartanam'; iti /
tathā māṃsarudhiropahatānāṃ śaṅkhavacanamārabdhaṃ-'mṛdariṣṭakeṅgudabilvasarṣapakalkagomūtragomayādīni śaucadravyāṇi'; iti /
tathā 'rajasvalāduṣṭānāmekadinaṃ pañcagavye nikṣipya ekaviṃśatiparimārjanācchuddhiḥ'; iti paiṭhīnasivacanam /
evamanyeṣvapi smṛtyantareṣu malāntaradūṣiteṣu taijaseṣu śuddhyantarāṇyāmnātāni /
atotrocchiṣṭaliptānāmeva kalpayituṃ nyāyyamiti /
teṣāmucchiṣṭaliptānāṃ parimārjanaṃ bhasmanā paritaḥ sarvataḥ /
mārttikānāṃ mṛnmayānāmaspṛśyopahatānām /
kutaḥ? smṛtyantare viśeṣadarśanāt /
tathośanaso vacanaṃ-'mṛnmayānāmucchiṣṭaliptānāmapamārjanamucchaṣṭaspṛṣṭānāṃ prokṣaṇam'; iti /
tathā vasiṣṭhavacanam-
children.translated_text: The purification of objects made of metal and so forth is by wiping and so forth, in order. The mention of 'objects' when their nature as objects is already established serves to indicate their capacity to fulfill their proper function. Thus, there is no purification for broken vessels and the like. Those which are made with fire (<s>tejas</s>) as their material cause are <s>taijasa</s> (metallic), such as gold vessels and the like. For those metallic objects smeared with food remnants— How is this known? Because another <s>smṛti</s> prescribes a different purification for those defiled by urine and the like. And thus <s>Uśanas</s> states: 'For metallic objects defiled by urine, feces, semen, or a corpse—turning, scraping, rubbing with ash three times or seven times. For non-metallic objects in such condition, they should be discarded.' And for those defiled by bodily impurities of others, the statement of <s>Kaṇva</s> is cited—'For those defiled by phlegm and the like, purification is by twenty-one wipings.' And thus the statement of <s>Uśanas</s> is appropriately cited regarding objects defiled by untouchables—'For those defiled by <s>anuloma</s> <s>Śūdras</s>, dogs, or crows—scraping; for those in the <s>pratiloma</s> category defiled by touchable persons—twenty-one wipings; for those defiled by untouchables—turning.' And for those defiled by meat or blood, the statement of <s>Śaṅkha</s> is cited—'Clay, <s>ariṣṭaka</s>, <s>iṅgudi</s>, <s>bilva</s>, mustard paste, cow urine, cow dung, and the like are purifying substances.' And the statement of <s>Paiṭhīnasi</s>: 'For those defiled by menstrual blood, purification is by immersing in <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five cow products) for one day and twenty-one wipings.' Thus, in other <s>smṛtis</s> as well, different purifications are prescribed for metallic objects defiled by different impurities. Therefore, it is proper to apply this rule here only to those smeared with food remnants. For those smeared with food remnants, wiping means rubbing with ash on all sides, all around. For <s>mārttika</s> (earthen) vessels defiled by untouchables— How so? Because of the specific distinction seen in another <s>smṛti</s>. Thus the statement of <s>Uśanas</s>: 'For earthen vessels smeared with food remnants—wiping; for those touched by food remnants—sprinkling.' And the statement of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>—
By liquor, urine, feces, phlegm, pus, tears, and blood—
An earthen vessel once defiled is not purified even by re-firing.

children.text:
iti madyādidūṣitānāṃ tyāga uktaḥ /
atotra caṇḍālādyupahatānāmeva kalpayituṃ nyāyyamiti /
pradāhaḥ prakarṣeṇa dāhaḥ pūrvasvabhāvotpādanamityarthaḥ /
dāravāṇāṃ āsanaśayanādīnāṃ aṇedhyādyupahatānāṃ takṣaṇaṃ tanūkaraṇaṃ yāvanmātramupahatam /
aspṛśyaspṛṣṭānāṃ prokṣaṇam /
kutaḥ ? 'prokṣaṇaṃ saṃhatānām'; iti manuvacanāt /
prakṣālanaśakyānāṃ prakṣālanam /
tāntavānāṃ tantumayānāṃ kārpāsādivikārāṇāṃ aspṛśyadūṣitānām /

children.translated_text: For those defiled by impurity, another <s>smṛti</s> should be consulted: 'Washing, cutting away the affected portion, or discarding.'
'For garments and the like defiled by impurity and the like'—this is the statement of <s>Paiṭhīnasi</s>.

children.text: tathā 'śrīphalairaṃśupaṭṭānām'; ityevamādīni manunoktāni draṣṭavyāni,aspṛśyadūṣitānāṃ bahūnāṃ vastrāṇāṃ prokṣaṇam 'bahūnāṃ dhānyavāsasāma'; iti manunā prokṣaṇenaiva śuddhividhānāt /
children.translated_text: Likewise, 'with <s>śrīphala</s> (bilva fruit) for silk fabrics'—such statements made by <s>Manu</s> should be consulted. For sprinkling of many garments defiled by untouchables, <s>Manu</s> prescribes purification by sprinkling alone: 'For large quantities of grain and cloth.'
Therefore, for a small number of items defiled by untouchables, washing is prescribed.

Thus, discarding is prescribed for those defiled by liquor and the like. Therefore, it is proper to apply this rule here only to those defiled by <s>Caṇḍālas</s> and the like. <s>Pradāha</s> (intense heating) means burning to a high degree, that is, restoring to the original nature. For wooden objects such as seats, beds, and the like, defiled by impure substances, <s>takṣaṇa</s> (scraping) means paring away as much as has been defiled. For those touched by untouchables—sprinkling. How so? From the statement of <s>Manu</s>: 'Sprinkling for composite objects.' For those that can be washed—washing. For <s>tāntava</s> (woven) objects, that is, those made of thread, such as cotton products and the like, defiled by untouchables—
For stones, gems, conch shells, and oyster shells, the purification is like that of metallic objects. // Gaut. 1.32 //

children.text:
taijasavacchuddhirupalādīnām /
atideśaḥ smṛtyantaroktaśuddhyapekṣārthaḥ /
upalānāṃ maṇīnāṃ tāvacchrūyate-
children.translated_text: The purification of stones and the like is like that of metallic objects. The analogical extension is for the purpose of incorporating purifications stated in other <s>smṛtis</s>. Regarding stones and gems, it is heard—
A gold vessel free from grease is purified simply by water,
As also those made of water-born materials, stone, and silver that are unornamented.
And for conch shells, oyster shells, and gems—by cow urine or water.
This is the statement of <s>Manu</s>.
'For conch shells and oyster shells—by milk'—this is the statement of <s>Paiṭhīnasi</s>.
For bones and the ground, purification is like that of wood. // Gaut. 1.33 //

children.text:
asthi hastidantādisaṃvyavahāryadravyāṇi /
bhūmiḥ, gṛhādiḥ dāruvaditi prakṛtidravyeṇātideśaṃ bruvan etat jñāpayati-yat vikārasya śocamucyate prakṛtidravyasyāpi tadeva bhavatīti /

children.translated_text: Otherwise, the expression would have been 'like wooden objects.'
The analogical extension for bones and the ground is for the purpose of incorporating purifications taught in other <s>smṛtis</s>.
And the analogical extension is for the purpose of incorporating purifications taught in other <s>smṛtis</s>.

children.text: tathā ca smṛtyantaram-'aspṛśyaspṛṣṭānāṃ bhūmyasthnāṃ prokṣaṇācchuddhiḥ'; iti kaṇvavacanam //
children.translated_text: And thus another <s>smṛti</s>: 'For ground and bones touched by untouchables, purification is by sprinkling'—this is the statement of <s>Kaṇva</s>.

Bones refer to objects in common use made of elephant ivory and the like. Ground refers to houses and the like. By stating the analogy with wood as the primary substance, this indicates that the purification stated for a derivative product applies also to the primary substance itself.
And also digging up for the ground. // Gaut. 1.34 //

children.text:
bhūmigrahaṇamasthinivṛttyartham /
cakorāt smṛtyantaroktānyapi draṣṭavyāni /
tathācoktaṃ vasiṣṭhena-
children.translated_text: The mention of 'ground' is for the purpose of excluding bones. The word 'ca' (and) indicates that purifications stated in other <s>smṛtis</s> should also be consulted. And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> states—
By digging, burning, scrubbing, and trampling by cows,
The ground is purified by these four, and fifthly by smearing with cow dung.
Thus.
And likewise <s>Manu</s> states—
By sweeping, sprinkling, burning, scraping,
And by the sojourning of cows—the ground is purified by these five.
Thus.

children.text: yathālepaṃ vikalpena samuccayena vā śaucaṃ kartavyam //
children.translated_text: The purification should be performed either optionally or cumulatively, as appropriate to the degree of defilement.
For ropes, split bamboo articles, and hides, purification is like that of cloth. // Gaut. 1.35 //

children.text:
rajjuḥ darbhādiniṣpannaḥ /
vidalaḥ vaṃśamayūrapakṣādiniṣpannaḥ carma vyāghracarmādi teṣāmaspṛśyaspṛṣṭānāṃ celavat vastravacchaucam /

children.translated_text: By the word 'hide,' the mention of the primary substance implies the inclusion of its derivative products as well.
The analogical extension is for the purpose of including sprinkling as well for ropes and the like.
Therefore, for those touched by untouchables, sprinkling should also be performed.
And thus <s>Paiṭhīnasi</s> states: 'For ropes, split bamboo articles, and hides touched by untouchables, purification is by sprinkling.'

Rope is made from <s>darbha</s> grass and the like. Split bamboo articles are those made from bamboo, peacock feathers, and the like. Hide refers to tiger skin and the like. For those touched by untouchables, the purification is like that of cloth, that is, like that of garments.
Or discarding, for those that are extremely defiled. // Gaut. 1.36 //
That is, discarding of ropes and the like.
This option is a regulated alternative.
Therefore, for those that are extremely defiled, discarding is prescribed.
For the rest, purification applies.
Now, having stated 'one who is holding an object and becomes <s>ucchiṣṭa</s> should set it down and perform <s>ācamana</s>,' with the intention of prescribing the method of <s>ācamana</s>, he says—
One should begin the purification facing east or facing north. // Gaut. 1.37 //

children.text: nanu ca śauca grahaṇamanarthakam, uttaratrācāmoditi vakṣyati, tenaivārthasiddhatvāditi /
children.translated_text: Now, the mention of 'purification' is purposeless, since it will be stated later that 'one should perform <s>ācamana</s>' and the meaning would be established by that alone.
It is answered: one should perform all other subsidiary acts of purification also while facing that very direction.

children.text: evaṃ ca pādaprakṣālanādikamapi taddigabhimukha eva kuryāditi /
children.translated_text: And thus, the washing of feet and other such acts should also be performed while facing that very direction.

children.text: ārabheteti samāhitārtham, ato yāvadācamanaparisamāptiḥ tāvantaṃ kālamananyacitto bhavet //
children.translated_text: The word 'should begin' implies a composed mind; therefore, throughout the entire duration until the completion of <s>ācamana</s>, one should remain undistracted.
Facing east or facing north—the option is according to one's wish.

children.text: śucau deśa āsīno dakṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ jānvantarā kṛtvā yajñopavītyā maṇibandhātpāṇī prakṣālya vāgyato hṛdayaspṛśastriścaturvāpa ācāmet // Gaut_1.38 //
children.translated_text: Seated in a clean place, placing the right arm between the knees, wearing the sacred thread, having washed the hands from the wrist, silently, one should sip water three or four times, the water reaching the heart. // Gaut. 1.38 //

children.text:
śucau deśe sthāne anupahate /
evaṃ ca pādaprakṣālanamapyarthasiddhaṃ mā bhūt
children.translated_text: In a clean place, that is, a spot that is undefiled. And thus, the washing of feet is also implicitly established, lest

children.text:
aśuddhipādasambandhāddeśasyāpyaśucibhāva iti /
tathā ca vakhiṣṭhaḥ- 'prakṣālya pādau pāṇo cā maṇibandhanāt'; iti /
āsīna eva, nānyāvasthaḥ /
tathāca vasiṣṭhaḥ-'vrajan tiṣṭhan śayānaḥ praṇato vā nācāmet'; iti /
dākṣiṇaṃ bāhuṃ jānvormadhye kṛtvā /
yajñopavītoti /
yadi kadācit ayajñopavīti bhūtvāpyāste tathāpyācamane avaśyaṃ yajñopavītinā bhavitavyamiti /
tathā cāpaspambaḥ-'upāsane gurūṇāṃ vṛddhānāmatithīnāṃ home japyakarmaṇi bhojana ācamane svādhyāye ca yajñopavīti syāt'; iti /
ācamanāṅgatvenānyayajñopavītotpādanārthaṃ vā /
tathā ca vasiṣṭhaḥ-
children.translated_text: the place become impure due to contact with impure feet. And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> states: 'Having washed the feet and hands from the wrist.' One should be seated only, not in any other posture. And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> states: 'One should not perform <s>ācamana</s> while walking, standing, lying down, or bowing.' The right arm should be placed between the two knees. Regarding the sacred thread: even if one happens to be without the sacred thread, one must nevertheless wear it during <s>ācamana</s>. And thus <s>Āpastamba</s> states: 'One should wear the sacred thread while attending upon elders, the aged, and guests, during oblations, meditative recitation, eating, <s>ācamana</s>, and Vedic study.' Or, this is for the purpose of obtaining another sacred thread as an accessory to <s>ācamana</s>. And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> states—
For <s>snātakas</s> (graduated students), there should always be an inner garment and an upper garment,
Two sacred threads, a staff, and a water vessel filled with water.
Thus.

children.text:
maṇiryasmindeśe badhyate sa maṇibandhaḥ /
tasmādāmaṇibandhanātpāṇī prakṣālya vāgyatastūrṣṇīṃ hṛdayaspṛśo hṛdayaṃgamāḥ /
apāṃparimāṇārthamidam /
māṣanimajjanamātrāstāvatyo bhavanti /
tathācāhośanā 'māṣanimajjanamātrā hṛdayaṃgamā bhavanti'; iti /
triścaturvetyatra vikalpo vyavasthitaḥ- yadā 'āpaḥ punantu'; ityādimantramuktvā'camyate tadā catuḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>maṇibandha</s> (wrist) is the place where a bracelet is tied. Therefore, having washed the hands from the wrist, silently, meaning in silence, the water should reach the heart. This is for specifying the quantity of water. The amount should be enough to submerge a <s>māṣa</s> bean—that much water should be taken. And thus <s>Uśanas</s> states: 'The water should be enough to submerge a <s>māṣa</s> bean and should reach the heart.' Regarding 'three or four times,' the option is regulated: when one performs <s>ācamana</s> reciting the mantra beginning with '<s>āpaḥ punantu</s>' (may the waters purify), then four times;

children.text: abgrahaṇaṃ gomūtrādinivṛttyarthaṃ teṣāṃ śuddhihetutvasāmānyādgrahaṇaṃ mā bhūditi /
children.translated_text: The mention of 'water' is for the purpose of excluding cow urine and the like, lest they be included due to their similar capacity for purification.
Or, it is for the purpose of excluding hot water, bubbling water, water with foam, astringent substances, and the like.
Instead of saying 'he should drink,' the use of '<s>ācāmet</s>' (he should perform <s>ācamana</s>) in the <s>sūtra</s> is for the purpose of encompassing other prescribed methods.

children.text: tatra tūśanā'ha- 'dakṣiṇaṃ hastatalaṃ gokarṇākāraṃ vinyasya brāhmeṇa tīrthenāśabdaṃ pibedṛgyajuḥsāmavedān dhyāyan'; iti //
children.translated_text: Regarding this, <s>Uśanas</s> states: 'Arranging the right palm in the shape of a cow's ear, one should drink silently through the <s>Brāhma tīrtha</s> (the base of the thumb), while meditating on the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāma Vedas</s>.'
Otherwise, three times.
One should wipe twice. // Gaut. 1.39 //

The implied subject is the lips, since they are the topic under discussion; because they are not mentioned otherwise here; and because of evidence from other <s>smṛtis</s>—it should be done with the <s>Brāhma tīrtha</s> (base of the thumb) alone.
The prefix 'pari' (around) is for the purpose of encompassing other prescribed methods.

children.text: tatra tūktaṃ kaṇvena-'atharvavedetihāsapurāṇāni dhyāyan brāhmeṇa tīrthenoṣṭhayoḥ salomapradeśaṃ mṛjyāt'; iti //
children.translated_text: Regarding this, <s>Kaṇva</s> states: 'While meditating on the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, the <s>Itihāsas</s>, and the <s>Purāṇas</s>, one should wipe the lips with the <s>Brāhma tīrtha</s> in the direction of the hair growth, using the index finger.'
And one should sprinkle the feet. // Gaut. 1.40 //

children.text:
cakārāt mukhaṃ ca /
abhyupasargo vidhyantaropasaṃgrahārthaḥ /
tatrāha bhārgavaḥ-'oṣṭhau parimṛjyāttato mukhaṃ
children.translated_text: By the word 'ca' (and), the face as well. The prefix 'abhi' is for the purpose of encompassing other prescribed methods. Regarding this, <s>Bhārgava</s> states: 'Having wiped the lips, then one should wipe the face
while meditating on <s>Agni</s>, and then sprinkle the feet while meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'
And one should touch the orifices located on the head. // Gaut. 1.41 //

children.text:
khāni śīrṣaṇyāni nayananāsikākarṇāni /
cakārāddhṛdayaṃ ca /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: The orifices on the head are the eyes, nostrils, and ears. By the word 'ca' (and), the heart as well. And thus <s>Manu</s> states—
One should first sip water three times, then wipe the mouth twice,
And touch the orifices with water, as well as the self, the heart, and the head.
Thus.

children.text: upopasargo vidhyantaropasaṃgrahārthaḥ tannośanā 'aṅguṣṭhopakaniṣṭikābhyāṃ nayane candrādityau dhyātvā tata upaspṛśya tarjanyaṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ nāsikāvakāśau prāṇān dhyātvā tata upaspṛśya kaniṣṭhikāṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ karṇau diśo dhyātvā tata upaspṛśyāṅguṣṭhena kevalena hṛdayamupaspṛśedātmānaṃ dhyāyan'; iti //
children.translated_text: The prefix 'upa' is for the purpose of encompassing other prescribed methods. Regarding this, <s>Uśanas</s> states: 'With the thumb and little finger, having meditated on the moon and sun, one should touch the two eyes; then with the index finger and thumb, having meditated on the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths), one should touch the two nostrils; then with the little finger and thumb, having meditated on the directions, one should touch the two ears; then with the thumb alone, one should touch the heart while meditating on the <s>ātman</s> (self).'
And one should place water on the crown of the head. // Gaut. 1.42 //

children.text: mūrdhani cet vaktavye dadyāditi grahaṇaṃ sarvāṅgulyartham /
tathāca smṛtyantaraṃ 'sarvāṅgulibhiḥ śriyaṃ dhyātvā mūrdhani prakṣipet'; iti /
children.translated_text: And thus another <s>smṛti</s> states: 'With all fingers, while meditating on <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of prosperity), one should sprinkle water on the crown of the head.'
By the word 'ca' (and), on the left palm as well.

children.text: tathā ca vasiṣṭhaḥ-'mūrdhani ca dadyātsavye pāṇau'; iti /
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> states: 'One should place water on the crown of the head and on the left palm.'

children.text: kṣatriyavaiśyayorapyetadevācamanaṃ viśeṣānabhidhānāt strīśūdrau ca sakṛtsakṛt'; iti smṛtyantarābhidhānāt strīśūdrayośca sakṛtpānāt sakṛdoṣṭhasparśanācca śuddhirdraṣṭavyā atrānuktāpi //
children.translated_text: This same <s>ācamana</s> procedure applies to <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> as well, since no distinction is stated. However, from the statement in another <s>smṛti</s> that 'women and <s>Śūdras</s> should sip once each,' for women and <s>Śūdras</s>, purification should be understood as coming from sipping once and touching the lips once, even though this is not stated here.
Instead of simply saying 'on the crown of the head,' the use of the word 'should place' indicates that all fingers should be used.
Not only upon contact with food remnants should <s>ācamana</s> be performed; now he states other occasions for <s>ācamana</s> as well—

children.text: suptvā bhuktvā kṣutvā ca punaḥ // Gaut_1.43 //
children.translated_text: After sleeping, eating, and sneezing, one should perform <s>ācamana</s> again. // Gaut. 1.43 //
The repetition [of the word] is for the purpose [of indicating] that one should perform <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping) both at the beginning and at the end.
By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), [it includes] after bathing and after weeping.

children.text: tathā ca vasiṣṭhaḥ- 'suptvā bhuktvā kṣutvā snātvā pītvā ruditvā cācāntaḥ punarācāmet'; iti //
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> [states]: 'After sleeping, eating, sneezing, bathing, drinking, and weeping, one who has sipped should sip again.'

children.text:
tatra kṣutasyāniyatakālatvāt ādāvaśakyamācamanamiti cet tatrāpi nityaprāyatyārtha ārambhaḥ /
yathā'hāpastambaḥ-'muhūrtamapi śaktiviṣaye nāprayatastiṣṭhet'; iti /
svāpādau prayatasyāpyācamanamārambhasārmathyāt /
atastatrādāvante cācamanaṃ kuryāt tatra bhojane kecidādāvapi dvirācamanamicchanti /
tathācāpastambaḥ 'bhokṣyamāṇastu prayato dvirācāmet'; iti /
anye svāpādāvanta eva dvirācamanamicchanti yathā'hośanā-
children.translated_text: Regarding this, since sneezing occurs at an indeterminate time, if one objects that <s>ācamana</s> at the beginning is impossible—even there the commencement is for the purpose of constant ritual purity. As <s>Āpastamba</s> [states]: 'One should not remain in a state of impurity even for a moment, when it is within one's power.' Even for one who is ritually pure, <s>ācamana</s> is [required] after sleeping and the rest, by the force of the injunction. Therefore, one should perform <s>ācamana</s> both at the beginning and at the end in those cases. Regarding eating, some desire <s>ācamana</s> twice even at the beginning. And thus <s>Āpastamba</s> [states]: 'One who is about to eat, being ritually pure, should sip twice.' Others desire <s>ācamana</s> twice only at the end after sleeping and the rest. As <s>Uśanas</s> [states]—

children.text: 'suptvā bhuktvā kṣutvā snātvā pītvā ruditvā cācāntaḥ punarācāmeddvi'; iti /
children.translated_text: 'After sleeping, eating, sneezing, bathing, drinking, and weeping, one who has sipped should sip again twice.'

children.text: evaṃ ca bhojane ādāvante cca dvirācamanaṃ svāpādāvekamante ca dviḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, regarding eating, <s>ācamana</s> is performed twice both at the beginning and at the end; after sleeping and the rest, once at the beginning and twice at the end.
Since sneezing is of indeterminate [timing], twice at the end only—this is the established conclusion.

children.text:
idānīnucchiṣṭasaṃśleṣe aśucitve prāpte āha-
dantaśliṣṭeṣu dantavadanyatra jihvābhimarśanāt //
children.translated_text: Now, when the suspicion of impurity due to contact with food remnants (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>) arises, [the author] says: Regarding what clings to the teeth, one is [pure] like the teeth themselves, elsewhere [it is impure] due to contact with the tongue. (Gaut 1.44 [sic])
When particles of food cling between the teeth, the meaning is that one is not rendered impure (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>), just like the teeth [themselves remain pure].
Provided they are not touched by the tongue.
Regarding this also—
'Before dislodgement'—according to some. (Gaut 1.44)

children.text: satyapi jihvābhimarśane yāvat svasthānānna cyavanti tāvacchucirityeke manyante //
children.translated_text: Some hold that even when there is contact with the tongue, one is pure as long as [the particles] do not fall from their place.
When they have fallen, one should know [the rule] as with saliva; one who swallows them is indeed pure. (Gaut 1.46)

children.text:
cyuteṣu āsye yajjalaṃ tadāsrāve yadvadvijātīyāt tannigiran śucacireva bhavati /
ācamanaśaṅkā
children.translated_text: When [the particles] have fallen, the liquid in the mouth is like saliva; one who swallows that from a twice-born person is indeed pure. The doubt about [the need for] <s>ācamana</s>

children.text:
nāstītyarthaḥ /
evaṃ cāsrāvamapi nigiran śucireva bhavati /
kutaḥ cyuteṣu nigiran śuciriti vaktavye āsrāvavadvidyādityārambhāt /
children.translated_text: Why? Because when it should have been stated 'one who swallows [particles] that have fallen is pure,' the commencement with 'one should know as with saliva' [indicates this broader meaning].
But <s>Gautama</s>'s [view is that] when there is contact with the tongue regarding particles clinging to the teeth, one becomes impure.
The other opinion, however, is 'before dislodgement.'
This is an established alternative: for one who is engaged in the performance of a ritual act, <s>ācamana</s> [is required]; for another, it is not.
does not exist—this is the meaning. And thus, even one who swallows saliva is indeed pure.

children.text: yathocchiṣṭāvayavo bahirbhūtaḥ aśucitvamāpādayati tadvadāsrāvasyāpi prāpta āha-
children.translated_text: Just as a portion of leftover food (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>) that has gone outside causes impurity, so too when the same applies to saliva, [the author] says—

children.text: na mukhyā vipruṣa ucchiṣṭaṃ kurvanti na cedaṅge nipatanti // Gaut_1.47 //
children.translated_text: Drops from the mouth do not render one impure (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>), provided they do not fall on a limb. (Gaut 1.47)

children.text: mukhe bhavā mukhyāḥ vipruṣa āsrābāvayavāḥ te mantrayamāṇasya vinirgatā nāprāyatyaṃ janayanti yadyaṅge stanodarādau na nipatanti /
children.translated_text: Those originating in the mouth are 'oral drops'—portions of saliva. When they emerge from one who is reciting [mantras], they do not cause impurity, if they do not fall on a limb such as the chest or stomach.

children.text: niśabdo niścayārthaḥ ato niścayena yadyaṅge patanti tadānīmevocchiṣṭaṃ janayanti nāśaṅkāmātreṇeti /
