children.translated_text: The prefix 'ni-' has the meaning of certainty. Therefore, certainly if they fall on a limb, then they cause impurity—not from mere suspicion.

children.text: evaṃ cocchiṣṭāvayavo yatrakutracinnipatannucchiṣṭaṃ janayati, āsrāvo 'ṅga eveti siddhāntaḥ //
children.translated_text: And thus a portion of leftover food falling anywhere causes impurity, [but] saliva only [when falling] on a limb—this is the established conclusion.
For the purpose of all purification, this is now stated—
Purification of one smeared with impure matter consists in the removal of the smear and the smell. (Gaut 1.48)

children.text: lepagandhayorapanayane kṛte amedhyaliptasya amedhyasambaddhasya śucitvaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: When the removal of the smear and the smell has been accomplished, the purity of one smeared with impure matter—one who has come into contact with impure matter—is established.
By the word 'impure matter' (<s>amedha</s>), the twelve bodily impurities are denoted.
As <s>Manu</s> states—
Fat, semen, blood, marrow, urine, feces, nasal discharge, ear-wax,

children.text: śleṣmāśru dūṣikā svedo dvādaśaite nṛṇāṃ malāḥ //
children.translated_text: phlegm, tears, eye-discharge, and sweat—these are the twelve impurities of human beings.
The mention of 'smear' is because for phlegm and the rest, whose smell is not manifest, only the smear is observed.
The mention of 'smell' is because for urine and the rest, the smear is not perceived, but only the smell is perceived.

children.text: śaucādhikāre punaḥ śaucagrahaṇaṃ taijasādīnāmapi lepagandhāpanayanayādeva śaucamityevamartham //
children.translated_text: The repetition of the word 'purification' (<s>śauca</s>) in the context of purification is for the purpose [of indicating] that even for metallic and other objects, purification is accomplished precisely through the removal of smear and smell.
By what means should that [purification] be performed? Therefore [the author] says—
That [should be done] first with water and then with earth. (Gaut 1.49)

children.text:
tacchaucamadbhiḥ pūrvaṃ tato mṛdā /
cakārāttata ubhayena /
tadgrahaṇaṃ annalepasyāpi cūrṇādinā apakarṣaṇārtham /
tadadbhirmṛdā ceti vaktavye pūrvagrahaṇaṃ yatra nātīva lepo lakṣyate tatrādbhireva śasaucamityevamarthaṃ, yathā'ha manuḥ-
children.translated_text: That purification [is done] first with water, then with earth. By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), then with both. The word 'that' is for the purpose [of indicating] that the removal of food-smear also [may be done] with powder and the like. When it should have been stated 'that [is done] with water and earth,' the word 'first' is for the purpose [of indicating] that where the smear is not very visible, purification is by water alone. As <s>Manu</s> states—
'A golden vessel free of smear is purified by water alone,
as well as [vessels] of aquatic origin, stone, and unadorned silver.'
Thus.

children.text: athavā yatra yatra śaucamuktaṃ tatra tatrādbhireva śaucaṃ prathamaṃ kāryamityevamartham /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, wherever purification is enjoined, there purification should first be done with water alone—this is the meaning.

children.text: yathā mṛdā adbhiriti samuccīyate tathā bhasmādibhirapi samuccayārtho visamāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as earth is conjoined with water, so too the compound [implies] conjunction with ash and the like as well.

children.text: taisajādīnāṃ dravyāṇāmuktatvāt idaṃ śaucaṃ śarīrāvayavasyāmedhyaliptasya draṣṭavyam //
children.translated_text: Since metallic and other substances have [already] been mentioned, this purification should be understood as applying to a limb of the body smeared with impure matter.
And in cases of the discharge of urine, feces, and semen, and in connection with eating. (Gaut 1.50)

children.text:
cakāraḥ ācamanānukarṣaṇārthaḥ /
visraṃsanaṃ nirasanaṃ, tat mūtrapūrīṣasrehūṇāṃ pratyekaṃ sambadhyate /
abhyavahārasaṃyogo 'bhyavahāryadravyopayogaḥ /
tasyānamedhyatvāt lepagandhāpakarṣaṇārthamabhidhānaṃ, ācamanasya 'suptvā bhuktvā'; ityanena siddhatvāt lepagandhāpakarṣaṇaṃ ca mṛtsalilaprakṣālanena kuryāt /
evaṃ ca 'tadadbhiḥ pūrvam'; ityatra yaduktaṃ cūrṇādinā annalepāpakarṣaṇaṃ tenāśakyamidaṃ draṣṭavyam /
athavā-abhyavahārasaṃyogasyāpi ācamanārtha evopanyāsaḥ /
'suptvā bhuktvā'; ityanenaiva siddhamanūdyate kramārtham, kathaṃ-tadgrahaṇenānnalepāpakarṣaṇamuktaṃ tadapakarṣaṇaṃ pūrvaṃ kṛtvā tataācāmedityevamarthaṃ anyathā sandehaḥ syāditi /
tathā cāpastambaḥ 'mūtraṃ kṛtvā pūrīṣaṃ vā mūtrapurīṣalepānannalepānucchiṣṭalepān
children.translated_text: The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is for the purpose of drawing in <s>ācamana</s>. 'Discharge' (<s>visraṃsana</s>) means emission; that is connected with each of urine, feces, and semen individually. 'Connection with eating' means the use of edible substances. Since that is not [in itself] impure, the statement is for the purpose of removing smear and smell, since <s>ācamana</s> has already been established by 'after sleeping, eating' and so forth. And the removal of smear and smell should be done by washing with earth and water. And thus, what was stated in 'that [should be done] first with water'—[namely] the removal of food-smear with powder and the like—should be understood by this. Alternatively, the mention of 'connection with eating' is for the purpose of <s>ācamana</s> alone. What has already been established by 'after sleeping, eating' is restated for the purpose of [indicating] the sequence: how?—the word 'that' [implies] the removal of food-smear has been stated; having first performed that removal, then one should sip—this is the meaning; otherwise there would be doubt. And thus <s>Āpastamba</s> [states]: 'Having performed urination or defecation, having washed away the smears of urine, feces, food-remnants, leftover-food smears,

children.text: retasaśca ye lepāstān prakṣālya pādau cācamya prayato bhavati'; iti /
children.translated_text: and the smears of semen, and having washed the feet and sipped, one becomes ritually pure.'
Urine and feces are well-known.
<s>Srehu</s> means semen.
The mention of urine and the rest is for the purpose of <s>ācamana</s>, since the removal of smear and smell has already been established by 'purification consists in the removal of smear and smell.'
And where the sacred tradition (<s>āmnāya</s>) would prescribe. (Gaut 1.51)

children.text:
tatra tadeva bhavatīti śeṣaḥ /
āmnāyo vedaḥ, sa yatra yajñaviṣaye sphyādīnāṃ prakṣālanamātrādeva śuddhiṃ vidadhyāt tatra tadeva, na dārusāmānyena takṣaṇādi /
atulyabalatvādevedaṃ siddhamiti cet śrutyuktasya laukike ananupraveśanārtha upanyāsaḥ, yathār davyā yāgaviṣaye śrutyā prakṣālanena śuddhiruktā, tasyā laukike vyāpṛtāyā api
children.translated_text: There, that alone applies—this completes [the sentence]. The <s>āmnāya</s> is the <s>Veda</s>. Where it, in the context of sacrifice, would prescribe purification of the sacrificial ladle (<s>sphya</s>) and the like merely by washing, there that alone [applies], not planing and the like as would apply to wood in general. If one objects that this is already established because the [Vedic] injunction is of unequal force [i.e., stronger]—the statement is for the purpose of [ensuring] that what is stated by <s>śruti</s> does not enter into the secular domain. For example, in the context of sacrifice, purification of the ladle by washing is stated by <s>śruti</s>; lest [one think] that for a ladle used in secular contexts too,

children.text:
darvīsāmānyena śrutyuktā mā bhūt smṛtyuktāmeva kuryādityevamarthamupanyāsaḥ /
athavā-āmnāyaśabdena manurucyate /
sa yatra śaucaṃ vidadhyāt tatra tadeva, yathā 'yatīnāṃ tu caturguṇam'; ityādi /
children.translated_text: Where he would prescribe purification, there that alone [applies], as for example 'for ascetics, however, fourfold' and so forth.

children.text: taduktatvādevāsandeha iti cet ucyate- yasminviṣaye na kiṃciducyate tatra smṛtyantaroktaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: If [one objects that] since it is stated by him there is no doubt—it is said: in a matter where nothing is stated, the rule stated by another <s>smṛti</s> applies.

children.text: yatra lepagandhāpakarṣaṇādi kiṃciducyate tatra smṛtyantareṇa vikalpaśaṅkā bhavatīti tannirāsārthamuktaṃ 'yatra cāmnāyo vidadhyāt'; iti /
children.translated_text: Where something such as the removal of smear and smell is stated, there the suspicion of an alternative from another <s>smṛti</s> arises. To refute that, it is stated 'and where the sacred tradition would prescribe.'

children.text: evaṃ ca lepagandhāpakarṣaṇe kṛte 'pi 'dviguṇaṃ brahmacāriṇaḥ'; ityevamādyāśrayaṇīyam //
children.translated_text: And thus, even when the removal of smear and smell has been performed, [rules such as] 'twofold for a <s>brahmacārin</s>' and the like should be followed.

by the generality of 'ladle,' the <s>śruti</s>-stated [rule] should apply, one should follow only the <s>smṛti</s>-stated [rule]—this is the purpose of the statement. Alternatively, by the word <s>āmnāya</s>, <s>Manu</s> is referred to.
Now [the author] states the rule for the <s>brahmacārin</s>'s approaching the <s>guru</s> for the purpose of study, after purification has been performed—

children.text: pāṇinā savyamupasaṅgṛhyānaṅguṣṭhamadhīhi bho ityāmantrayeta gurum // Gaut_1.52 //
children.translated_text: Grasping [the <s>guru</s>'s] left [hand] with his hand, excluding the thumb, he should address the <s>guru</s>: 'Teach, sir!' (Gaut 1.52)

children.text:
pāṇinā dakṣiṇena savyaṃ pāṇimanaṅguṣṭhavarjitaṃ gṛhītvā adhīhi bho iti prārthayeta gurumadhyāpakam /
pāṇigrahaṇaṃ pādanivṛttyartham /
pāṇiprakaraṇātasavyamapi pāṇimeveti gamyate /
upasaṅgrahaṇaṃ aṅgulipradeśe iti
children.translated_text: Having grasped the left hand, excluding the thumb, with the right hand, he should request the <s>guru</s>, the teacher, [saying] 'Teach, sir!' The mention of 'hand' is to exclude the foot. Since this is in the context of 'hand,' [the word] 'left' is understood to refer to the hand as well. 'Grasping' is understood to be at the region of the fingers,
since 'excluding the thumb' has been stated.
Furthermore—
There, [one should fix] the eyes and the mind [on the <s>guru</s>]. (Gaut 1.53)
There, one should fix the eyes and mind on the <s>guru</s>—this is the meaning.
Furthermore—
Touching the vital organs (<s>prāṇa</s>) with <s>darbha</s> grass. (Gaut 1.54)
'Should be done'—this completes [the sentence].
Since directly touching the vital breaths is impossible, by '<s>prāṇa</s>' are meant the sense organs situated on the head, such as the eyes and the rest.
One should touch them with <s>darbha</s> grass in the sequence stated for <s>ācamana</s>.
Furthermore—
Three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-retentions), each of fifteen measures (<s>mātrā</s>). (Gaut 1.55)
'Should be done'—this completes [the sentence].

children.text: prāṇāyāmaḥ prāṇanirodhaḥ nirucchvāsenāvasthānaṃ, te trayaḥ kāryāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-retention) is the restraint of breath—remaining without exhalation. Three of these should be performed.
Each of fifteen measures.
A 'measure' (<s>mātrā</s>) is well-known in the world by the term 'middle finger-snap.'
Furthermore—
And sitting on [<s>darbha</s> grass with tips pointing] eastward. (Gaut 1.56)
On [grass] with tips pointing east—<s>darbha</s> grass, from the context—sitting means taking a seat. 'Should be done'—this completes [the sentence].
By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), also [having] a <s>darbha</s> purificatory ring (<s>pavitra</s>).
Furthermore—
The five <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred exclamations), preceded by <s>Oṃ</s>, ending with <s>Satya</s>. (Gaut 1.57)
'Should be recited'—this completes [the sentence].
Each preceded by the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> (<s>praṇava</s>), the three [<s>vyāhṛtis</s>] beginning with '<s>Bhūr</s>' and the rest, with '<s>Puruṣa</s>' in the middle, ending with '<s>Satya</s>.'
Thus it is well-known in the <s>Jābāli</s> <s>śruti</s>.
Furthermore—
Clasping the <s>guru</s>'s feet in the morning. (Gaut 1.58)

children.text:
kāryamiti śeṣaḥ /
upasaṅgrahaṇamiti vaktavye pādagrahaṇaṃ smṛtyantaropadiṣṭavidhyupasaṅgrahaṇārtham /
yathā'ha manuḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Should be done'—this completes [the sentence]. When 'clasping' (<s>upasaṅgrahaṇa</s>) should have been stated, the mention of 'feet' is for the purpose of incorporating the rule prescribed by other <s>smṛtis</s>. As <s>Manu</s> states—
'The clasping of the <s>guru</s> should be done with hands crossed:

children.text: savyena savyaḥ spṛṣṭavyo dakṣiṇena tu dakṣiṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: the left [foot] should be touched with the left [hand], and the right with the right.'
Thus.
'In the morning' means having risen, [i.e.,] every day.
The mention of '<s>guru</s>' is to [indicate that it should] not [be done] to oneself.
Therefore, prior [to clasping the <s>guru</s>'s feet], the touching of one's own vital organs (<s>prāṇa</s>) [should be done].
Furthermore—
And at the beginning and end of <s>Veda</s> recitation. (Gaut 1.59)
At the beginning and end—the commencement and conclusion—of <s>Veda</s> recitation.
The word 'and' (<s>ca</s>) is for the purpose of drawing in the clasping of [the <s>guru</s>'s] feet.
Furthermore—

children.text: anujñāta upaviśetprāṅmukho dakṣiṇataḥ śiṣya udaṅmukho vā // Gaut_1.60 //
children.translated_text: Having been permitted, the student should sit to the south, facing east or facing north. (Gaut 1.60)

children.text: ācāryeṇādiṣṭaḥ tasya dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vopaviśet saṃbhavato vikalpaḥ āsīnasyācāryasya yathā tadabhimukho bhavati tathā prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vā upaviśedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having been directed by the teacher, he should sit in the southern direction from him, facing east or facing north. The alternative is where possible. The meaning is that he should sit facing east or facing north, in whichever way he faces the teacher when the teacher is seated.
How so? Because it has been stated 'there, [one should fix] the eyes and the mind [on the <s>guru</s>].'
The mention of 'student' is to indicate that this very rule applies to any other person who has approached [for study].

children.text: 'anujñāto dakṣiṇataḥ'; iti ca niyamārthaḥ nānanujñāta upaviśennādakṣiṇata iti //
children.translated_text: 'Having been permitted, to the south' is also a restrictive rule: one should not sit without permission, nor [sit] other than to the south.
Furthermore—
And the <s>Sāvitrī</s> recitation at the beginning, at the commencement of <s>Veda</s> study. (Gaut 1.61)

children.text:
sāvitrī tatsaviturityādi /
cakārādoṅkārapūrvā vyāhṛtayaśca /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: The <s>Sāvitrī</s> is [the verse beginning] 'tat savitur' and so forth. By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), also the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> preceded by <s>Oṃ</s>. And thus <s>Manu</s> [states]—
'The three great <s>vyāhṛtis</s> preceded by <s>Oṃ</s>, imperishable,

children.text: tripadā caiva gāyatrī vijñeyā brahmaṇo mukham //
children.translated_text: and the three-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s>—these should be known as the mouth of <s>Brahman</s>.'
Thus.
'Recitation' (<s>anuvacana</s>) means it should be studied.
'At the commencement of the <s>Veda</s>' means at the beginning, at the time of commencing study—this is the meaning.
'At the beginning' means first.
Furthermore—
The syllable <s>Oṃ</s> [is used] on other occasions as well. (Gaut 1.62)

children.text:
anuvacanānantaraṃ oṅkāraścodāhartavyaḥ anyatrāpi /
atra kramaḥ prātarutthāya pādaupasaṅgrahaṇaṃ, tadāhūya upaviśet darbheṣu, tataḥ prāṇopasparśanaṃ darbhaiḥ, tataḥ prāṇāyāmānkṛtvā mahāvyāhṛtīḥ pañca uktvā, añjalinā 'adhīhi bhoḥ'; iti gurumāmantrya, oṅkārapūrvikā vyāhṛtīḥ sāvitrīṃ coktvā praṇavapūrvamadhīyīta /
prathamādhyayana evāyaṃ vidhiḥ kutaḥ ? sāvitrī cānuvacanaṃ tato 'dhīyīteti vaktavye ādito brahmaṇa ādāna ityārambhāt /
pratidivasamoṅkāramevoktvā /

children.translated_text: Why? Because it has been stated '<s>Oṃ</s> on other occasions.'
'Other occasions' means occasions other than the first study session.
The word 'also' (<s>api</s>) is for the purpose of including <s>praṇava</s> in the first study session as well.
Some, by 'on other occasions also,' desire <s>praṇava</s> at the beginning of subsidiary [texts] as well.

After the recitation, the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> should be uttered on other occasions as well. Here the sequence is: having risen in the morning, clasping [the <s>guru</s>'s] feet; then, having been summoned, sitting on <s>darbha</s> grass; then touching the vital organs (<s>prāṇa</s>) with <s>darbha</s> grass; then having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s> and recited the five great <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, addressing the <s>guru</s> with joined palms [saying] 'Teach, sir!', and having recited the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> preceded by <s>Oṃ</s> and the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, one should study preceded by <s>praṇava</s>. This rule applies only at the first [session of] study. Why? Because when it should have been stated 'and the <s>Sāvitrī</s> recitation, then one should study,' the commencement with 'at the beginning, at the commencement of <s>Veda</s> study' [indicates this]. On each [subsequent] day, one recites only <s>Oṃ</s>.
Upon arrival during an interval, re-approaching [is required]. (Gaut 1.63)

children.text:
yadyadhīyatāmantarā madhye kaścidgacchettataḥ punarapi pādopasaṅgrahaṇādipraṇavoccāraṇānto yo vidhistaṃ kuryāttasya prāyaścittārtham /
aprakaraṇe 'pi prāyaścittamānantaryeṇānuṣṭhānārtham /
mānuṣāṇāṃ gamana etat, itareṣāmūrdhvamabhidhānāt /

children.translated_text: Since no prohibition of study is heard here, one should study immediately after the expiation.
The repetition is with reference to the first study session as well, since there is no re-approaching on other occasions.
Therefore, on other occasions, the re-approaching should be done only for the purpose of expiation, and study should be done immediately after that.
And thus <s>Āpastamba</s> [states]: 'Having said "Teach, sir!" one should study or teach.'

If someone arrives in the middle of what is being studied, then again the entire procedure from clasping the feet up to the utterance of <s>praṇava</s> should be performed, for the purpose of expiation. Even outside the [study] context, the expiation is for the purpose of immediate performance [of purification]. This [rule] applies to the arrival of human beings; for others, it will be stated later.
Furthermore—
For [contact with] a dog, mongoose, snake, frog, or cat—three days of fasting and ritual seclusion. (Gaut 1.64)

children.text:
ete prasiddhāḥ /
śvādīnāṃ pratyekamantarā manage tryahaṃ bhaktatyāgaḥ prāyaścittaṃ, vipravāso guruṇā virahitasyāvasthānamekāham /
evaṃ ca guruviprayogopadeśādeva ekāhamanadhyāyasiddhiḥ /
kuta ekāhopalabdhiriti cet, visamāsāt /
anyathā tryahamupavāsavipravāsau cetyavakṣyat /
ata ekāhamevānadhyāyaḥ /
tathā ca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: These are well-known. For dogs and other [animals listed], individually, a three-day fast as <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) for each intervening [passage], and <s>vipravāsa</s> (separation) means staying for one day without one's <s>guru</s> (teacher). And thus, from the instruction regarding separation from the <s>guru</s> alone, the establishment of one day of non-study (<s>anadhyāya</s>) is achieved. If one asks, whence is the determination of one day obtained? From the compound analysis. Otherwise, he would have said 'three days of fasting and separation.' Therefore, the non-study period is one day only. And thus <s>Manu</s> states:
When a domestic animal, a frog, a cat, a dog, a snake, or a mongoose,
passes between [teacher and student], one should know that non-study (<s>anadhyāya</s>) lasts for a day and a night.
Thus.

children.text:
evaṃ cātrāpi śvagrahaṇaṃ catuṣpadāṃ paśūnāmupalakṣaṇam /
catuṣpādgrahaṇena gṛhyamāṇatvāt mārjārasya punarupanyāsaḥ prāyaścittagauravārthaḥ /
yathā'hośanā- 'mārjārāntarāgamane dhṛtaṃ prāśyatryahamupavaset'; iti /

children.translated_text: The word 'ca' (and) is for the purpose of drawing in <s>upasadana</s> (respectful approach [to the teacher]).
Therefore, having performed that during the time of study, one should study.
Some say fasting means cessation of study.
Whether that is proper or improper should be deliberated.

And thus here too, the mention of 'dog' is illustrative of four-footed domestic animals. The separate mention of 'cat,' though already included by the term 'four-footed,' is for the purpose of emphasizing the gravity of its expiation. As <s>Ahośanā</s> states: 'When a cat passes between [teacher and student], one should consume ghee and fast for three days.' Thus.
Moreover:
<s>Prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls) and consumption of ghee for the others. (Gaut. 1.65)
For the others, namely crows and so forth, three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls), because of the plural form being heard.
Consumption of ghee means merely a bodily purification.
The word 'ca' (and) has the purpose of drawing in <s>upasadana</s> (respectful approach).

children.text: tatastrīnprāṇāyāmān dhārayitvā ghṛtaṃ prāśyopasadanaṃ ca kṛtvādhīyīta, anadhyāyāśravaṇāt //
children.translated_text: Therefore, having held three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath controls), having consumed ghee, and having performed <s>upasadana</s> (respectful approach to the teacher), one should study, since no non-study (<s>anadhyāya</s>) is mentioned.
And likewise for studying near a cremation ground; and likewise for studying near a cremation ground. (Gaut. 1.66)

children.text:
āpastambena sarvataḥśamyāprāsānnādhīyītetyuktam /
tasmāttatsamīpe 'dhyayanaṃ śmaśānādhyayanam /
abhyupasargo buddhipūrvasūcanārthaḥ /
tato 'buddhipūrve anyatprāyaścittaṃ laghutaraṃ draṣṭavyam /
tathā cāhośanā- 'anabhisandhyā śmaśānābhyadhyayane 'dhīhi bho ityuktvādhīyīta'; iti /
cakārādanantaroktasya praṇāyāmādeḥ sarvasya prāptau evaṃśabdena anantaroktasyopasadanasyaiva prāptiḥ kriyate /
tarhyevaṃśabda eva vaktavya iti cet na, ubhayasakāśa evāyamartho labhyate /
kathaṃ ? evaṃśabde caśabde vā vaktavye ubhayapāṭhasya prayojanāntaraṃ kalpayituṃ nyāyyaṃ, na hyekasyaiveti /
ata upasadanameva kartavyam /
tathāca smṛtyantaraṃ-'śmaśānasamīpe 'dhītya prāṇān dhārayet prāṇopasparśanamabhivādanaṃ sāvitryanuvācanaṃ'; ityādi /
dviruktiradhyāyaparisamāptyarthā /
uktamidaṃ sarvaṃ prāyaścittaṃ śiṣyasyaiva, tadarthatvādadhyanaprabhṛteḥ /
kiñca-sarvatra sopasadanameva prāyaścittaṃ, upasadanaṃ tvabhivādanādi, tadabhivādanamācāryasya
children.translated_text: <s>Āpastamba</s> has stated: 'One should not study within the range of a <s>śamyā</s>-throw.' Therefore, studying near that [cremation ground] is called <s>śmaśānādhyayana</s> (study near a cremation ground). The prefix 'abhi' is for the purpose of indicating intentional [study]. Therefore, for unintentional [cases], a lighter expiation should be recognized. And thus <s>Ahośanā</s> states: 'For unintentional study near a cremation ground, having said "Recite, Sir," one should study.' By the word 'ca' (and), when all the previously mentioned <s>prāṇāyāma</s> and the rest would be applicable, the word 'evam' (likewise) restricts the applicability to only the <s>upasadana</s> (respectful approach) mentioned immediately before. If one objects that only the word 'evam' should have been stated, [we reply] no, for this meaning is obtained from both [words] together. How so? When either 'evam' or 'ca' could have been stated, it is proper to conceive a separate purpose for the reading of both, since a single [word] alone [cannot serve both purposes]. Therefore, only <s>upasadana</s> (respectful approach) is to be performed. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> states: 'Having studied near a cremation ground, one should hold the breaths; touching water, salutation, and recitation of the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [should be performed],' and so forth. The repetition [of the sūtra] is for the purpose of concluding the chapter on non-study days. All this expiation that has been stated is for the student alone, since study and the rest are for his sake. Moreover, the expiation everywhere includes <s>upasadana</s> (respectful approach), and <s>upasadana</s> means salutation and the like; but that salutation
is not possible [to be performed by] the teacher.
Thus ends the first chapter in <s>Maskarī's</s> commentary on the <s>Gautama</s> [Dharmasūtra].
Second Chapter

children.text:
dvijānāmuktamupanayanam /
teṣāmupanayanātprāgapi kaiścidvarṇadharmairadhikāra iṣyata iti tadarthamāha-
children.translated_text: The <s>upanayana</s> (sacred thread initiation) of the twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) has been described. Even before their <s>upanayana</s>, eligibility for certain duties of one's <s>varṇa</s> (social class) is accepted by some. To address that, he states:
Before <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), there is freedom of conduct, speech, and eating. (Gaut. 2.1)

children.text: nanu ca prāgevopanayanādetadvaktavyaṃ, tatra prāgupanayanādityetanna vaktavyaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: Now, this should have been stated earlier, before the <s>upanayana</s> itself; in that case, the phrase 'before <s>upanayana</s>' would not need to be stated.

children.text:
ucyate-satyametat /
kintu upanayanasyādāvabhidhāne prayojanamuktam /
nānena vidhīyate, arthaprāptatvāt /
na ca niyamyate, avaśyakartavyābhāvāt, 'upanayanādirniyamaḥ'; iti vakṣyamāṇatvāt pākṣikatvābhāvācca /
children.translated_text: Nor is it a restrictive rule (<s>niyama</s>), because there is no obligatory duty [to violate], and because it will be stated later that 'restriction begins from <s>upanayana</s>,' and because there is no optionality [to restrict].
Nor is it an exclusive enumeration (<s>parisaṅkhyā</s>), because there is nothing to be excluded.
For absence of freedom of conduct and the like has not been established for him [the uninitiated child].

children.text: ataḥ idaṃ sūtramanuvādakaṃ prāyaścittarājadaṇḍābhāvajñāpanārthaṃ, tayoḥ sāmānyenopadiśṭatvāt //
children.translated_text: Therefore, this sūtra is a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>), for the purpose of indicating the absence of expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) and royal punishment (<s>rājadaṇḍa</s>), since both of these have been taught in general terms.

It is replied: This is true. However, the purpose of mentioning <s>upanayana</s> at the beginning has been stated. This [sūtra] does not enjoin [anything new], since it is already established by the nature of things.

children.text:
nanu ca rājadaṇḍaprāyaścittāni ca vihitākaraṇe niṣiddhasevane vā vidhīyante /
na cāsya vidhipratiṣedhābhyāmadhikāraḥ /

children.translated_text: This [child] has no eligibility through injunctions or prohibitions.

children.text: na cāsya vidhiḥ pratiṣedho vā śrūyata iti /
children.translated_text: And no injunction or prohibition is heard [in scripture] regarding him.

children.text: na tvasyāhutāttvādi vidhāyiṣyate pratiṣidhyate vā, yadvyatikrame ubhayaṃ bhaviṣyatīti, pitrādīnāmupadeśāt /
children.translated_text: However, [certain acts] such as offering into the fire will be enjoined or prohibited for him, the transgression of which would result in both [punishment and expiation] — this is because of the instruction [being directed] to the father and others.
Therefore, this sūtra is purposeless — [so one might argue].

Now, royal punishment and expiation are prescribed either for failing to perform what is enjoined or for engaging in what is prohibited. And this [uninitiated child] has no eligibility through either injunctions or prohibitions.

children.text: atrocyate-yadvihitākaraṇe pratipiddhasevane vā prāyaścittamuktaṃ rājadaṇḍo vā tadubhayamasyāpi prāpnotyeva /
children.translated_text: To this it is replied: The expiation or royal punishment that has been stated for failing to perform what is enjoined or for engaging in what is prohibited — both of these apply to him as well.

children.text: yadyapyasyaivoddeśena vidhiḥ pratiṣedho vā na śrūyate, tathāpi yattu sāmānyenoktaṃ 'ahiṃsā satyamasteyam'; ityādi, tdavarṇadharmatvādasyāpi prāpnoti /
children.translated_text: Even though no injunction or prohibition is heard specifically with reference to him, nevertheless what has been stated in general terms — '<s>ahiṃsā</s> (non-violence), <s>satya</s> (truthfulness), <s>asteya</s> (non-stealing)' and so forth — that applies to him too, being duties common to all <s>varṇas</s> (social classes).
Upon transgression of those, both royal punishment and expiation do apply.
Therefore, this sūtra, which is in the form of a restatement, has been commenced for the purpose of negating those [punishments].

children.text:
'upanayanādirniyamaḥ'; ityanena sūtreṇa upanayanādārabhya yo vidhirucyate-tadvyatikrame eva prāyaścittaṃ nānyavyatikrame iti vakṣyamāṇatvāt /
tenaivāsyāpi varṇadhramātikrame prāyaścittābhāvo jñātuṃ śakyate, rājadaṇḍābhāvo 'pi /
tathāpi nityopanayanakālātītasya bhinnabuddheḥ śaktasya ekādaśavarṣādūrdhvaṃ ṣoḍaśavarṣātprāk prāyaścittārdhapraveśanārthaṃ, tator'vāk pañcavarṣādūrdhvaṃ pitrādīnāṃ prāyaścittapraveśārthaṃ, tata arvāgaparādhābhāvajñāpanārthaṃ ca sūtramārabdham /
tathāca bhārgavīyaṃ-
children.translated_text: By the sūtra 'restriction begins from <s>upanayana</s>,' it will be stated that expiation applies only for transgression of what is enjoined beginning from <s>upanayana</s>, not for other transgressions. From that alone, the absence of expiation for his transgression of <s>varṇa</s>-duties (class duties) can be understood, and also the absence of royal punishment. Nevertheless, for one whose prescribed time for <s>upanayana</s> has passed, who is of discerning intellect and capable, from after eleven years up to before sixteen years, [this sūtra is commenced] for the purpose of partial application of expiation; for the period after that but before five years, for the purpose of applying expiation to the father and others; and for the period before that, for the purpose of indicating the absence of offense. And thus the <s>Bhārgavīya</s> states:
One who is eighty years old, or a child under sixteen,
women, and the sick — these deserve half the expiation.
For a child under eleven years but over five years,
a kinsman or <s>guru</s> (elder/teacher) should perform the expiation for purification.
For one younger than that, there is no offense whatsoever.
Therefore, neither royal punishment nor expiation is prescribed for such a one.
Thus.

children.text: evaṃ copanayanātprāgyadyapi sāmānyena kāmacāritvādyuktaṃ, tathāpi pañcavarṣātprāgevātyantakāmacāritā, tata ūrdhvaṃ varṇadharmeṣu niyoktavyaḥ pitrādibhiḥ, tadvyatikrame bālasya sataḥ pitrādīnāṃ prāyaścittasya śravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: And thus, although freedom of conduct and the like before <s>upanayana</s> has been stated in general terms, nevertheless, complete freedom of conduct applies only before five years of age; after that, [the child] should be directed by the father and others in the duties of his <s>varṇa</s> (social class), since expiation for the father and others is heard [as prescribed] when the child transgresses those [duties].
Enough of this extended discussion.

children.text:
idānīṃ sūtraṃ vivriyate-upanayanātprākkāmacāra icchāgatiḥ tasmāccaṇḍālasparśanādau prokṣaṇamātraṃ vakṣyati 'avokṣaṇebhyaḥ'; iti tadapi pañcavarṣātprāgevetyuktam /
ata ūrdhvaṃ caṇḍālādisparśane snāpayitavyaḥ /
ekādaśavarṣādūrdhvaṃ svayameva snāyāt /
evaṃ sarvatra /
kāmavādaḥ aślīlādyapi vadati /
kāmapakṣaḥ paryuṣitādyapi bhakṣayati /
pañcavarṣādūrdhvaṃ varṇadharmāvirodhīni kārayitavyāni /
upanayanātprāgityāpatkalpopanayanasyāpi grahaṇam /
kutaḥ ? brahmacārīti liṅgāt /
nityakālātprāk brahmacaryasya skhalanāsambhavādeva siddhatvāt brahmacaryarakṣaṇopadeśo 'narthakaḥsyāditi /
kāmacārasyodāharaṇaṃ svayameva vakṣyati 'yathopapādamūtrapurīṣo bhavati'; iti /
children.translated_text: Now the sūtra is explained: Before <s>upanayana</s>, <s>kāmacāra</s> (freedom of conduct) means movement according to one's wish; therefore, for touching a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> and the like, he will prescribe mere sprinkling, as stated in 'except for wiping, washing, and sprinkling' — and that too applies only before five years, as has been stated. After that, upon touching a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> and the like, [the child] should be bathed. After eleven years, he should bathe himself. Thus in all cases. <s>Kāmavāda</s> (freedom of speech) means he may speak even improper words and the like. <s>Kāmabhakṣa</s> (freedom of eating) means he may eat even stale food and the like. After five years, he should be made to do things not contrary to <s>varṇa</s>-duties (class duties). The phrase 'before <s>upanayana</s>' also includes the emergency <s>upanayana</s> (<s>āpatkalpopanayana</s>). How so? Because of the marker '<s>brahmacārī</s>' (Vedic student). Since, before the prescribed time, there is no possibility of lapsing from <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), the instruction to preserve <s>brahmacarya</s> would be purposeless. He himself will give an example of freedom of conduct: 'He relieves himself of urine and feces as circumstances allow.' Thus.
Therefore, even in the stage of extreme infancy, [the child] should be carefully prevented from [committing sins like] <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brahmin) and the like.

children.text: kāmavāde abhiśaṃsādau kāmabhakṣaṇe surāpānādau cātyantavālyāvasthāyāmapi yatnato nivārayitavya-, kāmacāra ityanenaiva siddhe vādabhakṣaṇayoḥ punarupanyāsāt /
children.translated_text: Regarding freedom of speech, in cases of false accusation and the like, and regarding freedom of eating, in cases of drinking liquor and the like, even in the stage of extreme infancy, [the child] should be carefully prevented — since the separate mention of speech and eating, when already established by 'freedom of conduct' alone, [indicates the gravity of these offenses].

children.text: upanayanāditi vaktavye prāggrahaṇaṃ niyamārthaṃ, upanayanātprāgeva kāmacāritvādīti /
children.translated_text: When 'from <s>upanayana</s>' could have been stated [alone], the word 'before' (<s>prāk</s>) is used for the purpose of restriction — meaning freedom of conduct and the like applies only before <s>upanayana</s>.

children.text: asati niyame 'uttareṣāṃ caitadavirodhi'; ityanena hutaśiṣṭabhakṣaṇavarjanādi yatīnāmapi prāpnotīti //
children.translated_text: Without such restriction, [the rule] 'and this is not contradictory for those in later stages [of life]' would make eating only the remnants of offerings and similar [rules] applicable even to <s>yatis</s> (ascetics).
Now he states an exception to freedom of speech and eating:
The <s>brahmacārī</s> (Vedic student) [should eat only] from what has not been offered [into the fire]. (Gaut. 2.2)

children.text: hutaṃ hutaśiṣṭaṃ carupuroḍāśādi, na vaiśvadevaśiṣṭaṃ, tasya sarvārthatvāt /

children.translated_text: And thus <s>Āpastamba</s> states: 'One should make all persons share in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [offering].'
The word 'should eat' is to be supplied after 'from what has not been offered.'
This prohibition of what is already established [by inference] constitutes instruction for the father and others, since the child lacks discernment.
After eleven years, it is [instruction] for him alone, as stated.

<s>Huta</s> (what has been offered) means the remnants of oblations such as <s>caru</s> (rice porridge) and <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake), but not the remnants of <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (the offering to all gods), since that [offering] serves all purposes.
<s>Brahmacārī</s> (the Vedic student) — (Gaut. 2.3)
Preservation of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) is to be practiced.
Now he gives an example of freedom of conduct:
He relieves himself of urine and feces as circumstances allow. (Gaut. 2.4)

children.text: yathāpariveṣṭitaśirasaḥ kṛṣṭādāvapi mūtrapurīṣāvutpadyete tiṣṭhato vā tathā tatraiva kuryādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: The meaning is: just as for one whose head is covered, urine and feces arise even while plowing and the like, or while standing, so he may do it right there [without restriction].
Moreover:
There is no rule of <s>ācamana</s> (sipping water for purification) for him. (Gaut. 2.5)
From the negation of the 'rule,' it is understood that mere <s>ācamana</s> (sipping water) does exist [as a practice].

children.text: tatra 'śūdreṇa hi samastāvadyāvadvedena jāyate'; iti smṛtyantare śūdreṇa tulyadharmaśravaṇādācamanaṃ śūdravaddraṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: In this regard, since another <s>smṛti</s> states 'for he is equal to a <s>Śūdra</s> until he is born through the <s>Veda</s>,' and since equal dharmic status with a <s>Śūdra</s> is heard, the <s>ācamana</s> (sipping) should be understood as being like that of a <s>Śūdra</s>.

children.text: ūnaikādaśavarṣasyeti kutaḥ ? asyetyārambhāt, pañcavarṣatprāgdoṣābhāvaśravaṇāt ekādaśavarṣādūrdhvaṃ varṇadharme 'dhikṛtatvācca /
children.translated_text: Whence [the specification] 'for one under eleven years'? From the beginning with the word 'his' (<s>asya</s>), from the hearing that there is no fault before five years, and from the fact that after eleven years one is eligible for <s>varṇa</s>-duties (class duties).
It is understood that after eleven years, the rule of <s>ācamana</s> (ceremonial sipping) also exists for him.
After five years and before eleven years, there is no <s>ācamana</s>-rule — no injunction of <s>ācamana</s> (ceremonial sipping of water) — for him.
Now he states [the rule] for one who is very young:
Except for wiping, washing, and sprinkling. (Gaut. 2.6)

children.text:
asya na vidyata iti vartate /
asyonapañcavarṣasyāpamārjanādibhyaḥ anyatra kiñcidapi śaucaprakāraḥ na vidyata ityarthaḥ /
apamārjanaṃ bhuktocchiṣṭasya sodakena pāṇinā taducchiṣṭāpanayanam /
pradhābanaṃ prakṣālanaṃ mūtroccārādau /

children.translated_text: Sprinkling (<s>avokṣaṇa</s>) means sprinkling with water upon touching a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> and the like.
Since [purification rules] would not apply [to the very young], [one might argue that] the two negations in 'there is no rule of <s>ācamana</s> for him'

children.text: anyatrāpamārjanapradhāvanāvokṣaṇebhyaḥ'; iti pratiṣedhadvayasyānārambhaḥ prāpnotīti cet, naiṣa doṣaḥ, 'nāsyācamanakalpo dyitate'; ityanenonaṣoḍaśavarṣasyācamanakalpo vidhīyate ūnaikādaśavarṣasya pratiṣedhadvāreṇa /
children.translated_text: and 'except for wiping, washing, and sprinkling' need not have been commenced. If one objects thus, [we reply:] this is no fault. By the statement 'there is no rule of <s>ācamana</s> for him,' the <s>ācamana</s>-rule is enjoined for one under sixteen years through the negation [applicable to one] under eleven years.
And by 'except for wiping, washing, and sprinkling,' again, wiping and the like are enjoined for one under five years through the negation of other purification [methods].

The phrase 'does not exist for him' continues [from the previous sūtra]. For this [child] under five years, apart from wiping and the like, no other mode of purification exists — this is the meaning. Wiping (<s>apamārjana</s>) means removing food remnants from [the child's] mouth with a wet hand. Washing (<s>pradhāvana</s>) means cleansing after urination or defecation.
Moreover:
There is no impurity from touching him. (Gaut. 2.7)
By the word 'him' (<s>tad</s>), one who has not performed purification is referred to.
From touching one who has not performed purification, or from being touched by him, impurity does not arise.
This applies only to a very young child.

children.text: tarhyasya śaucavidhānamanarthakaṃ, kutaḥ ? dvayameva prayojanaṃ śaucavidhānasya dṛśyate itarasparśayogyārthamanuṣṭhānārthaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Then the prescription of purification for him would be purposeless. Why? Because only two purposes are seen for the prescription of purification: for the purpose of being fit to touch others, and for the purpose of [ritual] performance.

children.text: asya tu itarasparśayogyārthaṃ na bhavati, akṛtaśaucasyāpi sparśayogyatvāt /
children.translated_text: For him, the purpose of being fit to touch others does not apply, since even without purification he is fit to be touched,
as stated by 'there is no impurity from touching him.'
And the purpose of [ritual] performance also does not apply, since he has no [ritual] performances [to carry out].
[We reply:] It is not purposeless, because the prescription of purification is for the purpose of protection.
And thus another <s>smṛti</s> states: 'For a child up to five years of age, purification should be performed for the purpose of protection.'

children.text:
akṛtaśaucasyāsyaiva sparśane doṣābhāvajñāpanārthaḥ upaśabdaprayogaḥ /
evaṃ cānyeṣāmucchiṣṭakṛta mūtrapurīṣāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: The use of the prefix 'upa' [in <s>upasparśana</s>] is for the purpose of indicating the absence of fault in touching only this [child] who has not performed purification. And thus, [when touching] the food-remnants, urine, or feces produced by others,

children.text:
sparśane ācamanaṃ kartavyam /
tatsparśane na doṣaḥ śavaspṛṣṭisūtre parigaṇitatvāt /
tathā smṛtyantaraṃ-
children.translated_text: <s>ācamana</s> (ceremonial sipping) should be performed. In touching those [substances of the child], there is no fault, since [the child] is enumerated in the sūtra on touching a corpse. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> states:

children.text: aśuciṃ spṛśate yastu eka eva hi duṣyate /
children.translated_text: He who touches an impure person — he alone becomes impure.

children.text: taṃ spṛṣṭvānyo na duṣyeta sarvadravyeṣvayaṃ vidhiḥ //
children.translated_text: Another who touches him [the one who touched the impure person] does not become impure — this is the rule regarding all substances.
Thus.
But regarding touching a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, he will state [the rule] in the sūtra on touching a corpse.

children.text: 'tamupaspṛśet'; iti vaktavye 'na tadupasparśanādaśaucam'; iti gurasūtrakaraṇaṃ prāgupanayanādityatra niyamamyāpi bādhanārtham /
children.translated_text: Instead of saying 'one should touch him [without fault],' the elaborate sūtra formulation 'there is no impurity from touching him' is for the purpose of overriding the restriction in 'before <s>upanayana</s>' as well.
Therefore, even after <s>upanayana</s>, <s>ācamana</s> (ceremonial sipping) should be performed upon touching food-remnants, urine, or feces [of any person].
Moreover:
However, one should not employ him in fire-offering or receiving of <s>bali</s> (food-offerings). (Gaut. 2.8)

children.text:
enamiti sarvasyānupanītasyopasaṅgrahārtham /
agnau yatkriyate agnihotrahomādi tat agnihavanam /
vaiśvadevottarakālaṃ digdevatābhyo yo balirdīryate tadbaliharaṇam /
tuśabdo viśeṣavācī, aṣṭakādau brāhmaṇapādaprakṣālanādāvapi na niyuñjyāt, viśeṣato 'gnihavanabaliharaṇayoriti /
kāmacāritvādyatrakutracinmantramadhītyāgnihotrādau yadi svayameva pravartate tadā taṃ dṛṣṭvānumantāpi na syādityevamartha evaśabdaḥ /
upanītasya niyogārthamidaṃ vacanaṃ, anyatra prāptyabhāvātpratiniṣedhasya /
evaṃ ca 'vidvānāgnihotraṃ juhuyāt'; iti yadyapi śrutyā bahuśrutasyaivādhikāraḥ, tathāpi tadasambhave alpavidyamapyupanītaṃ niyuñjyāt /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text:
The word '<s>enam</s>' (this one) is for including any uninitiated person.
'<s>Agnihavana</s>' (offering into fire) is what is performed in the fire, such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> oblation and the like.
'<s>Baliharaṇa</s>' (offering of <s>bali</s>) is the <s>bali</s> offered to the directional deities after the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>.
The word '<s>tu</s>' is a specifier; at the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> and other [rites], the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>—

children.text: naiva kanyā na yuvatirnālpavidyo na bāliśaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Neither a girl, nor a young woman, nor one of little learning, nor a fool,"
"Should be the <s>hotṛ</s> (offerer) of the <s>Agnihotra</s>; nor one who is afflicted, nor one who is unconsecrated."

children.text:
tatrālpavidyapratiṣedhādeva pratiṣedhe siddhe nāsaṃskṛta iti pratiṣedho 'nyasya viduṣo 'bhāvelpavidyasyāpi saṃskṛtasyābhyanujñānārthamiti pratipāditam /
prāgupanayanādityādi yaduktaṃ tatstrīṇāmapi avivāhāddraṣṭavyam /
kutaḥ ? 'vaivāhiko vidhiḥ strīṇāmaupanāyanikaḥ smṛtaḥ'; iti smṛtyantaradarśanāt /
evaṃ cāgnihavanabalirharaṇayoḥ kanyāyā api niyogapratiṣedhaḥ siddhaḥ /

children.translated_text: Therefore the commission should be made after the time of marriage.

children.text: tatra 'na strī juhuyāt'; iti śrutyāgnihotre pratiṣiddhatvāt aupāsanādau draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Since the <s>śruti</s> 'a woman should not offer' prohibits [women] in the <s>Agnihotra</s>, it should be applied to the <s>Aupāsana</s> (domestic fire) and the rest.

children.text: tathā ca smṛtyantaraṃ-'patnyaupāsanaṃ juhuyādvaiśvadevaṃ ca'; ityādi /
children.translated_text: And another <s>smṛti</s> says: 'The wife should offer in the <s>Aupāsana</s> and the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>,' and so forth.
The prohibition 'nor a young woman' is not a fault, since it pertains to another's wife.

Since the prohibition of one of little learning itself already establishes the prohibition, the [separate] prohibition 'nor one who is unconsecrated' is for the purpose of permitting even one of little learning who is consecrated, in the absence of another learned person—this has been established.
What was stated beginning with 'before <s>upanayana</s>' applies to women as well, since they have no—
Moreover—
"He should not utter the <s>Brahman</s> (Veda) except at the offering of <s>svadhā</s> [to the ancestors]."

children.text:
evamityanuvartate /
brahmaśabdena vedā ucyante /
tasmādenaṃ nādhyāpayet /
upanītasyopākaraṇādūrdhvaṃ 'adhīyīta chandāṃsi'; ityanena vedādhyayanavidhānādevānupanītasya pratiṣedhe siddhe vedasya punaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ veda eva nādhyāpayitavyaḥ iti niyamārthaḥ tataścāṅgādhyāpane na doṣaḥ /
kāmacāritvādyenakenacitprakāreṇa gṛhātaṃ mantramapi noccārayet /
kutaḥ ? adhyāpayayedityanārabhyābhivyāhārayedityārambhāt /
anyatra svadhāninayanāt, svadhāninayanaṃ varjayitvā /
amuṣmai svadhetyuktvā yatpiṇḍodakādi pretebhyo dīyate tatsvadhāninayanam /
tadapi pretakarmaṇaḥ samastasyāpyupalakṣaṇam /
tathāca vasiṣṭhaḥ-'anyatrodakakarmasvadhāṣitṛsaṃyuktebhyaḥ'; iti /
evaṃca putre 'nupanīte 'pi
children.translated_text: '<s>Evam</s>' (thus) continues from the previous [rule]. By the word '<s>Brahma</s>' the <s>Vedas</s> are meant. Therefore one should not teach him [the uninitiated]. Since for the initiated person, the injunction of Vedic study through '<s>adhīyīta chandāṃsi</s>' (he should study the Vedic texts) [applies] after the <s>upākaraṇa</s> (commencement ceremony), and since the prohibition for the uninitiated is already established by that—the separate prohibition regarding the <s>Veda</s> again—

children.text: sati sapiṇḍādibhiḥ pretakriyā na kartavyā, śāstracodanānarthakyaprasaṅgo mā bhūditi //
children.translated_text: —[is] so that, when [the uninitiated person dies], the funeral rites need not be performed by <s>sapiṇḍas</s> and others, lest there be the unwanted consequence of the <s>śāstra</s>'s injunction being purposeless.
Having spoken about the uninitiated, now [the author] speaks about the initiated—
"The observance (<s>niyama</s>) begins from <s>upanayana</s>."

children.text: upanayanādārabhya yo vidhiruktaḥ sa niyamasaṃjño bhavati /
children.translated_text: The rule that has been stated beginning from <s>upanayana</s> is called '<s>niyama</s>' (observance).
Thus, for its non-performance there is expiation—not for the previous [rules].

children.text: ato vā ārabhya niyamaḥ vratadhāraṇaṃ yo vakṣyate 'gnīndhanādiḥ sa niyamaḥ upanayanādiḥ kartavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Or, the <s>niyama</s> (observance) beginning from that [<s>upanayana</s>], which is the observance of vows to be stated—fire-kindling and the rest—is the <s>niyama</s> that should be performed beginning from <s>upanayana</s>.
Moreover—
"<s>Brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) has been stated."
The word 'stated' [means:] the <s>niyama</s> before <s>upanayana</s> is exactly this.
And therefore, in case of its violation, the entitlement even of the uninitiated should be seen as being through the expiation of the <s>avakīrṇin</s> (one who has broken celibacy) alone.

children.text: tathāca smṛtyantaraṃ-'viplutamavakīrṇivratena śuddhamupanayedūnasaptadaśavarṣaṃ, ata ūrdhvaṃ brātyāvakīrṇivratābhyām'; iti /
children.translated_text: And another <s>smṛti</s> [says]: 'One who has lapsed should be purified with the <s>avakīrṇin</s> vow and then initiated, if under seventeen years; beyond that, with both the <s>vrātya</s> and <s>avakīrṇin</s> vows.'

children.text: brahmacāriṇastu strīprekṣaṇādipratiṣedhādarthasiddhamiti cet, na, paśvādaṣvapi sambhavāt //
children.translated_text: If it is said that this is already established by the prohibition of looking at women and the rest for the <s>brahmacārin</s>—no, because it is possible even with animals and the like.
Moreover—
"Fire-kindling and begging for alms."

children.text:
agnīndhanaṃ samiddhomaḥ /
itaratprasiddham /
te pratidinaṃ kartavye /
sahanirdeśo 'nantarānuṣṭhānārthaḥ /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Agnīndhana</s> (fire-kindling) means the <s>samidh</s>-oblation (offering of fuel sticks). The other [begging] is well known. Both should be performed daily. The joint mention is for the purpose of performing them in immediate succession. Thus <s>Manu</s> [says]:
"Having taken up the desired staff and having worshipped the sun,"
"Having circumambulated the fire, let him go begging for alms according to rule."

children.text:
tatrāpi pradakṣiṇaṃ parītyāgnimityanena samiddhoma ukta ityuktam /
'sāyaṃ prātastvannamabhaipūjitamanindan bhuñjīta'; iti dvirbhojanaśravaṇāt sāyaṃ prātaḥ dviragnīndhanamapi draṣṭavyam /
tathā ca smṛtyantaram-
children.translated_text: In that [verse] too, by 'having circumambulated the fire' the <s>samidh</s>-oblation is indicated—so it has been said. Since the <s>śruti</s> says 'he should eat twice, in the evening and morning, food that is not begged, not criticized'—since eating twice is heard, fire-kindling too should be understood as twice, in the evening and morning. And another <s>smṛti</s>—
"Having brought fuel sticks from afar, he should place them in the open air;"
"And he should offer with them in the fire, evening and morning, unwearied."
Some desire the <s>samidh</s>-oblation in the evening only.
Moreover—
"Truthful speech."

children.text:
sarvatra kartavyakriyādhyāhartavyā /
vacanagrahaṇamasaṃdehārthaṃ, satyamapāmupasparśanamityevaṃ saṃdehaḥ syāditi /
pṛthaggrahaṇaṃ āturasyāpyanuṣṭhānārtham /
tataśca pūrvayostanna /
tathācaca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: The word 'should be performed' is to be supplied everywhere. The mention of 'speech' is to remove doubt—lest there be confusion with '<s>satyam</s> (truth) is the touching of water.' The separate mention is for performance even by one who is ill. Therefore, for the previous two [rules], this does not [apply when ill]. Thus <s>Manu</s> [says]:
"Without having gone begging and without having kindled the fire,"
"One who is not ill should perform the <s>avakīrṇin</s> vow for seven nights."
Moreover—
"Touching of water."
The word '<s>ap</s>' (water) is a synecdoche for ashes and the rest. Thus <s>Bhṛgu</s> [says]:
"Five kinds of purificatory baths have been declared by the great sages:"

children.text: āgneyaṃ vāruṇaṃ vrāhyaṃ vāyavyaṃ divyameva ca //
children.translated_text: "Of fire, of water, of <s>Brahman</s>, of wind, and of heaven."
"The fire-bath is bathing with ashes; the water-bath is immersion;"

children.text: āpo hiṣṭheti ca brāhmaṃ vāyavyaṃ gorajaḥ smṛtam //
children.translated_text: "The <s>Brahma</s>-bath is [with the hymn] '<s>āpo hiṣṭhā</s>'; the wind-bath is [with] cow-dust;"

children.text: yattu syātsātapaṃ varṣaṃ divyaṃ snānaṃ taducyate /
children.translated_text: "Rain falling while the sun shines is called the divine bath;"
"One unable to take a water-bath should practice the fire-bath and the others."

children.text:
snānamiti vaktavye evamabhidhānaṃ smṛtyantaroktasnānavidherupasaṅgrahaṇārtham /
evaṃ ca smṛtyantaroktaṃ draṣṭavyam /
upaśabdo 'vijñātajalavarjanārthaḥ /
agnīndhanabhaikṣacaraṇayoḥ pṛthaggrahaṇaṃ bhuktasya nityasnānapratiṣedhārthaṃ, na naimittikasya /
ato naimittikaṃ kartavyam /
satyavacanasya pṛthaggrahaṇamāturasya naimittikasyāpi pratiṣedhārtham /
children.translated_text: Where one should have said 'bath,' this [indirect] expression is for including the bathing rules stated in other <s>smṛtis</s>. Thus what is stated in other <s>smṛtis</s> should be considered. The prefix '<s>upa</s>' (near) is for avoiding unknown waters. The separate mention of fire-kindling and begging is [because] after eating—

children.text:
upaśabdor'dharātrasnānapratiṣedhārthaṃ iti kecidvadanti /
yaduktamatra tatsarvaṃ manunanāpyuktaṃ-
children.translated_text: Some say the prefix '<s>upa</s>' is for prohibiting midnight bathing. What is stated here is all also stated by <s>Manu</s>—
"One should not bathe after eating, nor when ill, nor at midnight,"
"Nor always with garments on, nor in an unknown body of water."
"Some [prescribe] the <s>Godāna</s> (shaving ceremony) and the rest."

children.text:
godānaṃ nāma chandogānāṃ dvitīyaṃ vrataṃ anyeṣāmapi ṣoḍaśe varṣe dhārayitavyam /
teṣāmapi ṣoḍaśe godānadhāraṇaṃ kecidicchacanti /

children.translated_text: From that time onward, some desire bathing [as a regular practice].

children.text: godānāt prāk nityasnānaṃ na kuryāt, naimittikameva kartavyam /
children.translated_text: Before the <s>Godāna</s>, one should not perform the daily bath; only the occasional bath should be performed.
From that time onward, some teachers desire the daily bath as well.

children.text: eka iti vacanāt na tu gautamaḥ //
children.translated_text: From the word 'some' [it is understood that] <s>Gautama</s> does not [prescribe this].

The <s>Godāna</s> is the second vow of the <s>Chandogas</s> (Sāmavedins); for others too it is to be observed in the sixteenth year. Some desire that they too should observe the <s>Godāna</s> in the sixteenth year.
"And [that one should perform] the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship) outside [the village]."

children.text:
ekegrahaṇānuvartanārthaścacakāraḥ /
vahirgrābhātsandhyopāsanameke icchanti /
na tu gautamaḥ /
na tu gautamaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>ca</s>' (and) continues the word 'some.' Some desire that the <s>sandhyā</s> worship should be outside the village. But <s>Gautama</s> does not.

children.text: etaduktaṃ bhavati-grāmādbahireva sandhyopāsanaṃ kartavyamityekeṣāṃ mataṃ, bahirabhyantare vā yatra kutra cicchuddhadeśe kartavyamiti gautamamatam //
children.translated_text: This is what is said: the view of some is that the <s>sandhyā</s> worship should be performed only outside the village; <s>Gautama</s>'s view is that it should be performed in any clean place, whether outside or inside.

children.text: idānīṃ prasaṅgāt tat sandhyopāsanaṃ kadā kathaṃ ca kartavyamityata āha-
children.translated_text: Now, incidentally, when and how should this <s>sandhyā</s> worship be performed? Therefore [the author] says—
"One should stand [for] the morning [<s>sandhyā</s>] and sit [for] the evening one, with the star-light, until the seeing of the [next] light, observing silence."

children.text:
vāgyata iti sthānāsanayoḥ pratyekaṃ sambadhyate /
yasyāmāditya udeti sā pūrvā sandhyā /
pūrvasūtrakhaṇḍāt sandhyāśabdo 'nuvartate /
yasyāmādityo 'stameti sottarā sandhyā /
sthānāsane atra guṇabhūte /
upāsanamatra pradhānaṃ karma /
ato yadyapi tiṣṭhedityuktaṃ, tathāpi tiṣṭhannupāsīta, āsīna upāsīteti draṣṭavyam /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Observing silence' is construed with both standing and sitting separately. The <s>sandhyā</s> during which the sun rises is the morning <s>sandhyā</s>. The word '<s>sandhyā</s>' continues from the previous section of the <s>sūtra</s>. The <s>sandhyā</s> during which the sun sets is the evening <s>sandhyā</s>. Standing and sitting are here secondary—
"By reciting [the <s>Gāyatrī</s>] while standing at the morning <s>sandhyā</s>, one dispels the sin [committed] at night;"

children.text: paścimāṃ tu samāsīno malaṃ hanti divā kṛtam //
children.translated_text: "By sitting at the evening [<s>sandhyā</s>], one destroys the impurity committed during the day."

children.text:
sajyotiḥ kālaḥ, pūrvasyāṃ nakṣatrajyotiḥ /
yaḥ kālo nakṣatrajyotiṣā saha vartata sa sajyotiḥ tasmin sajyotiṣi kāle ārambhaḥ kartavyaḥ /
itarasyāṃ tathā ādityajyotiḥ /
tata ā jyotiṣo darśanāt-pūrvasyāmādityadarśanāt uttarasyāṃ nakṣatradarśanāt /
ā jyotiṣa iti vaktavye darśanagrahaṇaṃ sampagartham /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: 'With the star-light' is the time: for the morning [<s>sandhyā</s>], the star-light. The time during which the star-light is present is 'with star-light'—at that time with star-light, one should begin. For the other [evening <s>sandhyā</s>], similarly, the sun-light. Then, until the seeing of the [next] light—for the morning—
"The sages, through long <s>sandhyā</s> practice, obtained long life,"

children.text: prajñāṃ yaśaśca kīrtiṃ ca brahmavarcasameva ca //
children.translated_text: "Wisdom, fame, glory, and the luster of <s>Brahman</s>."

children.text: nanu ca 'uttareṣāṃ caitadavirodhi'; ityanena snātakasyāgnimata etanna prāpyate, tasyāgnihavanenāsya kālasyāvaruddhatvāditi /

children.translated_text: We reply: regarding the <s>smārta</s> (domestic) evening and morning oblation, there is no contradiction because of the difference in time.

children.text: kathaṃ ? sāyaṃśabdena rātrirucyate, prātaḥśabdena ca divasaḥ, uditahomādivākyavadatra tathāvidhasyābhāvāt sandhyopāsanānantarameva homasyānupraveśaḥ syāditi /
children.translated_text: How? By the word 'evening' the night is meant, and by 'morning' the day—since there is no statement of the type 'after sunrise offering' here, the oblation should follow immediately after the <s>sandhyā</s> worship.

children.text: athāpi keṣāṃcitsandhyākāla eva homa uktaḥ,tatrāpi dīrghasandhyatvasyābhiṣṭatvāddhomānantaramapi sandhyopāsanasyāvakāśo 'stīti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, for some, the oblation is prescribed at the very time of <s>sandhyā</s>; even there, since the long <s>sandhyā</s> practice is desired, there is scope for <s>sandhyā</s> worship even after the oblation.
Thus, even regarding the <s>Śrauta</s> (Vedic) after-sunrise offering and the rest, there is no contradiction.

But is this not inapplicable to the <s>snātaka</s> (graduate) who has the fire, since 'and for the later [castes] this is not contradictory' [applies]—because his time is occupied by the fire-offering?

children.text: 'tiṣṭhanpūrvāṃ sandhyāmāsīna uttarāmupāsīta'; iti vaktavye evamabhidhānaṃ smṛtyantaroktasyāpi vidhergrahaṇārtham /
children.translated_text: Where one should have said 'one should worship the morning <s>sandhyā</s> standing and the evening sitting,' this [alternate] expression is for including the rules stated in other <s>smṛtis</s>.

children.text: tathā'hośanā-'sāyaṃ prātarudakaṃ gatvā pūto bhūtvā pavitreṇa mārjayitvā āpohiṣṭhīyābhistisṛbhirabliṅgābhiḥ vāmadevyena ca, tataḥ śuco deśe darbheṣvāsīno darbhāndhārayamāṇaḥ pratyaṅmukho vāgyata ātmānaṃ dhyātvā tataḥ sarecakaṣūrakakumbhakādīn trīn prāṇāyāmān dhārayitvā ṛṣicchabdodevatādhyānapūrvakaṃ bhūrbhuvaḥsvarityādikāṃ sāvitrīṃ sahasrakṛtva āvartayecchatakṛtvo vā daśāvarāmathottiṣṭhamnagniyamabrahmabhyaḥ pratyagdakṣiṇodīcyāsu namaskṛtvā triḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā punarapi pratīcīṃ diśaṃ namaskuryāt /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Uśanas</s> [says]: 'Having gone to water in the evening and morning, having become pure, having wiped [himself] with the purifier, [reciting] the three [verses] beginning with "<s>āpo hiṣṭhā</s>" and the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, then in a clean place, seated on <s>darbha</s> grass, holding <s>darbha</s> grass, facing west, observing silence, the self—'
'Similarly in the morning, standing and facing east, one should make salutation to <s>Mitra</s> and the others.'
"One should not gaze at the sun."

children.text:
yadi sandhyākālayorevāyaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ syāt tadānīmekameva sūtraṃ kriyeta 'tiṣṭhetpūrvāmāsītottarāṃ sajyotipyā jyotiṣo darśanādvāgyato nādityamīkṣeta'; iti /
yadi sarvadā syāttadānīṃ 'varjayenmadhumāṃsa'; ityādāvādityekṣaṇamapi
children.translated_text: If this prohibition applied only to the two <s>sandhyā</s> times, then a single <s>sūtra</s> would have been composed: 'one should stand for the morning, sit for the evening, with star-light until seeing the light, observing silence, not gazing at the sun.' If it applied at all times, then '[he should avoid] honey, meat...'—
—'he should recite.'
From the fact that neither [formulation] was adopted, it can be understood that this is stated with a different intention.

children.text: abhiprāyaśca smṛtyantarokto draṣṭavyaḥ yathā cāhośanā-'nekṣetādityaṃ sandhyāgataṃ madhyaṃdinagataṃ rāhugrastaṃ vāristham'; iti //
children.translated_text: And the intention should be seen as stated in another <s>smṛti</s>. Thus <s>Uśanas</s> [says]: 'One should not look at the sun at the <s>sandhyā</s>, at midday, when eclipsed by <s>Rāhu</s>, or reflected in water.'

"One should avoid honey, meat, perfume, garlands, sleeping during the day, anointing [with oil], applying collyrium, riding vehicles, wearing shoes, using an umbrella, lust, anger, greed, delusion, [excessive] talking, playing instruments, bathing [for pleasure], tooth-cleaning [for beautification], elation, dancing, singing, slander, and fear."

children.text:
varjayediti pratyekaṃ sambadhyate /
madhu mākṣikaṃ, tasyābuddhipūrvabhakṣaṇe na doṣaḥ, 'akāmopanataṃ madhu vājasaneyake na duṣyati'; iti smṛtyantaradarśanāt /
māṃsaṃ gṛhasthasya apratiṣiddhamapi /
tatrāpyāturasyauṣadhārthaṃ gurorucchiṣṭasya māṃsasya bhakṣaṇe na doṣaḥ, 'sa cedavyādhīyīta kāmaṃ gurorucchiṣṭaṃ bhaiṣajyārthe sarvaṃ prāśnīyāt'; iti smṛtyantaradarśanāt /
evaṃ cānāturasya śrāddhe 'pi varjanīyam /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Should avoid' is construed with each separately. 'Honey' means bee-honey; in its unintentional consumption there is no fault, since another <s>smṛti</s> states: 'honey that comes unsought, according to the <s>Vājasaneyin</s> [school], is not faulty.' Meat, even though not prohibited for the householder, that—
"As in a vow, at a rite for a deity, at a <s>Pitṛ</s> (ancestor) rite, and as a <s>Ṛṣi</s>-like [act],"
"One may eat when earnestly requested—his vow is not broken."

children.text:
ityādi /
gandhaṃ candanādi /
tasyāpi sukhārthasya pratiṣedhaḥ, na devatāśiṣṭasya, 'devatāśiṣṭameva gṛhṇīyādbrahmacārī'; iti smṛtyantaradarśanāt /
mālāyā api tathaiva /
divāsvapno divā nidrāsevanaṃ, tadapyāturasya na doṣaḥ /
añjanamakṣṇoḥ /
atrāpyupabhogārthasya pratiṣedhaḥ, nauṣadhārthasya /
abhyañjanaṃ tailena gātrābhyaṅgaḥ /
kecidgandhatailasyāyaṃ pratiṣedha iti vadanti /
tasminpakṣe itarasya na doṣaḥ /
gandhapratiśedhenaivāyaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ siddha iti cenna, viśeṣata eva lokaprasiddherna gandhasāmānyasya grahaṇaṃ bhavatīti /
yānaṃ śibikādi /
tadapyanāturasyaiva /
upānacchatre prasiddhe /
mayūrapatrakṛtasyādoṣaḥ /
kāmaḥ strīgato bhogābhilāṣaḥ /
krodhaḥ parasyāniṣṭacintanam /
lobhaḥ anyāyena paradravyādyapaharaṇam /
moho 'jñānam /
vādo bahupralāpaḥ /
vādanaṃ bherītāḍanādi /
snānaṃ śirasnānādi yenopabhogaḥ, vihitatvāditarasya /
dantadhāvanaṃ prasiddham /
tāmbūlapatreṇāpi tanna kartavyaṃ 'paṅkadanto bhavedvratī'; iti smṛtyantaradarśanāt /
harṣaḥ prītiḥ evaṃ ca taddhetūnāṃ nāṭakādīnāṃ prekṣaṇasyāpi pratiṣedhaḥ siddhaḥ, taddarśane prītyutpatteḥ nivārāyetumaśakyatvāt /

children.translated_text: '<s>Nṛtta</s>' (dancing) means moving the limbs [expressively].
'<s>Gīta</s>' (singing) means the utterance of words connected with <s>gāndharva</s> (music).
'<s>Parivāda</s>' (slander) means proclaiming the faults of others.
'<s>Bhaya</s>' (frightening) means terrifying another, since it is impossible for the other person to avoid [the fear]. (End of section.)

And so forth. '<s>gandha</s>' (fragrance) refers to sandalwood and the like. The prohibition is of that which is for pleasure, not of that which is offered to deities, since another <s>smṛti</s> states: 'A <s>brahmacārin</s> should accept only what has been offered to the deities.' The same applies to garlands as well. '<s>Divāsvapna</s>' (daytime sleeping) means indulging in sleep during the day; this is not a fault for one who is ill. '<s>Añjana</s>' (collyrium) is for the eyes. Here too, the prohibition is of that used for enjoyment, not for medicinal purposes. '<s>Abhyañjana</s>' (anointing) means rubbing the body with oil. Some say this is a prohibition of fragrant oil. In that view, the other [non-fragrant oil] is not a fault. If one argues that this prohibition is already established by the prohibition of fragrance, [the response is] no, because due to its specific popular usage, it is not subsumed under the general category of fragrance. '<s>Yāna</s>' (conveyance) refers to palanquins and the like. This too [is prohibited] only for one who is not ill. Shoes and umbrellas are well-known. There is no fault in one made of peacock feathers. '<s>Kāma</s>' (desire) is the longing for enjoyment directed toward women. '<s>Krodha</s>' (anger) is thinking ill of another. '<s>Lobha</s>' (greed) is wrongfully seizing another's property and the like. '<s>Moha</s>' (delusion) is ignorance. '<s>Vāda</s>' (speech) means excessive chatter. '<s>Vādana</s>' (playing instruments) means striking a drum and the like. '<s>Snāna</s>' (bathing) means head-bathing and such that produces enjoyment, since the other kind [ritual bathing] is enjoined. '<s>Dantadhāvana</s>' (teeth-cleaning) is well-known. One should not do it even with a betel leaf, since another <s>smṛti</s> states: 'One observing a vow should have mud-covered teeth.' '<s>Harṣa</s>' (delight) means pleasure; and thus the prohibition of watching plays and the like, which cause it, is also established, since it is impossible to prevent the arising of pleasure upon seeing them.
Moreover—
In the presence of the <s>guru</s>: covering the throat, sitting with one thigh over the other, and stretching the legs [are prohibited]. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.20)

children.text:
gururācāryādi /
kutaḥ ? yadyācāryasyaiva grahaṇaṃ tadānīṃ ācāryadarśana iti vaktavyam /
gurugrahaṇaṃ sarveṣāṃ gurūsthānīyānāmapyupalakṣaṇam /
tathāca smṛtyantaraṃ-'manyānāṃ sarveṣāṃ sakāśe saṃkucitastiṣṭhet'; iti /

children.translated_text: '<s>Kaṇṭhaprāvaraṇa</s>' (covering the throat) means throwing a cloth over the neck.
'<s>Avasakthikā</s>' means tying the girdle-cloth above the knee and thigh.
The rest is well-known.
Since these are done involuntarily, the prohibition [applies to doing them deliberately]. (End of section.)

'<s>Guru</s>' refers to the <s>ācārya</s> and others. Why? If only the <s>ācārya</s> were meant, then it should have said 'in the presence of the <s>ācārya</s>.' The use of '<s>guru</s>' is indicative of all those who hold the position of a <s>guru</s>. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> [states]: 'In the presence of all others [who are venerable], one should stand in a contracted manner.'
Moreover—
Spitting, laughing, yawning, and cracking the joints [are to be avoided]. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.21)
Laughing should be restrained with effort even when it arises involuntarily.

children.text: tathā cāpastambaḥ-'na smayeta yadi smayetāpapṛhya smayeteti brāhmaṇaṃ'; iti /
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Āpastamba</s> [states]: 'One should not smile; if one does smile, one should smile while covering [the mouth]'—thus is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [text].
Yawning is well-known.
'<s>Avasphoṭana</s>' (cracking joints) means cracking the joints with an audible sound. (End of section.)
The separate mention [of these] is for the purpose of prohibiting them in the presence of the <s>guru</s> and in the presence of others as well. Spitting is well-known.
Moreover—
Gazing at and touching a woman when there is suspicion of sexual intent [are to be avoided]. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.22)

children.text:
varjayediti vartate /
prekṣaṇaṃ prakarṣeṇekṣaṇaṃ avayavanirūpaṇaṃ, na rūpamātradarśanaṃ, tasya nimiṣato vārayitumaśakyatvāt /
ālambanaṃ sparśanam /
sparśane iti vaktavye evamabhidhānamabhisandhisparśanavarjanārtham /

children.translated_text: And thus there is no fault in [touching] through inadvertence.
But with intention, one should not touch [a woman] even in darkness and such [situations].
One should not do both [gazing and touching] with respect to a woman.
Only with regard to a woman about whom others would have suspicion of sexual intent—not with regard to any other woman. (End of section.)

'Should avoid' is carried over [from the previous sūtra]. '<s>Prekṣaṇa</s>' (gazing) means looking intently, examining the limbs—not merely seeing the form, since it is impossible to prevent that for one who blinks. '<s>Ālambana</s>' (touching) means physical contact. Although 'touching' could have been stated, the expression is used thus to indicate that intentional touching should be avoided.
Gambling, serving the lowly, taking what is not given, and causing harm [are to be avoided]. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.23)

children.text: evaṃ ca gurorapyanurūpā sevā na kartavyā /
children.translated_text: And thus even for the <s>guru</s>, inappropriate service should not be performed.
'<s>Adattādāna</s>' (taking what is not given) means taking even what has been discarded if it has not been permitted.
'<s>Hiṃsā</s>' (harm) means killing living beings or causing pain to them.
One should not cause [others to do these], nor should one approve of [them being done]. (End of section.)
'Should avoid' is understood. '<s>Dyūta</s>' (gambling) means with dice and the like. '<s>Hīnasevā</s>' (serving the lowly) means service such as cleaning urine and excrement.
Moreover—
The names of the <s>ācārya</s>, his son, his wife, and a <s>dīkṣita</s> (one who has undergone consecration) [are not to be uttered]. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.24)
'Should avoid' is understood from the context.

children.text: ācāryasya tatputrasya ca tadbhāryāyāśca dīkṣitasya ca saṃjñāṃ pitrādikṛtāṃ noccārayet //
children.translated_text: One should not utter the given name—assigned by the father and others—of the <s>ācārya</s>, his son, his wife, or a <s>dīkṣita</s>. (End of section.)
Moreover—
Harsh words [are to be avoided]. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.25)
'<s>Śuktāḥ</s>' means harsh, causing agitation and distress to others.
One should avoid [such words] toward all persons. (End of section.)
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [should avoid] liquor at all times. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.26)

children.text:
varjayediti prakṛtam /
madyaṃ guḍamadhupiṣṭakṛtaṃ anyadapi yanmadakaraṃ yatsarvaṃ brāhmaṇo nityaṃ prāgapyupanayanādvarjayet /
evaṃ kṣatriyavaiśyayoḥ prāgupanayanādūrdhvaṃ ca brahmacaryāt paiṣṭīvarjitāyāḥ surāyā apratiṣedhaḥ, smṛtyantaradarśanāt /
yathā'ha manuḥ-
children.translated_text: 'Should avoid' is understood from the context. '<s>Madya</s>' (liquor) means that made from molasses, honey, or flour, and also anything else that is intoxicating—all of this a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should always avoid, even before <s>upanayana</s> (initiation). Likewise for <s>kṣatriyas</s> and <s>vaiśyas</s>, before and after <s>upanayana</s> and during <s>brahmacarya</s>, there is no prohibition of <s>surā</s> (liquor) other than the flour-based kind, as seen from another <s>smṛti</s>. As <s>Manu</s> states—

children.text: gauḍī mādhvī ca paiṣṭī ca vijñeyā trividhā surā /
children.translated_text: <s>Surā</s> (liquor) is known to be of three kinds: <s>gauḍī</s> (from molasses), <s>mādhvī</s> (from honey), and <s>paiṣṭī</s> (from flour).

children.text: yathaivaikā tathā sarvā na pātavyā dvijottamaiḥ //
children.translated_text: Just as one [of these is prohibited], so are all of them—they should not be drunk by the best of the twice-born.
Thus [ends the quotation]. (End of section.)
Now, for the purpose of teaching what should be done, [the author] states—
[The student should use] a low bed and seat, rise first, and go to sleep last. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.27)

children.text:
gurvapekṣayā nīcaiḥśayyāsane kuryāt /
tasyaiva ca pūrvotthāyī paścātsaṃveśī /
yathā'ha manuḥ-
children.translated_text: In relation to the <s>guru</s>, one should use a lower bed and seat. And one should rise before him and retire after him. As <s>Manu</s> states—
His bed and seat should always be low in the presence of the <s>guru</s>.
He should rise before him and retire after him.
Thus [ends the quotation]. (End of section.)
Moreover—
[He should be] restrained in speech, arms, and stomach. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.28)
'Restrained in arms' means avoiding [idle activities] such as crushing clods of earth.
'Restrained in stomach' means eating what is wholesome and moderate in quantity.
Some read: 'restrained in speech, arms, stomach, and action.'
In that case, since [restraint of action] is already accomplished by 'restrained in arms,' whether the [additional reading] is appropriate or not should be examined. (End of section.)
'Should be' is to be supplied. 'Restrained in speech' means having ceased from unconnected prattle.
Moreover—
One should announce the name and <s>gotra</s> (lineage) of the <s>guru</s> while bowing respectfully. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.29)

children.text:
gurugrahaṇamācāryādīnāmapyupalakṣaṇam /
samānataḥ samyagānataḥ prahvaḥ /
taṃ dhyātvā namaskāraṃ kṛtvetyarthaḥ /
evañca tatrāpi 'ācāryatatputra'; ityasminnācāryagrahaṇaṃ gurvādīnāmapyupalakṣaṇam, teṣāmapi nāmadheyoccāraṇasya pratiṣiddhatvāt /
tathāca smṛtyantaram-
children.translated_text: The use of '<s>guru</s>' is indicative of the <s>ācārya</s> and others as well. '<s>Samānataḥ</s>' means 'properly bowed,' that is, in a humble posture. The meaning is: having meditated upon him and having made obeisance. And thus in the [earlier sūtra] '<s>ācārya</s> and his son,' the mention of '<s>ācārya</s>' is also indicative of the <s>guru</s> and others, since uttering their names is also prohibited. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> [states]—

children.text: ācāryaṃ caiva tatputraṃ tadbhāryāṃ dīkṣitaṃ gurum /
children.translated_text: The <s>ācārya</s>, his son, his wife, a <s>dīkṣita</s> (consecrated person), the <s>guru</s>,

children.text: pitaraṃ ca pitṛvyaṃ ca mātaraṃ mātulaṃ tathā //
children.translated_text: the father, the paternal uncle, the mother, the maternal uncle,

children.text: hitaiṣiṇaṃ ca vidvāṃsaṃ śvaśuraṃ patimeva ca /
children.translated_text: a well-wisher, a learned person, the father-in-law, and the husband—

children.text: na brūyānnāmato vidvān mātuśca bhaginīṃ tathā //
children.translated_text: a wise person should not address them by name, nor the mother's sister.

children.text: yadi brūyāttu taṃ dhyātvā namaskṛtvā vadedatha //
children.translated_text: If one must address them, one should meditate upon them and, having made obeisance, then speak.
Thus [ends the quotation]. (End of section.)
The same applies to a respected person and one who is senior. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.30)
'<s>Arcita</s>' (respected) means one who is honored, that is, a learned person.

children.text: śreyān hitaiṣī vayasā ca vṛddha iti draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Śreyān</s>' (senior) should be understood as a well-wisher and one who is elder in age.
Since this is already established by the word 'ca' (and), the word '<s>evam</s>' (thus) is for the purpose of extending all [the preceding rules] as a whole.
Therefore, the salutation and other [observances] prescribed in the presence of the <s>guru</s> should be observed here too. (End of section.)
One should respond after leaving one's bed, seat, or standing position. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.31)
When the <s>guru</s> gives an instruction, [one should leave] the bed, such as a cot.
The seat, such as a plank.
The standing position, wherever one is standing.

children.text: etāni vihāya tyaktvā pratiśravaṇaṃ prativacanaṃ dadyādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: Having left, that is, having abandoned these, one should give a response—this is the meaning. (End of section.)
One should approach upon being called by one who is not seen. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.32)

children.text: adṛṣṭena guruṇā ājñāyāṃ dīyamānāyāṃ abhikramaṇaṃ tadabhimukhena gamanaṃ kuryādityarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: When a command is being given by the <s>guru</s> who is not seen, one should approach, that is, go toward him—this is the meaning. (End of section.)
One should stand up when [the <s>guru</s> is] in a lower position, [when one is] seated, or [when one is] attending to bodily functions, and upon seeing the <s>guru</s>. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.33)

children.text:
yadā guruḥ adho nīcaiḥ tiṣṭhet āsīta vā, tiryagvātasevā mūtrapurīṣotsargaḥ /
tatra guruṃ dṛṣṭvā uttiṣṭhet /
cakārādanyamukho bhūtvā /
tathāca smṛtyantaram-
children.translated_text: When the <s>guru</s> is standing or sitting below, at a lower level; '<s>tiryagvātasevā</s>' means attending to the discharge of urine and feces. There, upon seeing the <s>guru</s>, one should stand up. By the word 'ca' (and), [one should also] turn away. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> [states]—

children.text: kūpasthitaṃ guruṃ dṛṣṭvā taṭākasthaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Upon seeing the <s>guru</s> standing at a well or at a tank,
the student—and likewise a servant—should stand facing another direction.
Thus [ends the quotation]. (End of section.)
Alternatively—by the word 'ca,' departure is indicated.

children.text: evaṃ sūtrārthaśca tadānīṃ draṣṭavyaḥ adhaḥsthānāsanatiryagvātasevāyāmuttiṣṭhet apayāyācca krameṇeti tatrādhaḥsthānāsane dṛṣṭvottiṣṭhet /
children.translated_text: Thus the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s> should then be understood as follows: when in a lower position, when seated, or when attending to bodily functions, one should stand up and also withdraw in order. That is, when in a lower position or when seated, upon seeing [the <s>guru</s>], one should stand up.
When attending to bodily functions, one should withdraw—this is the sequence. (End of section.)
One should follow [the <s>guru</s>] when he walks. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.34)

children.text:
gacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvānuvrajet /
cakāro 'nuvartate /
tena anuktamapi samuccīyate āsīnaṃ dṛṣṭvā uttiṣṭhet śayānaṃ dṛṣṭvā'sīteti /
tathāca smṛtyantaram-'gacchantamanugacchedāsīnaṃ cottiṣṭhecchayānaṃ cāsīna
children.translated_text: Upon seeing [the <s>guru</s>] walking, one should follow him. The word 'ca' carries over [from the previous sūtra]. By that, what is unstated is also included: upon seeing [the <s>guru</s>] seated, one should stand up; upon seeing him lying down, one should sit. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> [states]: 'One should follow him when he walks, stand up when he is seated, and when he is lying down, one should sit
and attend upon him.'
Thus [ends the quotation]. (End of section.)
Having announced the task, one should report its completion. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.35)

children.text: yadasya karma kartavyaṃ tatkaromītyācāryasya vijñāpya tatkṛtvā kṛtamityākhyāya tiṣṭhet /
children.translated_text: Whatever task is to be done, having informed the <s>ācārya</s> 'I shall do this,' and having done it, one should report 'It is done' and then stand [ready]—this is the meaning.
Since the sentence is incomplete, at '<s>vijñāpya</s>' (having informed), the word 'having done' (<s>kṛtvā</s>) must be supplied.

children.text: ākhyāyetyatrāpi tiṣṭhediti kriyā ca, 'praviśa piṇḍīm'; itivat //
children.translated_text: And at '<s>ākhyāya</s>' (having reported), the verb 'should stand' (<s>tiṣṭhet</s>) is [to be understood as] the action, as in [the expression] 'Enter the <s>piṇḍī</s>.' (End of section.)
One should study when called. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.36)
Only when called by the <s>guru</s> should one study.
One should not urge him [to teach]—this is the meaning. (End of section.)
One should be devoted to what is both pleasing and beneficial [to the <s>guru</s>]. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.37)
'Of the pleasing and the beneficial' [taken] together.
Because what is beneficial but displeasing should not be done.
'<s>Priya</s>' (pleasing) means what gives pleasure; '<s>hita</s>' (beneficial) means what is conducive to future welfare.
