One should do only that which is both pleasing and conducive to future welfare—this is the meaning. (End of section.)
'Should be' is to be supplied. '<s>Yukta</s>' means devoted to that.
The same applies to his wife and sons. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.38)

children.text: tasya yau savarṇau sadṛśau bhāryāputrau tayorapi priyahitayoryuktaḥsyāt /
children.translated_text: His wife and son who are of the same <s>varṇa</s> (class)—one should be devoted to what is pleasing and beneficial to them as well.
By the word 'ca,' the [prohibition of] covering the throat and so forth [also applies].
If one asks why only those of the same <s>varṇa</s> are meant, [the answer is] because the plural is used in the sense of respect. (End of section.)
Now [the author] states an exception to that—
Eating the remnants of their food, bathing them, adorning them, washing their feet, massaging them, and attending upon them [should not be done]. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.39)

children.text:
tadbhāryāputrayoretāni na kuryāt /
priyahitatvātprāptaṃ pratiṣiddhyate /
anayoreva pratiṣedhāt guroretāni kartavyānyeva /
tathācāpastambaḥ-'proṣito bhaikṣādagnau kṛtvā bhuñjīta bhaikṣaṃ haviṣā saṃstutaṃ tatrācāryo devatārtha āhavanīyārthe ca taṃ bhojayitvā yaducchiṣṭaṃ prāśnāti havirucchaṣṭameva tat'; ityādi /
children.translated_text: And thus <s>Āpastamba</s> [states]: 'When away, having placed the alms-food in the fire, one should eat the alms-food which is consecrated with an oblation. There, the <s>ācārya</s> is for the purpose of the deity, and for the purpose of the <s>āhavanīya</s> fire; having fed him, whatever remains is eaten—that is indeed the remnant of the oblation.' And so on.
And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> also [states]: 'The remnants of food of one who is not a <s>guru</s> should not be eaten.' And so on.
'<s>Prasādhana</s>' (adorning) means decoration.
The rest is well-known. (End of section.)

One should not do these for the <s>guru's</s> wife and sons. What was obtained through [the rule about] being devoted to their pleasure and benefit is [here] prohibited. Since the prohibition applies only to these two, for the <s>guru</s> himself these should indeed be done.
Now [the author] states an exception regarding attending upon [them]—
After returning from a journey, attending upon the <s>guru's</s> wives [is to be done]. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.40)
After returning from a journey, one should attend upon (greet by touching the feet of) the <s>guru's</s> wives.
Not at other times.
And not of any other [woman]. (End of section.)
However, regarding that—
Some [say] not of young women, by one who has attained the age of worldly transactions. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.41)

children.text:
vyavahārasamarthena pūrṇaṣoḍaśavarṣeṇetyarthaḥ /
yuvatīnāṃ taruṇīnāṃ viproṣyāpi na kāryamityeke manyante na tu
children.translated_text: 'One who is capable of worldly transactions' means one who has completed sixteen years—this is the meaning. Some hold that even upon returning from a journey, this should not be done with young women. But not
<s>Gautama</s> [himself holds this view].
This should be understood with reference to women who might arouse suspicion and those who would not. (End of section.)

children.text:
uktaṃ 'agnīndhanabhaikṣacaraṇe'; iti /
tatrāgnīndhanaṃ gṛhyebhya eva pṛthakpṛthagupalabhyata iti, bhaikṣacaraṇavidhimāha-
children.translated_text: It has been stated: 'Tending the fire and collecting alms.' Regarding that, the tending of the fire is obtained separately from each of the <s>gṛhya</s> [sūtras]; [now the author] states the rule for collecting alms—
Collecting alms is from all <s>varṇas</s>, except from those who are accused and outcaste. (<s>Gaut</s> 2.42)

children.text: kimarthamidaṃ sūtramārabhyate ? bhaikṣacaraṇaṃ tāvadanena na vidhīyate 'agnīndhanabhaikṣacaraṇe'; ityanena vihitatvāt /
children.translated_text: For what purpose is this <s>sūtra</s> introduced? Collecting alms is not being enjoined by this, since it has already been enjoined by 'tending the fire and collecting alms.' And the exclusion of the accused and outcaste is already stated by 'of those who are approved, in their own duties.' (End of section.)
[This is stated] because [the exclusion] has already been stated by 'of those who are approved, in their own duties.'

children.text:
atraika āhuḥ-śūdraprāpaṇārtho 'yamārambhaḥ, 'praśastānāṃ svakarmasu'; ityanenāprāptatvāditi /
na caitadyuktaṃ, 'vṛttiścennāntareṇa śūdrāt ityanenāpadi śūdrābhyanujñānasiddheḥ /
na cānāpadyapi brahmacāriṇaḥ śūdrābhyanujñānamanena kalpayituṃ yuktaṃ, smṛtyantare atyantapratiṣiddhatvāt,'-
children.translated_text: Here some say: this [sūtra] is introduced for the purpose of including <s>śūdras</s>, since they are not obtained by 'of those who are approved, in their own duties.' But this is not correct, because the permission to [receive from] <s>śūdras</s> in times of distress is already established by 'if livelihood is not [possible] without [it], then from a <s>śūdra</s>.' And it is not proper to infer from this [sūtra] that a <s>brahmacārin</s> may [receive from] <s>śūdras</s> even when there is no emergency, since this is absolutely prohibited in other <s>smṛtis</s>—
One whose limbs are nourished by the food and essence of a <s>śūdra</s>, even if he studies constantly,
even if he offers oblations and recites <s>japas</s>, does not attain the upward path.
Thus [ends the quotation]. (End of section.)

children.text: tasmādanāpadyeva brahmacāriṇaḥ apraśastadvijātiprāpaṇārthoyamārambhaḥ apraśastānāmaviśeṣeṇa prāptau satyāṃ 'abhiśastapatitavarjaṃ'; iti yujyate ca pratiṣedhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, when there is no emergency, this [sūtra] is introduced for the purpose of [allowing] a <s>brahmacārin</s> to receive [alms] from <s>dvijātis</s> (twice-born) who are not approved, since when all non-approved persons are equally obtained [by default], the prohibition 'except from those who are accused and outcaste' is appropriate.

children.text: itarathā śūdraprāpaṇe sati abhiśastādīnāṃ prāptyabhāvādeva pratiṣedho na yujyata iti na ca śakyate vaktuṃ śūdraviṣaya evāyamapavāda iti, yatra hi dvijātayaḥ praśastā adhikriyante tatra śūdro 'pi praśasta eveti itarasya prasaṅga eva nāstīti //
children.translated_text: Otherwise, if [the sūtra] were for the purpose of including <s>śūdras</s>, the prohibition of the accused and others would not be appropriate since there is no [logical] basis for their inclusion in the first place. And one cannot say that this exception applies only to <s>śūdras</s>, for where twice-born persons who are approved are the intended [recipients], a <s>śūdra</s> who is also approved would be included—there is simply no occasion for [including] the other [unapproved <s>śūdra</s>]. (End of section.)

children.text: tena prathamakalpastāvat brahmacāriṇaḥ praśastebhya eva bhaikṣacaraṇaṃ, tadalābhe apraśastebhyaḥ, tadalābhe ācāryādibhyaḥ, sarvābhāve āpadi śūdrāditi sthitam //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the first rule is established: a <s>brahmacārin</s> should first collect alms from those who are approved; if that is not available, from those who are not approved; if that too is unavailable, from the <s>ācārya</s> and others; and in the complete absence [of all these], in times of distress, from a <s>śūdra</s>—this is settled. (End of section.)

children.text:
sarvavarṇānarhatīti sārvavarṇikaṃ, sarveṣāṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
sarvagrahaṇaṃ kṣatriyavaiśyaprāpaṇārthaṃ, anyathā brāhmaṇasyaiva pratigrahādhikārāt tasyaiva syāditi /
varṇagrahaṇaṃ śūdrasyāpi prāpaṇārthaṃ asati varṇagrahaṇe sarvagrahaṇaṃ tayoreva syāditi tadarthaṃ varṇagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam /
tena śūdrasyāprāptau tatprāpaṇārthaṃ varṇagrahaṇam /
tataśca śūdrasyāpi vṛttihīnasya bhikṣācaraṇe na doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: And therefore there is no fault in begging alms even for a <s>Śūdra</s> who is destitute of livelihood.

children.text: bhikṣāsamūho bhaikṣaṃ, tataśca bahubhyo gṛhebhya āhartavyam /
children.translated_text: A collection of alms is <s>bhaikṣa</s>; therefore, [alms] should be gathered from many houses.

children.text: abhiśasta upapātakadoṣeṇābhiśasto gṛhyate, pātakadoṣeṇābhiśastasya patitagrahaṇenaiva siddhatvāt /
children.translated_text: 'Accused' (<s>abhiśasta</s>) is understood as one accused of a minor sin (<s>upapātaka</s>), since for one accused of a major sin (<s>pātaka</s>), the matter is already established by the [earlier] mention of 'fallen' (<s>patita</s>).
And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> [states]: 'Having accused a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> falsely, by a [sin] causing fall or a minor fall.'

'Deserving of all classes' (<s>sārvavarṇika</s>) means 'belonging to all'—the meaning is that it applies to all. The word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>) is for the purpose of extending [the rule] to <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s>, since otherwise, because only a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has the right to accept gifts, it would apply to him alone. The word 'class' (<s>varṇa</s>) is for the purpose of extending [the rule] to the <s>Śūdra</s> as well; without the word 'class,' the word 'all' would apply only to those two [<s>Kṣatriya</s> and <s>Vaiśya</s>]—for that purpose the word 'class' was used. Thus, since [the rule] does not extend to the <s>Śūdra</s> [otherwise], the word 'class' is for the purpose of extending it to him.

children.text: kecitsarveṣu varṇeṣu bhavaṃ sārvavarṇikamiti vigrahaṃ kurvanti teṣāṃ sarvaśabdasya prayojanaṃ na vidmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some analyze '<s>sārvavarṇika</s>' as 'occurring in all classes' (<s>sarveṣu varṇeṣu bhavam</s>). For their [analysis], we do not see the purpose of the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>).
If [one argues] it is for the purpose of extending [the rule] to unworthy twice-born [persons]—that is not so, because the very commencement of the <s>sūtra</s> serves that purpose.
Even if [it is argued to be] for the purpose of extending [the rule] to the <s>Śūdra</s>, the refutation already stated applies. Therefore, this should be considered by the learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
The word '<s>bhavat</s>' should be employed at the beginning, middle, and end, according to the order of classes. (Gaut 2.43)

children.text:
dvipadasya bhikṣāṃ dehīti śabdasya prārthanāyāṃ dehītyasyāpi ca sārmathyāt prāptasyādau brāhmaṇena bhavacchabdaḥ prayoktavyaḥ, madhye kṣatriyeṇa, ante vaiśyena /
bhavacchabdasya prātipadikatvātkevalasya ca prayogābhāvāt strīṇāṃ sakāśe tadāmantritavibhaktyantaḥ prayoktavyaḥ, bhavati bhikṣāṃ dehīti /
puruṣasakāśe bhavan bhikṣāṃ dehīti /
pretyupasargāt smṛtyantaroktamapi draṣṭavyam /
tadapi kṣakārahikārau noccairvaktavyāviti /
yathāha gṛhyasmṛtiḥ 'brāhmaṇo bhikṣeta bhavati bhikṣāṃ dehīti, bhavanmadhyayā rājanyo bhikṣāṃ bhavati dehīti, bhavadantyayā vaiśyo bhikṣāṃ dehi bhavati, kṣāṃ ca hiṃ ca na vardhayet'; iti /
varṇagrahaṇaṃ śūdrasya mantraprāpaṇārthaṃ, tataśca trayāṇāmeva varṇānāmanyatamo mantro draṣṭavyaḥ /
anyo vā racanāviśeṣaḥ kartavyaḥ /

children.translated_text: Since another <s>smṛti</s> shows '<s>Śūdra</s> conduct is like that of a <s>Vaiśya</s>,' the one stated for the <s>Vaiśya</s> may be used.
A specific mantra is not directly stated, in order to indicate the indeterminate nature of [the <s>Śūdra</s>'s] practices.
And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> [states]: 'And his practices are indeterminate, [as are] his indeterminate hair and attire,' and so forth.
The mention of 'order' (<s>anupūrva</s>) is so that there should not be an [arbitrary] option for any single [class].

Of the two-word [phrase] '<s>bhikṣāṃ dehi</s>' ('give alms'), since even '<s>dehi</s>' alone has the capacity for requesting—the word '<s>bhavat</s>' should be employed at the beginning by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, in the middle by a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and at the end by a <s>Vaiśya</s>. Since '<s>bhavat</s>' is a nominal stem and a bare [stem] is not used [in practice], before women it should be used in the vocative case: '<s>bhavati bhikṣāṃ dehi</s>' ('Lady, give alms!'). Before men: '<s>bhavan bhikṣāṃ dehi</s>' ('Sir, give alms!'). From the prefix 'pra-,' what is stated in other <s>smṛtis</s> should also be considered. In that [formula] too, the syllables '<s>kṣa</s>' and '<s>hi</s>' should not be pronounced loudly. As the <s>Gṛhyasmṛti</s> states: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should beg [saying] "<s>bhavati bhikṣāṃ dehi</s>" (with <s>bhavat</s> at the beginning); a <s>Rājanya</s> [saying] "<s>bhikṣāṃ bhavati dehi</s>" (with <s>bhavat</s> in the middle); a <s>Vaiśya</s> [saying] "<s>bhikṣāṃ dehi bhavati</s>" (with <s>bhavat</s> at the end); one should not raise the [syllables] <s>kṣāṃ</s> and <s>hi</s>.' The word 'class' is for the purpose of extending a mantra to the <s>Śūdra</s> as well; therefore, one of the mantras of the three classes should be used for him. Or a different arrangement should be composed.
When [alms] cannot be obtained from the teacher, kinsmen, elder, and one's own [family], then from others. (Gaut 2.44)
The 'teacher' (<s>ācārya</s>) has been defined.
'Kinsman' (<s>jñāti</s>) means one within the <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relationship; 'elder' (<s>guru</s>) means maternal uncle and the like; 'own' (<s>sva</s>) means one's own [family].
When [alms] cannot be obtained elsewhere, <s>bhaikṣa</s> should be requested from these.
The order, however, has been explained.
Regarding this also—
Among these, one should skip the first among the first. (Gaut 2.45)

children.text:
teṣāṃ yo yaḥ prathamanirdiṣṭaḥ tatra tatra pariharet /
anyatrālābhe pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ parihṛtyāpi teṣāmeva sakāśe
children.translated_text: Among these, whoever is mentioned first, that [person's house] one should skip. When [alms] cannot be obtained elsewhere, even after skipping the first among the first, one should still solicit <s>bhaikṣa</s>
from those very [persons].
The mention of 'these' is for the purpose of the restrictive rule 'not from the teacher's house'—[meaning not that one never begs there, but that one skips it first].
And therefore, when [alms] cannot be obtained anywhere, one should understand [that it is obtained] only from the teacher's house.
And thus another <s>smṛti</s> [states]: 'When it cannot be obtained elsewhere, even from the teacher's house.'
Having informed the <s>guru</s>, and being permitted, one should eat. (Gaut 2.46)

children.text: idaṃ bhaikṣamiti gurave kathayitvā tato bhuṃkṣveti tenānujñāto bhuñjīta /
children.translated_text: Having told the <s>guru</s> 'this is the alms-food,' and then being permitted by him [saying] 'eat,' one should eat.

children.text: evañca nivedanaṃ bhaikṣasaṃskārārthaṃ, anujñāta iti vacanāt /
children.translated_text: And thus the informing is for the purpose of consecrating the alms-food, from the statement 'being permitted.'
If the <s>guru</s> should take [the food], then one should fetch more.
In [the <s>guru</s>'s] absence, [one should inform] his wife, son, co-student, or a virtuous person. (Gaut 2.47)
In the absence of the teacher, the informing should be done to his wife and the rest, as circumstances permit.
The word 'his' is for the purpose of indicating that the wife and son are of the same class.
A 'co-student' (<s>sabrahmacārin</s>) is one of the same <s>Veda</s>-school; 'virtuous' (<s>sat</s>) means one of excellent qualities.
Now, how should one eat? Therefore [the author] says—
Silently, being content, without greed, having placed water nearby. (Gaut 2.48)

children.text:
vāgyatastūṣṇīṃ, tṛpyansaṃtoṣaṃ kurvan, pūrvamasaṃtuṣṭo 'pyannadarśanamātrādeva hṛṣyedityarthaḥ /
tathāca smṛtyantaram-
children.translated_text: 'Silently' means in silence; 'being content' means being satisfied—the meaning is that even though previously unsatisfied, one should be delighted at the mere sight of food. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> [states]—
'Seeing [the food], one should be delighted, pleased, and welcome it in every way.'

children.text:
iti /
alolupyamāno viśeṣaspṛhāṃ pariharannatibhojanaṃ varjayedityarthaḥ /
tathāca smṛtyantaram-
children.translated_text: Thus. 'Without greed' means avoiding desire for special [foods] and abstaining from overeating—this is the meaning. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> [states]—
'Overeating is not conducive to longevity, not to health, not to heaven,
not meritorious, and despised by the world—therefore one should avoid it.'

children.text:
iti /
athavā bhojanavidhimaparivarjayannityarthaḥ /
tathāca smṛtyantare bhojanavidhirdraṣṭavyaḥ /
samyaṅi#nadhāyodakaṃ prāśyetyarthaḥ /
samupasargaḥ smṛtyantaroktamārgopasaṃgrahārthaḥ /
tathā'hośanā-"satyaṃ tvartenetyādinodakaṃ pariṣicyāmṛtopastaraṇamityādinā prāśayet"iti /
athavā-udakamiti kamaṇḍalurucyate, tat sannidhāya /
tataśca brahmacāriṇo 'pi kamaṇḍaludhāraṇaṃ kartavyam /
tathaiva manurapi mekhalādibhiḥ saha pratipattividhānāt brahmacāriṇaḥ kamaṇḍaludhāraṇaṃ jñāpayati-
children.translated_text: Thus. Alternatively, [it means] not transgressing the rules of eating—this is the meaning. And thus the rules of eating should be found in other <s>smṛtis</s>. 'Having properly placed water nearby and having sipped'—this is the meaning. The prefix 'sam-' is for the purpose of incorporating the procedure stated in other <s>smṛtis</s>. And thus <s>Uśanas</s> [states]: 'With "truth and not falsehood" and so forth, having sprinkled water, one should eat with "the nectar-spread" and so forth.' Alternatively, by 'water' is meant the water-pot (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>); having placed that nearby. And therefore the <s>brahmacārin</s> too should carry a water-pot. <s>Manu</s> too, by prescribing the procedure [for the <s>brahmacārin</s>] together with the girdle and the rest, indicates the carrying of a water-pot—
'The girdle, the deer-skin, the staff, the sacred thread, and the water-pot—
having cast them into water when destroyed, one should take new ones with mantras.'

children.text:
iti /
evaṃca tata evācamanaṃ kartavyaṃ, vacanasārmathyāt /
ucchiṣṭasparśane na doṣaḥ /
smṛtyantaroktaṃ vā draṣṭavyam /
yathā'ha vasiṣṭhaḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus. And therefore <s>ācamana</s> should also be performed from that very [water-pot], by the force of the statement. There is no fault in touching [the pot when in a state of] having food remnants. Or one should follow what is stated in other <s>smṛtis</s>. As <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> states—

children.text: apsu pāṇau ca kāṣṭhe ca kalpitaḥ pāvakaḥ śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Fire that is established in water, in the hand, or in wood is pure;
therefore, one should wipe the water-pot with water and hands.'
Thus.
Some establish this very meaning from the prefix 'sam-.'

children.text: idānīṃ yadi brahmacārī guroḥ samyagvinayenāvatiṣṭheta tadānīṃ kiṃ kartavyamityata āha-
children.translated_text: Now, if the <s>brahmacārin</s> does not properly conduct himself with obedience to the <s>guru</s>, then what should be done? Therefore [the author] says—
The discipline of the student [should be done] without beating. (Gaut 2.49)

children.text: śiṣyāśiṣṭiḥ śiṣyaśāsanaṃ, avadhena vadhaṃ muktvā, nirrbhatsanādinā kartavyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Student-discipline' (<s>śiṣyaśiṣṭi</s>) means the correction of the student—without beating, that is, excluding actual striking—it should be done through scolding and the like. This is the meaning.

children.text: adhikārādeva siddhe śiṣyagrahaṇamanyasyāpi śāsanīyasya bhāryāputrāderayameva dharma iti jñāpanārtham //
children.translated_text: Although [this] is already established from the context, the mention of 'student' is for the purpose of indicating that this very rule applies also to anyone else who is to be disciplined—wife, son, and the rest.
When [verbal correction] is incapable, [it should be done] with a thin rope or bamboo strip. (Gaut 2.50)
When correction through scolding and the like is incapable, [then] with a rope or a bamboo strip.
Although both are mentioned together, there is an option because they serve the same purpose.
Even with that, [the student] should be corrected [only] lightly.
One who strikes with anything else is punishable by the king. (Gaut 2.51)
One who strikes with anything else—hand, foot, and the like—in anger is punishable by the king.
The mention of 'king' is for the purpose of [conveying] severity.
Now, for how long should one conduct oneself thus? [The author] says—
One should observe <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship) for twelve years for one <s>Veda</s>. (Gaut 2.52)

children.text:
ekavedamadhyeṣyamāṇo dvādaśavarṣāṇyabhihitarūpaṃ brahmacaryaṃ caret kuryāt /
brahmacaryaśabdena yamaniyamakalāpa
children.translated_text: One intending to study a single <s>Veda</s> should observe <s>brahmacarya</s> of the described form for twelve years. By the word '<s>brahmacarya</s>,' the collection of restraints and observances (<s>yama-niyama</s>)
is denoted, because it is for the purpose of [studying] <s>Brahman</s> (the <s>Veda</s>).
Or twelve [years] for each [<s>Veda</s>]. (Gaut 2.53)
Or one should observe <s>brahmacarya</s> for twelve years per <s>Veda</s>.
Or for all [<s>Vedas</s>], until [the study is] completed. (Gaut 2.54)

children.text:
sarveṣu vedeṣu yāvataiva kālenādhyayanamabhinirvartayet tāvantameva kālaṃ brahmacaryaṃ caret tasya tadarthatvāt /
sarvagrahaṇaṃ yadyekamadhīyīta yadi vā dvau yadi vā sarvānityevamartham /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: One should observe <s>brahmacarya</s> for however long it takes to complete the study of all the <s>Vedas</s>, since [<s>brahmacarya</s>] exists for that purpose. The word 'all' is for this meaning: whether one studies one, or two, or all. And thus <s>Manu</s> [states]—

children.text: vedānadhītya vedau vā vedaṃ vāpi yathākramam //
children.translated_text: 'Having studied the <s>Vedas</s>, or two <s>Vedas</s>, or even one <s>Veda</s>, in proper order—'
Thus.
This is an exception [to the rule] above or below the stated limit.
The statement of the fixed rule is because what is studied with discipline becomes powerful.
At the end of [Vedic] learning, the <s>guru</s> should be asked with a gift. (Gaut 2.55)

children.text: vidyāsamāptau, na tu vratānām, gururācāryaḥ arthena prayojanena nimantryaḥ praṣṭavyaḥ kiṃ gurvarthe karavāṇīti //
children.translated_text: At the completion of learning—not of the vows—the <s>guru</s>, the teacher, should be asked with a gift, a purpose: 'What shall I do for the <s>guru</s>'s sake?'
Then—
The bath (<s>snāna</s>) [is taken] after having given [the gift], or having been given permission. (Gaut 2.56)
'Having done' means having given—the meaning is [having given] the gift prescribed by the <s>guru</s>.

children.text: tena vā alaṃ gurudakṣiṇayetyanujñātasya snānaṃ samāvṛttiḥ //
children.translated_text: Or for one who has been permitted by him [saying] 'enough with the <s>guru</s>-fee'—the bath [marks] the completion (<s>samāvṛtti</s>) [of studentship].

children.text: idānīṃ pitrādyanekagurusannidhāne kaḥ prathamaḥ pūjya ityata āha-
children.translated_text: Now, when the father and other multiple <s>gurus</s> are present together, who is to be honored first? Therefore [the author] says—
The teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) is the foremost among <s>gurus</s>. (Gaut 2.57)

children.text: ācārya uktalakṣaṇaḥ, sa śreṣṭhaḥ pradhāno gurūṇāṃ anyeṣāṃ pitrādīnām /
children.translated_text: The teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) is as characterized [earlier]. He is the foremost, the chief, among the other <s>gurus</s> such as the father and the rest.
And therefore, in [the rule] 'when there is a meeting, [one should honor] the superior,' the word 'superior' refers to this very [teacher].
The mother, according to some. (Gaut 2.58)

children.text:
eke mātā śreṣṭheti manyante /
itikaraṇātpitetyapare /
anyathā mātaika ityeva siddhatvāt /
kevalāt piturācāryaḥ pradhānaḥ /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: Some hold that the mother is the foremost. By the word 'iti,' [it is implied that] others [say] the father. Otherwise, 'the mother, according to some' alone would have been sufficient. The teacher is foremost over the father alone [i.e., when compared only to the father]. And thus <s>Manu</s> [states]—
'The mother and father who produce him from mutual desire—
one should know that birth of his to be [merely] the birth that occurs in the womb.'
'But the birth that a teacher who has mastered the <s>Veda</s> produces for him
through the <s>Sāvitrī</s> according to rule—that is the true [birth], that is free from old age and death.'

children.text:
iti /
yadi pitaivācāryo bhavati tadā pitā viśiṣyate /
mātā sarveṣāṃ śreṣṭhā /
tathāca vasiṣṭhaḥ-
children.translated_text: Thus. If the father himself is the teacher, then the father is superior. The mother is the foremost of all. And thus <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> [states]—
'The teacher exceeds the sub-teacher (<s>upādhyāya</s>) tenfold; the father exceeds the teacher a hundredfold;
the mother exceeds the father a thousandfold in weight of reverence.'

children.text: ityatra pitṛśabdena pitaivācāryo yo bhavati sa eva gṛhyata iti //
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'father' is understood only the father who is also the teacher—this is [the correct interpretation].
Thus ends the second chapter of <s>Maskarī</s>'s commentary on the <s>Gautama</s> [<s>Dharmasūtra</s>].
Third Chapter
For one who has thus completed the observances and attained learning—
Some declare the option of life-stages (<s>āśrama</s>) for him. (Gaut 3.1)
For him whose <s>brahmacarya</s> has been unbroken. And thus <s>Manu</s> [states]—

children.text: vedānadhītya vedau vā vedaṃ vāpi yathākramam /
children.translated_text: 'Having studied the <s>Vedas</s>, or two <s>Vedas</s>, or even one <s>Veda</s> in proper order,
with unbroken <s>brahmacarya</s>, one should enter the householder <s>āśrama</s>.'
Thus.

children.text:
evaṃ ca viplutasyopapātakaprāyaścittaṃ draṣṭavyam /
śūdraparyudāsārthaṃ vā tadgrahaṇaṃ, āśramadharmābhidhānaṃ mā bhūttasyāpīti /
vīpsārthaṃ vā tasya tasyeti, brāhmaṇasya kṣatriyasya vaiśyasya ceti /
children.translated_text: And thus, for one whose [<s>brahmacarya</s>] has been broken, the expiation for a minor sin (<s>upapātaka</s>) should be prescribed. Or, the mention of 'him' (<s>tasya</s>) is for the purpose of excluding the <s>Śūdra</s>, [meaning] 'let not the teaching of <s>āśrama</s> duties apply to him.' Or [the word <s>tasya</s> is used] with distributive meaning—'of each one': of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, of the <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and of the <s>Vaiśya</s>.

children.text:
tadgrahaṇamantareṇāpyadhikārādevaitatsiddhamiti cenna, smṛtyantarābhāsāśaṅkānivṛttyarthatvāt /
evaṃ hi smṛtyantaraṃ pratibhāti-"eṣa vo 'bhihito dharmo brāhmaṇasya caturvidhaḥ"iti, tatra brāhmaṇasyaivāyaṃ caturvidho dharmaḥ itarayorekavidha ityāśaṅkā syāditi /
tarhi tatkathamiti cet tatra brāhmaṇagrahaṇaṃ pradarśanārtham /
tatkathaṃ gamyata iti cet trayāṇāmeva varṇānāṃ catvāra āśramā iti smṛtyantaradarśanāt /
tathā cāpastambaḥ-"sarveṣāmupanayanaprabhṛti samānamācāryakule vāsaḥ sarveṣāmanūtsargo vidyāyā buddhvā karmāṇi yatkāmayettadārabheta"iti /
eke bruvate,- tulyaphalatvādāśramavikalpaḥ /
dvividhaṃ hi phalamabhyudayarūpaṃ niḥśreyasarūpaṃ ceti, tadanyatamenava labhyata iti /
tathā ca śrutiḥ-"trayo dharmaskandhā yajño 'dhyayanaṃ dānamiti prathamastapa eva dvitīyastṛtīyamācāryakule vasanametānāruhya brahmalokaṃ gacchati brahmasaṃstho 'mṛtatvameti"iti /
arthastu-trayo dharmasyāśrayā-, yajñādhyayanaṃ dānamiti gṛhasthanirdeśaḥ, tapa eveti vānaprasthaparivrājakayordharmaḥ, ācāryakulavasanaṃ brahmacāriṇaḥ /
etānāruhyeti brahmacāryāśramaṃ, gṛhasthāśramaṃ, vānaprasthāśramaṃ, parivrājakāśramaṃ vā samyagāsthāyetyarthaḥ /
yasteṣāṃ brahmasaṃstho brahmaniṣṭho
children.translated_text: If [one objects that] even without the word 'his,' this is already established from the context—that is not so, because [the word serves] to refute the suspicion [arising from] the appearance of another <s>smṛti</s>. For another <s>smṛti</s> appears thus: 'This fourfold <s>dharma</s> has been taught to you for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.' There, the suspicion might arise that this fourfold <s>dharma</s> is only for the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, and for the other two [classes] only one [<s>āśrama</s>]. If one asks how then [to understand that passage]—the mention of '<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>' there is for the purpose of illustration. If one asks how this is known—from the evidence of other <s>smṛtis</s> that the four <s>āśramas</s> are for the three classes only. And thus <s>Āpastamba</s> [states]: 'For all, from the <s>upanayana</s> onward, residence in the teacher's house is the same; for all, there is no abandonment of learning; having understood, whatever actions one desires, those one should undertake.' Some declare the option of <s>āśramas</s> because they yield equal results. For the result is twofold: in the form of prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) and in the form of the highest good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>)—and [each] is obtainable by any one of them. And thus the <s>śruti</s> [states]: 'Three are the branches of <s>dharma</s>: sacrifice, study, and charity—this is the first; austerity alone is the second; the third is residing in the teacher's house; entering upon these, one goes to <s>Brahmaloka</s>; one who is established in <s>Brahman</s> attains immortality.' But the meaning is: Three are the supports of <s>dharma</s>—sacrifice, study, and charity is the description of the householder; austerity alone is the <s>dharma</s> of the forest-dweller and the renunciant; residence in the teacher's house is for the <s>brahmacārin</s>. 'Entering upon these' means properly establishing oneself in the <s>brahmacārin</s> <s>āśrama</s>, the householder <s>āśrama</s>, the forest-dweller <s>āśrama</s>, or the renunciant <s>āśrama</s>. Whoever among them is 'established in <s>Brahman</s>'—intent on <s>Brahman</s>,
the knower—attains immortality, that is, liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).

children.text:
tataśca sarveṣāmapi brahmalokaprāptipratipādanāt, tulyaphalataivoktā /
tathā jābālaśrutāvapi tulyaphalataiva śrūyate-'brahmacaryaṃ samāpya gṛhī bhavet /
gṛhī bhūtvā vanī bhavet /
vanī bhūtvā pravrajat /
yadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva pravrajet gṛhādvā vanādvā brahmalokaṃ gacchati'; iti /
manurapyāha-
children.translated_text: And therefore, since the attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s> is taught for all of them, equal results are indeed stated. And thus in the <s>Jābāla</s> <s>śruti</s> too, equal results are heard: 'Having completed <s>brahmacarya</s>, one should become a householder. Having become a householder, one should become a forest-dweller. Having become a forest-dweller, one should renounce. Or alternatively, one may renounce directly from <s>brahmacarya</s>, or from the household, or from the forest. One goes to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.' <s>Manu</s> too says—
'All of these [<s>āśramas</s>], when followed in proper sequence according to the scriptures,
lead the twice-born who acts as prescribed to the highest destination.'
Thus.
Here, by the word 'also' (<s>api</s>), even a single [<s>āśrama</s>] should be understood.

children.text: āpastambopyāha-'catvāra āśramā gārhasthyamācāryakule vasanaṃ maunaṃ vānapraśthyāmiti /
children.translated_text: <s>Āpastamba</s> too says: 'The four <s>āśramas</s> are: householdership, residence in the teacher's house, the vow of silence [i.e., renunciation], and forest-dwelling.

children.text: teṣu sarveṣu yathopadeśamavyagraṃ vartamānaḥ kṣemaṃ gacchati'; iti /
children.translated_text: Among all of these, one who conducts himself diligently according to the instruction attains well-being.'
Therefore, because of equal results, there is the option [among <s>āśramas</s>].

children.text:
nanu tulyatve sati brahmacaryeṇaivobhayavidhaphalaprāpteritarāśramavidhānānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ iti /
ucyate- yo yasyānuṣṭhāne samarthaḥ tasya tadāśramapratipattyarthaṃ itarāśramavidhānamiti /
janmāntaravāsanayā vā iṣṭāśramapratipattyartham /
śrutirupi-"taṃ vidyākarmaṇī samanvārabhete pūrvaprajñā ca"iti /
yāvajjīvaśrutirapi gṛhasthasyārthinaḥ śaktiviṣaye draṣṭavyā /
evaṃ gṛhīte vyutthānaśrutirapyupapadyate-'evaṃ vai tamātmānaṃ viditvā putreṣaṇāyāśca vitteṣaṇāyāśca lokeṣaṇāyāśca vyutthāyātha bhikṣācaryaṃ caranti'; iti /
itarathā hi bhikṣācaryamiti saṃnyāsopadeśo nopapadyata iti /
jāyamānaśrutyāpi yajñādīnāmavaśyakartavyatā pratipādyate gṛhasthasya, na tu jāyamānasyaiva, ṛṇatrayasambandhasyātyantāsambhavāt 'brahmacaryādeva pravrajet'; iti śrutiviruddhatvāt 'so 'ta eva brahmacaryātpravrajati,'; 'yamicchettamāvaset'; ityādismṛteraviruddhatvācca /
arthavādānāṃ ca kāryaśeṣatvāt /
tataśca padārtho 'pyevaṃ grahītavyaḥ-gṛhastho jāyamānaḥ pūrvavāsanayā gārhasthyaṃ praviṣṭaḥ /
brahmaṇagrahaṇaṃ kṣatriyavaiśyayorupalakṣaṇam /
tribhiḥ ṝṇaiḥ sambadhyate-yajñena devebhya ṝṇī bhavatyato yajñaḥ kartavyaḥ /
prajayā pitṛbhyaḥ ataḥ prajotpādanaṃ kartavyam /
brahmacaryeṇa ṝṣibhyaḥ ataḥ parvādau brahmacaryarakṣaṇaṃ kartavyamiti /
evaṃ gṛhīte sarvatra śrutismṛtyaravirodho bhavati /
ekegrahaṇānna tu gautamaḥ, tasya tu samuccayo mataḥ /
kathamavagamyate ?"aikāśramyaṃ tvācāryāḥ"iti bādhapakṣasyāpi paramatatvena nirdeśāt,"prāguttamāttraya āśramiṇaḥ"iti ca liṅgāt,prāguttamāśramāttrayasyābhāvāt /
vikalpapakṣe gautamastāvadevaṃ manyate-
children.translated_text: Now, if they are equal, there arises the objection that since both types of results are attained through <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship) alone, the prescription of other <s>āśramas</s> (life-stages) would be purposeless. To this it is said: the prescription of other <s>āśramas</s> is for the purpose of enabling each person to adopt that <s>āśrama</s> for which he is capable. Or it is for the purpose of adopting the desired <s>āśrama</s> according to the impressions from previous births. The <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) also states: "Knowledge and action take hold of him, as well as prior wisdom." The injunction 'for life' should be understood as applying to the householder who desires results and has the capacity. When understood thus, the <s>śruti</s> regarding renunciation also becomes consistent: 'Having thus known that Self, having risen above the desire for sons, the desire for wealth, and the desire for worlds, they then practice the mendicant life.' For otherwise, the instruction of <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) through the word 'mendicant life' would not be consistent. By the <s>śruti</s> about being 'born with debts,' the obligatory nature of sacrifices and the like is established for the householder, but not for one who is merely born, because the connection with the three debts is absolutely impossible [for one who renounces directly], because it would contradict the <s>śruti</s> 'One may renounce directly from <s>brahmacarya</s>,' because it is not contradicted by the <s>śruti</s> 'He renounces directly from <s>brahmacarya</s>' and by <s>smṛtis</s> (traditional texts) such as 'One should remain in whichever [<s>āśrama</s>] one desires.' And because <s>arthavādas</s> (explanatory passages) are subordinate to injunctions. Accordingly, the meaning of the passage should be understood thus: the householder, being 'born' means one who has entered the householder life due to previous impressions. The mention of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is illustrative of <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> as well. He is bound by three debts: he becomes indebted to the gods through sacrifice, therefore sacrifice must be performed; indebted to the ancestors through progeny, therefore offspring must be produced; indebted to the sages through <s>brahmacarya</s>, therefore the observance of <s>brahmacarya</s> must be maintained on <s>parva</s> (sacred) days and the like. When understood thus, there is no contradiction with any <s>śruti</s> or <s>smṛti</s>. By the word 'some,' it is not <s>Gautama</s>'s [view]; his view is rather the cumulative approach (<s>samuccaya</s>). How is this known? Because even the opposing view is presented as another's opinion in the statement 'But the teachers hold there is only one <s>āśrama</s>,' and from the indication in 'The three [lower] <s>āśrama</s>-dwellers are prior to the highest,' since the three do not exist without the prior ones. On the alternative view, <s>Gautama</s> holds thus:
Through sacrifice one attains the gods, through <s>tapas</s> (austerity) the realm of <s>Virāj</s>,
Through <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) the abode of <s>Brahman</s>, and through <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).

children.text:
iti bhinnaphalatvenopadeśāt jābālaśrutāvapyanyatamamāruhyetyanuktvā etānāruhyeti samuccayābhiprāyeṇoktatvāt, brahmalokaprāpterapi samuccayaphalatvenopadiṣṭatvāt jābālaśrutāvapi prādhānyena pūrvaṃ samuccayapakṣasyaivābhihitatvāt, 'sarve 'pi kramaśaḥ'; ityasmin manuvākye 'piśabdasya samuccayārthatvāt, āpastambavākye 'pi teṣu sarveṣviti bahuvacanāt- naikasminneva vartamānaḥ kiṃ tu sarveṣveva vartamāna ityabhiprāyeṇoktatvāt, ṛṇatrayaśruterapi yathārtha evopapadyamānatvāt,"pūrvaprajñā ca"iti śruterapi vidyābhiprāyeṇopapadyamānatvāt, yāvajjīvaśruterapi"gṛhī vanaṃ praviśedyadi gṛhameva kāmayeta tadā yāvajjīvasagnihotraṃ juhuyāt"iti jābālaśrutivākye anityatvadarśanāt, asmin pakṣe vyatthānaśruterapi sutarāmupapadyamānatvāt,"caturthamāyuṣo bhāgaṃ"ityanenāpi manunā samuccayapakṣamevāśrityoktatvāt, samuccayapakṣa eva śreyāniti /
ata eva vikalpabādhapakṣau paramatatvenopanyastau /
evañca -"yamicchettamāvaset"ityādivākyāni vikalpācāryadarśanenoktānīti draṣṭavyāni /
asamartho yaḥ samuccayānuṣṭhāne andhapaṅgutvādidoṣeṇa niḥsvatvādinā vā tena vikalpapakṣo 'pyāśrayaṇīyaḥ ityabhiprāyeṇa bruvata ityarthasiddhasyāpyupanyāsaḥ /
athavā-yo 'dhyātmajñānī tena vikalpapakṣa āśrayaṇīyaḥ,itareṇa samuccayapakṣa iti /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, one who possesses knowledge of the Self (<s>adhyātmajñāna</s>) should resort to the alternative view, while the other [who lacks such knowledge] should follow the cumulative view.
Why? Because the purpose of ritual practice is the arising of spiritual knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>).

children.text: tasminnutpanne yatra kvāpyāśrame sthitasya puruṣārthaḥ sidhyatīti /
children.translated_text: When that [knowledge] has arisen, the supreme goal of man (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) is accomplished for one situated in any <s>āśrama</s> whatsoever.
The use of the word '<s>āśrama</s>' is for conventional usage, as in 'of the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes) and <s>āśramas</s>' and so forth.

Because the instruction presents different fruits [for different āśramas], and because in the <s>Jābāla</s> <s>śruti</s> it is stated with the cumulative intent by saying 'having ascended these' rather than 'having ascended any one of these,' and because even the attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s> is taught as the fruit of the cumulative [practice], and because in the <s>Jābāla</s> <s>śruti</s> the cumulative view is primarily stated first, and because in the verse of <s>Manu</s> 'all indeed in sequence' the word 'also' has the sense of cumulation, and because in the statement of <s>Āpastamba</s> too, the plural 'in all of those' [is used], meaning one who abides not in just one but in all of them, and because the <s>śruti</s> about the three debts is consistent as literally meaningful, and because the <s>śruti</s> 'and prior wisdom' is consistent when understood as referring to knowledge, and because the 'for life' <s>śruti</s> is seen to be non-permanent in the <s>Jābāla</s> <s>śruti</s> passage 'The householder may enter the forest; if he desires the household life, then he should offer the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire offering) for life,' and because in this view the <s>śruti</s> about renunciation is all the more consistent, and because <s>Manu</s> too says 'the fourth part of life' relying on the cumulative view alone — therefore the cumulative view is superior. For this very reason, the alternative and exclusion views are presented as the opinions of others. And thus, statements such as 'One should remain in whichever one desires' should be understood as stated according to the view of the teachers who hold the alternative position. The presentation, though the meaning is already established, is with the intent that one who is incapable of cumulative practice due to defects such as blindness or lameness, or due to poverty and the like, may also resort to the alternative view.
Now, what are those <s>āśramas</s>? To this he says:
The <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student), the <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder), the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant), and the <s>vaikhānasa</s> (forest hermit). // Gaut. 3.2 //

children.text:
brahmacaryaṃ caratīti, brahmaṇa eva vā viṣaye niḥspṛhaścaratīti, brahmacārī /
gṛhaṃ patnī tatsaṃyogādagṛhasthaḥ /
bhikṣāśīlatvādibhakṣuḥ /
vikhanasā proktaṃ śāstraṃ vaikhānasaṃ tadvidhinā vartata iti vaikhānasaḥ /
visamāsa eṣāmeva
children.translated_text: One who practices <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), or one who moves without desire in the domain of <s>Brahman</s> alone, is a <s>brahmacārī</s>. A house means a wife; through association with her, one is a <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder). Because of the habit of begging for alms, one is a <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant). The scripture taught by <s>Vikhanas</s> is the <s>Vaikhānasa</s>; one who lives according to its rules is a <s>vaikhānasa</s>. The separate enumeration of these

children.text:
pṛthaktvajñāpanārthaḥ, yathā'hośanā-'dvau brahmacāriṇāvupakurvāṇo naiṣṭhikaśceti, dvau vaikhānasau sapatnīko vipatnīkaśceti, dvau saṃnyāsinau bhikṣusanyāsī vedasanyāsī ceti, bahudhā gṛhasthaḥ śālīnayāyāvarādibhedena'; ityādi /
nanu ca smṛtyantare vaikhānasamabhidhāya bhikṣurityuktaḥ iha kimarthaṃ kramabheda iti /
ucyate 'prāguttamāstraya āśramiṇaḥ'; ityatra vaikhānasavarjanārthaḥ kramabhedaḥ /
tasya grāmapraveśanapratiṣedhādeva siddhamiti cet na, arthināmaraṇyagamanasyāpi sambhavāt tathāca smṛtyantaram-
children.translated_text: is for the purpose of indicating their distinct varieties, as <s>Śaunaka</s> says: 'There are two types of <s>brahmacārīs</s>: the <s>upakurvāṇa</s> (temporary student) and the <s>naiṣṭhika</s> (lifelong student); two types of <s>vaikhānasas</s>: one with a wife and one without a wife; two types of renouncers: the <s>bhikṣu-saṃnyāsī</s> (mendicant renouncer) and the <s>veda-saṃnyāsī</s> (renouncer of Vedic rites); and the <s>gṛhastha</s> is of many kinds, distinguished as <s>śālīna</s> (settled), <s>yāyāvara</s> (wandering), and so forth.' Now, in another <s>smṛti</s>, after describing the <s>vaikhānasa</s>, the <s>bhikṣu</s> is mentioned — so why is the order different here? It is said: the change in order is for the purpose of excluding the <s>vaikhānasa</s> in the passage 'The three <s>āśrama</s>-dwellers prior to the highest.' If one objects that this is already established by the prohibition of entering the village for him, [the reply is] no, because it is possible for those who desire [results] to go to the forest as well. And thus another <s>smṛti</s> states:
One versed in the four <s>Vedas</s>, one who holds the alternative view, a <s>Nairukta</s> (etymologist), a reciter of <s>Dharma</s> texts,
a <s>brahmacārī</s>, a <s>gṛhastha</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s> — this assembly is of ten members at minimum.
Thus.
But some [say]:
Having performed the <s>Prājāpatya</s> <s>iṣṭi</s> (sacrifice to <s>Prajāpati</s>) with the fee of all the <s>Vedas</s>,
having consigned the sacred fires into oneself, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should renounce from the household.

children.text: iti smṛtyantaramavalambya gārhasthyādeva saṃnyāsaḥ kartavya ityevamarthaḥ kramabheda iti varṇayanti /
children.translated_text: Relying on this other <s>smṛti</s>, they explain that the change in order means that <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) should be undertaken from the householder stage alone.
Whether this has already been established by the previous <s>sūtra</s> or not is to be deliberated upon by the learned <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
Among them, the householder is the source, because the others do not procreate. // Gaut. 3.3 //

children.text:
caturṇāmapyāśramāṇāṃ gṛhasthaḥ kāraṇaṃ, aprajanatvāditareṣāṃ brahmacāryādīnām /
vaikhānasārthā hetūktiḥ, brahmacāriṇo brahmacaryarakṣaṇādeva siddhatvādibhakṣorapyūrdhvaretastvavidhānāt /
evaṃ ca vaikhānasasya sapatnīkatvapakṣe 'pi brahmacaryarakṣaṇaṃ kartavyam /
adhikārādeva siddhe 'teṣāṃ'; grahaṇaṃ gṛhasthotpannānāmeva teṣāṃ dharme ādhikāra ityevamartham /
tathāca śātātapaḥ-
children.translated_text: Of all four <s>āśramas</s>, the <s>gṛhastha</s> (householder) is the cause, because the others — the <s>brahmacārī</s> and the rest — do not procreate. The statement of the reason is for the sake of the <s>vaikhānasa</s>, since for the <s>brahmacārī</s> it is already established through the observance of <s>brahmacarya</s> alone, and for the <s>bhikṣu</s> too through the injunction of <s>ūrdhvaretas</s> (upward retention of seed). And thus, even in the view where the <s>vaikhānasa</s> has a wife, the observance of <s>brahmacarya</s> must be maintained. Although this is already established from the [general] qualification itself, the word 'among them' means that only those born as householders have the qualification for this <s>dharma</s>. And thus <s>Śātātapa</s> states:
<s>Caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts) are those who have turned back — the wandering ascetics and hermits.
The offspring born to them should be made to dwell with the <s>Caṇḍālas</s>.

children.text: iti teṣāṃ gṛhastha eva yonirityukte evakārādevetareṣāṃ brahmacaryarakṣaṇe siddhe evamabhidhānameṣāṃ punarnivṛttirmā bhūditi /
children.translated_text: Thus, when it is stated that the householder alone is the source for them, since the observance of <s>brahmacarya</s> for the others is already established by the word 'alone,' this statement is made so that there be no turning back for them.

children.text: yadi te gārhasthyaṃ prati nivṛtti bhaveyuḥ tadā te caṇḍālā bhavanti kutaḥ ? udāhṛtaśātātapavacanāt /
children.translated_text: If they were to turn back toward the householder life, then they would become <s>Caṇḍālas</s>. Why? Because of the cited statement of <s>Śātātapa</s>.
In that regard: they become <s>Caṇḍālas</s>.

children.text: pratyavasitāḥ pratinivṛttāḥ ye parivrājakatāpasāḥ naiṣṭhikavaikhānasāḥ tasmātteṣāṃ jātānyapatyāni caṇḍālaiḥsahavāsayedrājā grāmo vetyarthaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Turned back' means those who have returned — the wandering ascetics and hermits who are <s>naiṣṭhika</s> (lifelong) <s>vaikhānasas</s>. Therefore the king or the village should make the offspring born to them dwell with the <s>Caṇḍālas</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: idānīmāśramadharmeṣu krameṇa vaktavyeṣu prāpteṣu sarvāśramasāmyādupakurvāṇasya pūrvamuktvā naiṣṭhikasya krameṇa prāptaṃ vaktumāha-
children.translated_text: Now, when the <s>āśrama</s> duties are to be stated in order, since, due to their being common to all <s>āśramas</s>, the duties of the <s>upakurvāṇa</s> (temporary student) have been stated first, he proceeds to state what comes in order for the <s>naiṣṭhika</s> (lifelong student):
What has been stated [applies] to the <s>brahmacārī</s> there. // Gaut. 3.4 //

children.text:
tatropanayanaprakareṇa yadagnīndhanādyuktaṃ tadasyāpi bhavatītyatideśaḥ /
nanu ca naiṣṭikasyaivedaṃ nopakurvāṇasyeti kathaṃ jñāyata iti ? ucyate-upakurvāṇasyoktatvāt, gṛhasthabhikṣuvaikhānasānāṃ vakṣyamāṇatvāt, naiṣṭikasyaiva bhavatīti /
tarhi brahmacārigrahaṇaṃ kimartamiti cet yenopakurvāṇavratamanuṣṭhitaṃ tasyaiva
children.translated_text: This is an extension (<s>atideśa</s>): what has been stated regarding kindling the fire and so forth in the context of <s>upanayana</s> (initiation) applies to this one [the <s>naiṣṭhika</s>] as well. Now, how is it known that this applies to the <s>naiṣṭhika</s> alone and not to the <s>upakurvāṇa</s>? It is said: because [the duties of] the <s>upakurvāṇa</s> have already been stated, and because the duties of the <s>gṛhastha</s>, <s>bhikṣu</s>, and <s>vaikhānasa</s> are yet to be stated, this applies to the <s>naiṣṭhika</s> alone. If asked, then what is the purpose of mentioning '<s>brahmacārī</s>'? It means that only one who has first practiced the vow of the <s>upakurvāṇa</s>

children.text:
naiṣṭhikatvasyādhikāra ityevamartham /
atideśāt upakurvāṇavratameva naiṣṭhikasyāpyanuṣṭātavyamityuktvā idānīmasya viśeṣavidhimāha-
children.translated_text: has the qualification for <s>naiṣṭhika</s> status — this is the meaning. Having stated through the extension that the vow of the <s>upakurvāṇa</s> must be practiced by the <s>naiṣṭhika</s> as well, he now states a special rule for him:
Dependence on the teacher until the end. // Gaut. 3.5 //
Subservience to the teacher, conformity to his will, must be maintained until death.
Moreover:
He should recite during the time remaining from the teacher's work. // Gaut. 3.6 //
During the time beyond service to the teacher, he should perform <s>japa</s> (recitation).

children.text: evaṃ ca japa evāsya viśiṣṭaṃ dharmasādhanamiti //
children.translated_text: And thus, <s>japa</s> alone is his distinctive means of <s>dharma</s> (spiritual merit).

children.text:
ācārya iti prakṛte gurugrahaṇaṃ mātāpitrorapi śuśrūṣāprāpaṇārtham /
tathāca manuḥ-
children.translated_text: The use of the word 'teacher' (<s>guru</s>) when '<s>ācārya</s>' (preceptor) has been mentioned in the preceding context is for the purpose of including service to the mother and father as well. And thus <s>Manu</s> states:

children.text: teṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ śuśrūṣā paramaṃ tapa ucyate /
children.translated_text: Service to those three is declared to be the highest <s>tapas</s> (austerity).
Without their permission, one should not practice any other <s>dharma</s>.
Thus.
In the absence of the teacher, [one should serve] his offspring. // Gaut. 3.7 //

children.text: gurorabhāve tadapatye śuśrūṣā, adhyāpayiturabhāve tadapatye śuśrūṣeti niyamārtham /
children.translated_text: In the absence of the <s>guru</s>, service to his offspring; in the absence of the one who taught, service to his offspring — this is a restrictive rule.
The use of the word '<s>guru</s>' is for the purpose of including offspring of the same class.
The use of the word 'offspring' is for the purpose of excluding the wife.
In the absence of that, [one should serve] an elder fellow-student, or the sacred fire. // Gaut. 3.8 //

children.text: tadabhāve guruputrābhāve vidyādibhirvṛddhe, tadabhāve sabrahmacāriṇiṃ samānacaraṇe, tadabhāve agnau /
children.translated_text: In the absence of that — in the absence of the teacher's son — one who is senior in learning and the like; in the absence of that, a fellow-student of the same Vedic school; in the absence of that, the sacred fire.
Service to the fire means meditation on the fire in its luminous form.
Now, what is the fruit of this <s>āśrama</s>? To this he says:
One who conducts himself thus, with senses controlled, attains the world of <s>Brahman</s>. // Gaut. 3.9 //

children.text:
evaṃ yathopadeśaṃ vartamāno brahmalokaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sthānamavāpnoti sa cejjitendriyo bhavati /
brahmacaryarakṣaṇopadeśāt upasthendriyasyoktatvāt idaṃ cakṣurādiviṣayaṃ draṣṭavyam /
yathā'ha manuḥ-
children.translated_text: One who lives thus according to the instruction attains <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of <s>Brahman</s>), the abode of <s>Brahman</s>, provided he has conquered his senses. Since the instruction about maintaining <s>brahmacarya</s> has [already] addressed the organ of generation, this should be understood as referring to the senses of sight and so forth. As <s>Manu</s> says:

children.text: śrutvā spṛṣṭvā ca dṛṣṭvā ca bhuktvā ghrātvā ca yo nara /
children.translated_text: A man who, having heard, touched, seen, eaten, and smelled,

children.text: na hṛṣyati glāyati vā sa vijñeyo jitendriyaḥ //
children.translated_text: neither rejoices nor grieves — he is to be known as one who has conquered his senses.
Thus.
The injunction at the conclusion regarding the fruit has the meaning that this [sense-control] is the principal [duty] for the subsequent [<s>āśramas</s>] as well.
Now he states the duties common to the others as well:
And for the subsequent ones, whatever is not contradictory to this. // Gaut. 3.10 //

children.text: yadbrahmacāriṇa uktaṃ taduttareṣāmapi bhavati yadaviruddhaṃ dyūtādivarjanam /
children.translated_text: What has been stated for the <s>brahmacārī</s> applies to the subsequent [<s>āśrama</s>-dwellers] as well, insofar as it is not contradictory — such as the avoidance of gambling and the like.

children.text: yadvirudhyate tadvyāvartate yathāgnikāryaṃ pravrajitasya, gurukulavāso vaikhānasasya, gṛhasthasya brahmacaryarakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: What is contradictory is excluded: for example, fire-ritual for the renunciant, residence in the teacher's house for the <s>vaikhānasa</s>, and the observance of <s>brahmacarya</s> for the householder.

children.text: caśabdaḥ uttarasya yadvakṣyamāṇaṃ tadapyaviruddhaṃ pūrveṣāmapi bhavatīti jñāpayati, 'yathā na mlecchāśucyadhārmikaiḥsaha sambhāṣeta'; ityādi //
children.translated_text: The word 'and' indicates that what will be stated for the subsequent [<s>āśrama</s>] also applies, where not contradictory, to the prior ones as well — such as 'one should not converse with barbarians, impure persons, and the unrighteous,' and so forth.
The <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) is without accumulation. // Gaut. 3.11 //

children.text: idānīṃ kramaprāptasya gṛhasthasya dharmā vaktavyāḥ, tānvilaṅghya kimarthaṃ bhikṣorabhidhīyata iti cet,atrocyate- bahuvaktavyo gṛhasthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the duties of the householder, whose turn has come in order, ought to be stated. If asked why, skipping over him, the duties of the <s>bhikṣu</s> are stated [first], the reply is: the householder has much to be stated about him. While his duties are being stated, some that are not contradictory — how could they apply to the prior [<s>āśramas</s>]? For that purpose, the statement is made out of sequence.

children.text: tasyābhidhīyamānāḥ dharmāḥ aviruddhāḥ kecitkathaṃ nāma pūrveṣāṃ syuriti tadarthaṃ vyutkrameṇābhidhānam /
children.translated_text: While his duties are being stated, some that are not contradictory — how would they apply to the prior [<s>āśramas</s>]? For that purpose, the statement is made out of sequence.

children.text: tarhi vaikhānasasya vaktavya iti cet, upanyāsakrameṇoktatvādadoṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: If then the <s>vaikhānasa</s> should be stated [first instead], [the reply is:] there is no fault, because [the <s>bhikṣu</s>] has been mentioned in the order of presentation.
Therefore, the <s>bhikṣu</s> is stated first.

children.text: anicayaśabdenaupacayikadravyasya tyāga ucyate, na nityadravyasya śikhāyajñopavītādeḥ //
children.translated_text: By the word <s>anicaya</s> (without accumulation), the abandonment of accumulable possessions is meant, not of permanent articles such as the topknot and sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>).

children.text: nanu ca nityasyaiva tyāgo yuktaḥ upavītaśabdena nyāsaviśeṣo 'bhidhīyate-
children.translated_text: But surely it is the abandonment of permanent things that is appropriate! [Objection:] By the word <s>upavīta</s>, a particular mode of wearing is referred to —
When the right hand is raised, the wise call it <s>upavītī</s> (wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder).
Thus.
The <s>upavīta</s> literally means the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>). [He has no right to it] because he has no qualification for sacrifice.

children.text: na kuṇḍyāṃ nodake saṅge na cele na tripuṣkare //
children.translated_text: Not in the water-pot, not in water, not in attachment, not in cloth, not in the triple staff,

children.text: nāgāre nāsane nānne yasya syānmokṣavittu saḥ //
children.translated_text: not in a shelter, not in a seat, not in food — one who [has no attachment to these] is indeed a knower of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text:
iti kuṇḍyādīnāṃ tyāgopadeśāt /
jābālaśrutāvapi-'nakhāni nikṛtya yajñopavītaṃ visṛjya'; iti yajñopavītasya
children.translated_text: Because there is an instruction to abandon the water-pot and the like. In the <s>Jābāla</s> <s>śruti</s> also: 'Having trimmed the nails and cast off the sacred thread' — thus of the sacred thread
there is an instruction for abandonment — thus [the objector concludes].

children.text: ucyate-prathamaṃ tāvadyaduktaṃ yajñādhikārābhāvāt iti tatra yāgaśabdo devapūjanādāvapi vartate devapūjanaṃ tvasya dhyānena paramātmapūjanāmastyeva kutaḥ ?
children.translated_text: It is replied: First, regarding what was said — 'because he has no qualification for sacrifice' — there the word 'sacrifice' (<s>yāga</s>) also applies to the worship of gods and the like. And he does have worship of the Supreme Self through meditation. Why?
For one who dwells always in the forest, who has conquered the senses, who has turned away from all self-centered pleasures,
whose mind has turned to contemplation of the Self — for such a dispassionate one, non-return [to <s>saṃsāra</s>] is certain.

children.text:
iti smṛtyantaradarśanāt autmayāga evādhikārāt /
tathāca śrūyate śrutau-'dharmādharmau havirmanaḥsruvaḥ prāṇo 'dhvaryurindriyāṇyudgātāraḥ śabdādayo hotā etai ṛtvigbhistena sruveṇa taddhaviraharaharyatinā paramātmanyagnau hotavyam'; iti /
ato yogādhikārasadbhāvādadoṣaḥ /
yaccoktam- 'na kuṇḍyāṃ nodake saṅgaḥ'; iti tatrāpi kuṇḍikādīnāṃ vaicitryavarjanārthaḥ saṅgasyaiva parityāgaḥ, na kuṇḍikādeḥ /
kutaḥ ? tatraiva
children.translated_text: Because this is seen in another <s>smṛti</s>; because his qualification is for the sacrifice of the Self alone. And thus it is heard in the <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are the oblation, the mind is the ladle, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) is the <s>adhvaryu</s> (officiating priest), the senses are the <s>udgātṛs</s> (chanters), the sense-objects are the <s>hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) — with these priests, with that ladle, that oblation, day after day, one should offer into the fire of the Supreme Self through <s>yoga</s>' — thus. Therefore, because the qualification for <s>yoga</s> exists, there is no fault. And regarding what was said — 'not in the water-pot, not in water, not attachment' — there too, the abandonment is of attachment to variety in water-pots and the like, not of the water-pot itself. Why? Because in that very [text]

children.text:
'yajñopavītyudakakamaṇḍaluhastaḥ'; iti vakṣyamāṇatvāt /
tatra 'sarvāśrayāṇāṃ dharmiṣṭhaṃ'; iti sarvāśramādhikārāt sāmānyatvena vartamāno 'pi viśeṣadharmeṇa bādhyata iti cet, na, yadi sarvāśramādhikārastatreṣyate tatra prakaraṇe vākyārthaghaṭanārthaṃ 'yajñopavītyudakakamaṇḍaluhastatvam'; iti bhāvapratyayenaivāvakṣyat 'paiśunamatsarābhimānāhaṃkārānārjavātmastavaparagarhadambhalobhakrodhamohavivarjanaṃ sarvāśramāṇāṃ dharmiṣṭham'; iti pūrvamuktvā tataścābhāvapratyayena viśeṣoddeśena 'yajñopavītyudakakamaṇḍaluhastaḥ'; iti nirdeśaḥ sarvāśramādhikāranivṛttyartha iti jñātuṃ śakyate /
tatastatra sarvāśramādhikārābhāvāt pūrvāparavirodhaprasaṅgo mā bhūditi 'na kuṇḍyāṃ nodake saṅgaḥ'; iti saṅgamātrasyaiva tyāgaḥ kriyata iti grahītuṃ śakyata eveti /

children.translated_text: The use of the word 'attachment' (<s>saṅga</s>) is for that very purpose.

children.text: tasmāttenāpi na kuṇḍyādīnāṃ tyāgaḥ yaccoktam-'nakhāni nikṛtya yajñopavītaṃ visṛjya'; iti tatrāpi prathamaṃ saṃnyāsāśramapraveśakāle purāṇasya yajñopavītasya tyāgamātraṃ kriyate, na tadānīṃ gṛhyamāṇasya pratiṣedhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even by that, there is no abandonment of the water vessel (<s>kuṇḍī</s>) and the like. And as for what was stated — 'having cut the nails and discarded the sacred thread' — there too, at the time of first entering the <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) stage of life, only the abandonment of the old sacred thread is performed; it is not a prohibition of accepting a new one.

children.text: kutaḥ ? 'nakhāni nikṛtya purāṇaṃ vastraṃ yajñopavītaṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ tyaktvā navāni gṛhītvā'śramaṃ praviśet'; iti smṛtyantaraśravaṇāt /
children.translated_text: Why? Because another <s>smṛti</s> (authoritative tradition) states: 'Having cut the nails, having discarded the old garment, sacred thread, and water vessel, and having taken new ones, one should enter the <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life).'
Therefore, the abandonment is of accumulated possessions of that kind.

Because it will be stated: 'wearing the sacred thread, holding a water vessel (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>) in hand.' Therein, although the statement 'the most righteous of all <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life)' applies to all <s>āśramas</s> in general, if one argues that the general rule is overridden by a specific rule — no, if the applicability to all <s>āśramas</s> is intended there, then in that context, for the purpose of construing the sentence meaning, 'wearing the sacred thread and holding a water vessel' would have been stated with an abstract suffix (-tva) indicating a state of being. Having first stated 'freedom from slander, envy, pride, egoism, crookedness, self-praise, blame of others, ostentation, greed, anger, and delusion is the most righteous for all <s>āśramas</s>,' and then afterward, with a specific designation using a non-abstract suffix, the prescription 'wearing the sacred thread, holding a water vessel in hand' — it can be understood that this is for the purpose of excluding the applicability to all <s>āśramas</s>. Therefore, since there is no applicability to all <s>āśramas</s> in that passage, in order to avoid the contingency of contradiction between the earlier and later statements, it can indeed be understood that through the statement 'there should be no attachment to the water vessel or to water,' only the renunciation of mere attachment is enjoined.

children.text: kiñca-nityadravyatyāge bhikṣorācamanābhāvaśca prāpnoti, 'ācamane yajñopavīti'; ityārambhāt tadabhāve ācamanasyāpyabhāvaḥ prāpnotīti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, if there were abandonment of essential articles, then the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) would lack the ability to perform <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping of water), because of the stipulation 'one should wear the sacred thread during <s>ācamana</s>'; in its absence, the impossibility of <s>ācamana</s> itself would follow.

children.text: 'muṇḍaśikhī vā'; iti muṇḍapakṣe ācamanāṅgaśikhāvarjitasyāpi ācamanaṃ yuṣmābhirabhyupagamyate, tadvadasmābhirapīti cet, na, tatra vacanādadoṣaḥ 'muṇḍaḥśikhī vā'; iti /
children.translated_text: If one argues that in the case of the option 'shaven-headed or with a topknot (<s>śikhā</s>),' you yourselves accept that <s>ācamana</s> is performed even by one who lacks the topknot, which is an auxiliary of <s>ācamana</s>, and likewise we too accept this — no, in that case there is no fault because of the explicit statement 'shaven-headed or with a topknot.'

children.text: yuṣmākaṃ tu yajñopavītaṃ tyaktavyamiti vacanābhāvāddoṣa eveti //
children.translated_text: But for you, there is indeed a fault because there is no statement that the sacred thread should be abandoned.

children.text:
bhikṣuranicaya iti vaktavye dharmāsyādāvabhidhānaṃ nityasyāgnihotradārāderapi tyāgārtham /
evaṃ ca gārhasthyādeva yaḥ pravrajet tena śrautasya ca smārtasya cāgneḥ dāraputraprapañcayajñādisahitasya tyāgaḥ
children.translated_text: Where it should have been said 'the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) has no accumulation,' the mention of <s>dharma</s> (duty) at the beginning is for the purpose of abandoning even the permanent obligations such as the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire sacrifice) and wife. And thus, one who renounces directly from the householder stage must abandon the <s>śrauta</s> (Vedic) and <s>smārta</s> (traditional) fires together with wife, children, the five great sacrifices, and so forth.
This must be done.

children.text: vaisānasādeva yaḥ pravrajet tatrāpi sapatnīkapakṣe prāptasya dārasya śrāmaṇakāgnisahitasya pañcayajñāderapi tyāgaḥ kartavyaḥ //
children.translated_text: And for one who renounces from the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller) stage itself, in the case where he has a wife, the abandonment must be made of the wife, the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire, and even the five sacrifices (<s>pañcayajña</s>) and the like that have been obtained.
Some explain that the mention at the beginning is for the purpose of prescribing non-accumulation even for the lifelong celibate (<s>naiṣṭhika</s>).

children.text: tadayuktaṃ, 'guroḥ karmaśeṣeṇa japet'; iti japasyaiva pradhānatvenopadiṣṭatvāt tenaivāgniparigrahāderapyabhāvo jñātuṃ śakyata eveti //
children.translated_text: That is incorrect, because through the statement 'after completing service to the teacher, one should perform <s>japa</s> (recitation),' <s>japa</s> alone has been taught as primary; from that itself, the absence of maintaining fire and the like can be understood.
<s>Ūrdhvaretāḥ</s> (one whose seed flows upward, i.e., a celibate). // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.12 //

children.text:
'uttareṣāṃ caitadavirodhi'; ityanena brahmacāriṇaḥ uktena brahmacaryarakṣaṇenāsyāpi siddherūrdhvaretograhaṇaṃ yathā yathā retasaḥ kṣayo bhavati tathā tathopāyaḥ kartavya ityevamartham /
upāyaścālpānnābhyavahārādi /
yathā cāha bhagavānvāsudevaḥ-
children.translated_text: Since through the statement 'and for the later ones, whatever is not contradictory to this,' the preservation of <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) stated for the <s>brahmacārin</s> (student) is already established for this one too, the mention of <s>ūrdhvaretas</s> (upward seed) means that whatever methods prevent the loss of seed should be employed. The method includes eating little food and the like. As the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s> has said:
Sense objects turn away from one who abstains from food,
Except for the taste; but even the taste turns away upon seeing the Supreme.

children.text:
iti /
tathālpānnāmyavahārābhiprāyeṇa smṛtyantare 'pyuktam 'aṣṭau grāsā munerbhakṣaḥ'; ityādi /
evaṃca brahmacāriṇaḥ saṃpūrṇabhojane na doṣaḥ /
tathā ca smṛtyantaram-
children.translated_text: Thus. Similarly, with the intention of eating little food, another <s>smṛti</s> also states: 'Eight morsels are the food of a sage,' and so on. And thus, for the <s>brahmacārin</s> (student), there is no fault in eating a full meal. And so another <s>smṛti</s> states:
A draft ox, a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), and one who has established the sacred fires — these three,
They succeed while eating; their success does not come from not eating.
Thus.
<s>Dhruvaśīlaḥ</s> (of steady conduct) during the rains. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.13 //

children.text:
varṣāsviti bahuvacanāt grāmādgrāmāntaraṃ caturṣu māseṣu na gacchedityarthaḥ /
ekatrāpi vasanna caṅkramaṇaprayāsaḥ syāditi śīlagrahaṇam /

children.translated_text: By this very rule, his state of being without a fixed abode (<s>aniketatva</s>) is established.

children.text: tathāca smṛtyantaram- 'grāmānte devagṛhe śūnyāgāre vṛkṣamūle vā'; iti /
children.translated_text: And so another <s>smṛti</s> states: 'At the outskirts of a village, in a temple, in an empty house, or at the foot of a tree.'

children.text: śīlagrahaṇaṃ ca kurvannetat jñāpayati, nāvaśyamevaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: And by using the word 'conduct' (<s>śīla</s>), this indicates that it need not necessarily be so.
And therefore, in cases of famine, banishment from the country, and the like, one may go even then.

The plural 'during the rains' means that one should not go from one village to another during the four months. The word 'conduct' (<s>śīla</s>) indicates that even while dwelling in one place, one should not exert oneself in walking about.
Seeking alms, one should go to the village. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.14 //

children.text: bhikṣā bhikṣyamāṇatvādannaṃ vāsaḥ kamaṇḍalvādiḥ, tadarthaṃ grāmaṃ gacchet arthāccheṣaṃ kālamaraṇye devāyatanādau tiṣṭhediti siddham //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhikṣā</s> (alms), because it is what is begged for, means food, clothing, a water vessel (<s>kamaṇḍalu</s>), and the like. For that purpose one should go to the village; by implication, the rest of the time one should stay in the forest, at a temple, and so on — this is established.
Now, when the time for begging alms arrives for the <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student), he states:
One should beg at the end of mealtime, without returning. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.15 //
'At the end' (<s>jaghanya</s>) means after the activity of eating, i.e., afterward. And so <s>Manu</s> states:
When the smoke has ceased, when the pestle is laid down, when the embers have died, when people have finished eating,
When the serving of food from plates is over, the renunciant (<s>yati</s>) should always go begging for alms.
Thus.

children.text: anivṛttaṃ yasmin gṛhe pratyākhyātaṃ tasmindine tadgrahaṃ punarna praviśedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Without returning' (<s>anivṛtta</s>) means: at a house where one has been refused, one should not enter again on that day — this is the meaning.
The word 'should beg' (<s>caret</s>) is for the purpose of including the rules from other <s>smṛtis</s> (authoritative traditions).

children.text: yathā'ha vasiṣṭhaḥ-'vidhūme sannamusale ekaśāṭhīparihito 'jinena vā'; iti //
children.translated_text: As <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> says: 'When the smoke has ceased and the pestle is laid down, wearing a single garment or a deerskin.'
One from whom blessings have ceased. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.16 //
The meaning is: one should not utter blessings (<s>āśis</s>) on occasions such as the giving of alms and being saluted.

If one argues that this is already obtained through the statement 'one who does not initiate either harm or favor' — no, because favor (<s>anugraha</s>) is of the nature of action, while blessings (<s>āśis</s>) are of the nature of speech.
Restrained in speech, sight, and action. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.17 //

children.text:
brahmacāriprakaraṇe 'vāgbāhūdarasaṃyataḥ'; ityanenaiva siddhe atiśayārthaṃ punarvacanam /
ato vāksaṃyamo maunam, anyatra svādhyāyajapapathipraśnadharmayogapraśnebhyaḥ-
children.translated_text: Since this is already established by the statement 'restrained in speech, arms, and stomach' in the section on the <s>brahmacārin</s> (student), this repetition is for the purpose of indicating a higher degree of restraint. Therefore, restraint of speech means silence (<s>mauna</s>), except for Vedic recitation (<s>svādhyāya</s>), <s>japa</s> (repetitive chanting), asking directions, and questions about <s>dharma</s> and <s>yoga</s>:

children.text: dharmayogaṃ pathipraśnaṃ svādhyāyaṃ ca tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Discussion of <s>dharma</s> and <s>yoga</s>, asking directions, Vedic recitation (<s>svādhyāya</s>) as well,
And the words 'please give' for the purpose of alms — these are not censured even for a renunciant (<s>yati</s>).
This is according to the statement of another <s>smṛti</s> (authoritative tradition).
Restraint of sight means: one should not look even at one's own body in illness.
And so <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> states: 'Indifferent toward all beings.'
Restraint of action means: only the performance of what is prescribed, so that engagement in desire-prompted actions may not occur.

children.text: idānīṃ 'anicayo bhikṣuḥ'; ityanena sarvasyaipacayikadravyasya parityāge sati pratiprasavaḥ kriyate-
children.translated_text: Now, since through the statement 'the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant) has no accumulation,' all accumulated possessions have been renounced, an exception is made:
One should keep a garment for covering one's private parts (<s>kaupīna</s>). // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.18 //

children.text:
kaupīnāmiti nagnatocyate /
tadāvaraṇamātraṃ vāsaḥ paridadhyāt /
evaṃ ca praśastadvijātibhyastāvanmātrapratigrahe na doṣa /
tataśca-
children.translated_text: The word <s>kaupīna</s> refers to nakedness. One should wear a garment sufficient only to cover that. And thus, in accepting only that much from worthy twice-born persons (<s>dvijāti</s>), there is no fault. And therefore:
He who, having granted safety to all beings, then turns back,
He who always kills both the born and the unborn and accepts gifts —
The enumeration of faults in another <s>smṛti</s> should be understood as referring to cases other than this.
Some say, having washed what has been discarded. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.19 //

children.text: eke manyante pratigrahadoṣaparihārārthaṃ prahīṇaṃ yadrathyādau tyaktaṃ tatprakṣālya paridadhyāt nirṇijyeti pratyātmikaśaucaprāpaṇārtham //
children.translated_text: Some hold that, for the purpose of avoiding the fault of accepting gifts, one should wash what has been discarded — that which has been thrown away on roads and such places — and wear it. The word 'having washed' (<s>nirṇijya</s>) is for the purpose of attaining personal purity.
One should not take a part that is not separated from herbs and trees. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.20 //

children.text:
oṣadhayaḥ phalapākāntāḥ /
apuṣpeṇa ye phalavantaste vanaspatayaḥ /
ubhayagrahaṇena sarve sthāvarā api gṛhyante /
teṣāmaviprayuktaṃ tato 'napagataṃ śākhāpatrādi na gṛhṇīyāt 'hiṃsānugrahayoranārambhī'; ityanena siddhamiti
children.translated_text: <s>Oṣadhis</s> (herbs) are those that perish after bearing fruit. <s>Vanaspatis</s> (trees) are those that bear fruit without flowering. By mentioning both, all stationary beings (<s>sthāvara</s>) are included. One should not take from them what is not separated, that is, branches, leaves, and such that have not fallen off. If one argues that this is already established by the statement 'one who does not initiate either harm or favor' —

children.text: cet, tatra jaṅgamavadha eva hiṃseti kecidvadanti /
children.translated_text: Some say that in that context, <s>hiṃsā</s> (harm) refers only to the killing of moving creatures.
Since it is stated with that intention, there is no fault.
By the prefix 'upa-' (in <s>upādadīta</s>), one should not even cause another to take it.
Since steadiness of conduct has been prescribed during the rains, and free movement at other times is implied, he states:
One should not stay in a village for a second night outside the rainy season. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.21 //

children.text:
ṛtuśabdena varṣā evocyante /
apagate ṛtau dvitīyāṃ rātriṃ grāme na vaset /
ekasmingrāme dinadvayaṃ na vasedityarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: By the mention of 'village,' there is no fault in staying in the forest.

children.text: apartugrahaṇādvarṣāsu kadācit dvitīyāmapi vasato na doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: By the qualification 'outside the rainy season' (<s>apartu</s>), there is no fault if one occasionally stays even a second night during the rains.
By the word 'rains' (<s>varṣā</s>), winter (<s>hemanta</s>) and summer (<s>grīṣma</s>) are meant.

children.text: tataśca tasminvarṣākāle ekatraiva vasedanyatra na vasedityarthasiddham //
children.translated_text: And thus, during that rainy period, one should dwell in one place only and not elsewhere — this meaning is established.

By the word <s>ṛtu</s> (season), the rains alone are meant. When the season has passed, one should not stay a second night in a village. The meaning is: one should not stay two days in a single village.
Shaven-headed or with a topknot (<s>śikhī</s>). // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.22 //
The prescription begins for the purpose of prohibiting matted hair (<s>jaṭā</s>). The option is according to one's wish.
One should avoid the destruction of seeds. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.23 //

children.text: bījānāṃ vrīhyādīnāṃ vadhaṃ avahananādi na kuryāt //
children.translated_text: One should not perform the husking and such destruction of seeds like rice (<s>vrīhi</s>) and others.
Equal toward all beings. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.24 //
One should be impartial toward all living beings, meaning: free from the distinction of one's own side and another's side.
One who does not initiate either harm or favor. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.25 //
Therefore, even for unknowing killing of living creatures, an expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) must be performed day after day for its avoidance.
And so <s>Uśanas</s> says: 'For the purification of unknowing killing, one should perform three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath control exercises) at night.'
By the word 'favor' (<s>anugraha</s>), affection (<s>sneha</s>) is meant.
The meaning is: one should not engage in that either.
Since harm (<s>hiṃsā</s>) is already established by that very term in the section on the <s>brahmacārin</s> (student), this repetition is for the purpose of indicating a higher degree.
Having stated the rules for the <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant), he now sets forth the duties of the <s>vaikhānasa</s> (forest-dweller):
The <s>vaikhānasa</s> (forest-dweller) lives in the forest, eats roots and fruits, and is devoted to austerity (<s>tapas</s>). // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.26 //
The word <s>vaikhānasa</s> is derived through established etymology.
He, dwelling in the forest, should have the habit of eating roots and the like; the meaning is: he should not eat prepared food.
'Devoted to austerity' (<s>tapaḥśīla</s>) means one whose habit is the mortification of the body.

children.text: evaṃca mūlaphalādyapi svalpamevāśnīyāt, smṛtyantaradarśanāt ṣoḍaśakṛtva eva 'vānaprasthasya ṣoḍaśa'; iti //
children.translated_text: And thus, even roots, fruits, and the like should be eaten only in small quantities, as indicated by another <s>smṛti</s>: 'sixteen morsels for the <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller).'
Having established the fire according to the <s>Śrāmaṇaka</s> rite. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.27 //
The <s>Śrāmaṇaka</s> is the name of the scripture of the <s>vaikhānasas</s> (forest-dwellers).
Having established the fire according to that, one should perform the evening and morning fire ritual — this is the remainder of the rule.
One who does not eat village food. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.28 //
One should not eat even roots and fruits that are from the village (cultivated).
One who worships the gods, ancestors, humans, beings, and sages. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.29 //

children.text:
grāmyānnasādhanāḥ gṛhasthasya pañca mahāyajñāḥ /
asya cāgrāmyāhārapratiṣedhāttannivṛttirmā bhūdityārambhaḥ /
children.translated_text: The five great sacrifices (<s>pañca mahāyajña</s>) of the householder require village food as their means. Since eating village food is prohibited for this one, the prescription begins lest those sacrifices be abandoned.
And so <s>Manu</s> states:
With various pure forest products, or with vegetables, roots, and fruits,
One should perform these very great sacrifices in the prescribed manner.
Every visitor is a guest, except those who are prohibited. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.30 //
Whoever comes to his hermitage (<s>āśrama</s>), all of them are his guests.
The meaning is: there is no restriction by <s>varṇa</s> (social class) such as 'a non-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is not a guest of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,' nor is there a restriction by number.
The prohibited ones are thieves and the like, as well as those born of <s>pratiloma</s> (reverse-order mixed) marriages; they are to be excluded.
One may even eat meat killed by predators. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.31 //
<s>Vaiṣka</s> refers to the flesh of an animal killed by predators such as tigers and the like.
One may eat that.
The particle 'api' (even) expresses reluctance or censure.
Therefore, one should eat it only in times of distress.
One should not stand on ploughed ground. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.32 //

children.text: araṇye 'pi phālakṛṣṭapradeśaṃ nākrāmeta, āvāsaṃ tatra na kuryādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in the forest, one should not step on ground that has been ploughed; the meaning is: one should not make one's dwelling there.

children.text: ākrāmediti siddhe adhitiṣṭhediti vacanaṃ pramādādākramato doṣābhāvajñāpanārtham /
children.translated_text: Although 'one should not step on' would have sufficed, the use of 'should not stand on' (<s>adhitiṣṭhet</s>) indicates that there is no fault if one accidentally steps on it.
Although 'cultivated' would have sufficed, the mention of 'plough' (<s>phāla</s>) is for the purpose of prohibiting dwelling even near a field.
And one should not enter a village. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.33 //
Even by a path that is not ploughed, one should not enter an inhabited settlement.
By the particle 'ca' (and), even another village is included.
Having matted hair, wearing bark and deerskin garments. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.34 //

children.text:
jaṭilaḥ keśī /
jaṭila eva syāditi niyamārtha ārambhaḥ /
cīraṃ darbhādiniṣpannam /

children.translated_text: This should be understood as the lower garment.
<s>Ajina</s> means a skin (hide).
This is the upper garment.
And so another <s>smṛti</s> states: 'Wearing bark garments, with a deerskin as the upper garment.'

<s>Jaṭila</s> means having long hair in matted locks. The prescription 'one should indeed have matted hair' begins for the purpose of establishing it as a fixed rule. <s>Cīra</s> (bark garment) is made from <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) and the like.
One should not eat food stored for more than a year. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.35 //

children.text:
mūlaphalamapi gatasaṃvatsaraṃ na bhuñjīta /
tathāca manuḥ-'tyajedāśvayuje māsi'; ityādi /
evaṃca
children.translated_text: Even roots and fruits that are more than a year old should not be eaten. And so <s>Manu</s> states: 'One should discard in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>' and so on. And thus,
Accumulation for only a year's duration is established.
Having stated the rules for the <s>vaikhānasa</s> (forest-dweller), now, wishing to present the view of some that there is supersession of the <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life), he states:

children.text: aikāśramyaṃ tvācāryaḥ pratyakṣavidhānāt gārhasthasya gārhasthasya // Gaut_3.36 //
children.translated_text: The teacher holds that there is only one <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), that of the householder, because it is directly prescribed. // <s>Gaut</s>. 3.36 //

children.text:
ekāśrame bhavamaikāśramyam /
tuśabdo 'vadhāraṇe /
gārhasthasyeti karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhī /
gārhasthyamevācāryā icchanti /
children.translated_text: 'That which exists in one <s>āśrama</s>' is <s>aikāśramya</s> (the doctrine of a single stage of life). The particle 'tu' is for emphasis. 'Of the householder' is a genitive in the sense of the object. The teachers hold that the householder stage alone is valid.
Why? Because of direct prescription — meaning, because of a prescription found in the revealed scripture (<s>śruti</s>).

children.text: yadyapi gṛhasthobhavedityevaṃ na vihitam, tathāpyagnihotrādigṛhasthasādhyakriyāvidhānāttasyaiva vidhānaṃ draṣṭavyam //
children.translated_text: Although it is not directly prescribed as 'one should become a householder,' nevertheless, since rituals such as the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire sacrifice) and others that can only be performed by a householder are prescribed, the prescription of the householder stage itself should be understood from that.
Thus ends the third chapter of <s>Maskarī's</s> commentary on the <s>Gautama Dharmasūtra</s>.
